a_rows_sample.anchor: 107.18 — Security drift ... Expected Agent↛ProductionDB. Observed Agent→ProductionDB. Expected: SecurityDrift. This may be higher severity than ordinary architecture drift.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines SecurityDrift (an observed forbidden Agent→ProductionDB connection), noted as potentially higher severity than ordinary drift.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 107.19 — Configuration drift ... Expected PolicyMode=Enforced. Observed PolicyMode=Permissive. Expected: ConfigurationDrift.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines ConfigurationDrift, e.g. PolicyMode observed as Permissive against an expected Enforced.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Eight-type drift taxonomy: distribution, conditional, label, structural, parameter, semantic, governance, architectural
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines eight drift types: concept/conditional drift P_t(Y|X)!=P_{t+1}(Y|X) (the X-Y relationship changed, potentially more consequential than input drift); distribution drift P_t(X)!=P_{t+1}(X) (input population changed); label drift P_t(Y)!=P_{t+1}(Y) (outcome prevalence changed); structural drift (a causal edge A->B present before a redesign no longer holds, A-not->B); parameter drift (A->B structure persists but strength beta_t != beta_{t+1}); semantic drift (Meaning(Approved,t1) != Meaning(Approved,t2)); governance drift (Policy_t1 != Policy_t2, historical decisions remain historical); architectural drift (Architecture_2025 != Architecture_2026, claims about one should not automatically apply to the other). Consolidates: Drift in {Distribution, Conditional, Label, Parameter, Structural, Semantic, Governance, Architectural} -- useful because different drift types require different responses.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Drift detection threshold; statistical drift versus operationally material drift; materiality-gated local adaptation
b_rows_sample.statement: A generic drift detector evaluates divergence D(P_t,P_{t+1}) > delta for a chosen threshold delta, but a huge dataset can make tiny changes statistically significant (p<0.001) without operational relevance, so drift detection must distinguish StatisticalDrift from OperationallyMaterialDrift; defines Material(D,d) (drift D materially affects decision d) so a detected drift need not trigger global recomputation. If drift affects only BC_A, only K_A should be updated without unnecessarily invalidating K_B, K_C -- 'this follows directly from bounded-context isolation'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Drift-triggered investigation; DriftDetected does not imply ModelInvalid
b_rows_sample.statement: If DriftScore > delta, KnowledgeOS can generate an InvestigationRequest, but DriftDetected does not automatically imply ModelInvalid -- it triggers investigation, not automatic invalidation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Twelve falsification experiments for Step 45 adaptive-learning model (all PASS)
b_rows_sample.statement: Runs twelve falsification tests, all PASS: (1) new evidence contradicts an old interpretation => interpretation revised, original evidence unchanged; (2) a model becomes obsolete => historical decisions retain the old model version; (3) a new model performs better => does not automatically replace the active model unless promotion policy allows it; (4) input distribution changes but decision-relevant behavior does not => distribution drift recorded without declaring causal/model failure; (5) statistically significant drift has negligible operational impact => no automatic critical escalation from statistical significance alone; (6) a model predicts poorly despite good historical calibration => performance reevaluated, calibration alone does not protect the model; (7) a successful outcome follows a poor decision => outcome success does not automatically validate decision quality; (8) a justified decision produces an adverse low-probability outcome => not automatically classified as irrational; (9) a governance policy changes => future decisions use the new policy, historical decisions retain the old policy version; (10) a new interpretation of old evidence is created => both historical and current interpretations remain traceable; (11) a model trained on one bounded context detects drift => impact stays scoped to relevant contexts unless evidence supports broader generalization; (12) a candidate model performs well in shadow mode but violates a safety constraint => cannot be promoted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Parameter drift, distribution/covariate shift (DistributionShift⇏ModelFailure), concept drift, calibration decay with a model-status lifecycle (experiments 1-4)
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 1: P_t0(Y|X) != P_t1(Y|X) detected as parameter drift needing possible recalibration, given tracked temporal model performance -- PASS. Experiment 2: P_train(X) != P_prod(X) detected as DistributionShiftDetected -- PASS; but explicitly DistributionShift ⇏ ModelFailure since P(Y|X) may remain unchanged -- 'a warning condition', not automatic failure. Experiment 3: P_t(Y=1|X=1) changing from 0.8 to 0.4 while the model keeps using the old relationship is detected as ConceptDrift -- PASS. Experiment 4: calibration monitored by temporal window; predictions remaining P=0.8 while realized success drops from ~80% to 55% is CalibrationDecay, and performance deteriorating beyond tolerance sets ModelStatus=Degraded -- PASS. Suggests a model lifecycle Experimental -> Validated -> Production -> Degraded -> Suspended -> Retired as domain/governance states, not mathematical truths.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.13 — Concept drift ... D_t distribution of reality. D_{t1}≠D_{t2}. A model that was accurate under D_{t1} may become inaccurate under D_{t2}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates concept drift: reality's distribution D_t can change (D_{t1}≠D_{t2}), degrading a previously accurate model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.14 — Experiment 7 ... Model accuracy 95% during t1. After organizational change: 70%. Expected: KnowledgeOS detects possible model degradation rather than assuming historical performance continues. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 7: a model's accuracy dropping from 95% to 70% after organizational change must be detected as possible degradation, not assumed continued; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.15 — Model validity is temporal ... Valid(M,t,C) rather than simply Valid(M). A model may be valid only within a declared context.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines model validity as Valid(M,t,C) — temporal and context-scoped, not a context-free Valid(M).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.16 — Experiment 8 ... Model was validated for Domain=A. It is applied to Domain=B. Expected: applicability is not automatically established. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 8: applying a Domain-A-validated model to Domain B does not automatically establish applicability; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.19 — Data quality changes model assurance ... if Quality(D)↓ then potentially Confidence(M)↓. Not necessarily linear, but must be represented where relevant.
b_rows_sample.statement: States Quality(D)↓ potentially implies Confidence(M)↓ (not necessarily linearly), requiring explicit representation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.20 — Experiment 10 ... Training dataset contains systematic bias. Model achieves excellent benchmark accuracy. Expected: benchmark accuracy does not prove real-world validity. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 10: high benchmark accuracy on a systematically biased dataset does not prove real-world validity; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.52 — Knowledge regression ... A new model may reduce knowledge quality. Precision(M_1)>Precision(M_2). But aggregate performance may hide failures in a critical domain.
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns aggregate model performance can hide domain-specific regression, even when Precision(M_1)>Precision(M_2) is not the case overall.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.53 — Experiment 26 ... Overall accuracy 96%. Critical architecture classification accuracy 72%. Expected: overall metric alone is insufficient. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 26: 96% overall accuracy masking 72% critical-domain accuracy shows the overall metric alone is insufficient; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.54 — Domain-specific assurance ... Assurance(M,D,C) rather than merely Assurance(M).
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines domain-specific assurance Assurance(M,D,C), not merely Assurance(M).

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'architecture-drift-classification-model' POSSIBLY relates to 'concept-drift-taxonomy' (batch B0024). Note: Step 107: six mutually exclusive discrepancy categories D1 (architecture defect) / D2 (implementation defect) / D3 (deployment defect) / D4 (runtime defect) / D5 (authorized deviation) / D6 (unknown/insufficient evidence) explaining WHY A_I/A_C/A_D/A_R differ, rejecting automatic A_I!=A_R => ArchitectureWrong inference in favor of Difference->Classification->Decision. Extends the drift lifecycle (Detected->Triaged->Classified->Assigned->Remediated->Verified->Closed), Remediation!=Verification, the resolution taxonomy {Remediate,AuthorizeDeviation,ChangeArchitecture}, risk-routed assurance automation for AI-agent change velocity, and the named non-autonomous Architecture Conformance Engine capability. Distinct from concept-drift-taxonomy (B0023, statistical/type-of-drift taxonomy) and drift-detection-capability (B0012, knowledge-item validity monitoring) in that it classifies causal explanation and resolution of a detected discrepancy across the four-representation chain, not drift types or knowledge staleness.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Language test · Ownership test · Change-reason test ... A context can pass all three with no code (rules-only contexts are real)
a_rows_sample.statement: A three-part strategic-DDD test (language, ownership, change-reason) is applied to every declared bounded context, explicitly allowing a context with zero executable realization to still pass (rules-only contexts are real), while a context failing the language test cannot be rescued by code.

a_rows_sample.anchor: BC-1..BC-6 verdict table: CONFIRM boundary UNRESOLVED (BC-1) · CONFIRM but overloaded (BC-2) · CONFIRM (BC-3) · CONFIRM capability/CHALLENGE context (BC-4) · CHALLENGE as declared Core (BC-5) · CONFIRM cleanest boundary (BC-6)
a_rows_sample.statement: Each of the six declared bounded contexts receives a distinct strategic verdict from the three-part test: BC-1 confirmed but with a possibly-two-systems internal boundary unresolved; BC-2 confirmed but overloaded (hosts a second, foreign orchestration language); BC-3 confirmed cleanly; BC-4's capability is real but its context status is challenged (no state, no component, realized only by role model and human acts); BC-5's declared-Core status is challenged as not matching the measured center of gravity; BC-6 is the cleanest confirmed boundary in the system.

a_rows_sample.anchor: PROMOTE TO CANDIDATE BC-7 ... the strongest candidate on the record
a_rows_sample.statement: An undeclared area realized entirely by workflow-record mechanisms (work item, session, role, transition, grant, handoff, human act) is promoted from the baseline's low-confidence Inferred status to the strongest candidate bounded context, named 'Governed Session Orchestration' (candidate BC-7), pending an ADR since it would reverse a recorded Increment-1 parsimony decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: M-1..M-5 Misplaced responsibilities ... M-3 Composition root (CMP-001) | registry only — no declared context at all
a_rows_sample.statement: Five misplaced-responsibility findings are recorded, including the workflow-record mechanism sitting in the wrong declared context (M-1), the platform registry sitting under Design & Decision Support rather than its own governance context (M-2), and the composition root having no declared context home at all (M-3).

a_rows_sample.anchor: C-1..C-6 Coupling problems ... Authority state has no provenance — all workflow records gitignored, zero history
a_rows_sample.statement: Six coupling problems are recorded, most materially that the candidate orchestration context's own authority store has no provenance (gitignored, zero history, C-3) despite the context's purpose being auditable authority, and that the registry-first contract is declared binding but measured bypassable by three unregistered hooks (C-6).

a_rows_sample.anchor: PLATFORM → PRODUCT (PublicDigit / Election = declared CORE DOMAIN, AIP-14) ... platform reads/guards app/; product never invokes platform
a_rows_sample.statement: A current-state context map is produced showing the human PO/ARB as the authority origin flowing through a governance-registering role into the candidate orchestration context, out to the other declared contexts, and states the platform-to-product relationship as a one-way Supporting-to-Core guard seam that is never inverted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ADR-C1 Recognize or decline BC-7 Governed Session Orchestration ... highest — every other boundary question touches it
a_rows_sample.statement: Eight ADR candidates (ADR-C1..C7) are proposed as future governed decisions, with ADR-C1 (recognize/decline BC-7) marked highest priority since every other boundary question in the report depends on it; drafting and deciding them is explicitly left to future PO/ARB work.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Create Architecture Landscape v2: update the bounded-context map from 6 to 7 contexts · introduce BC-7 Governed Session Orchestration · update the capability map with CAP-14
a_rows_sample.statement: KOS-ARCH-BASELINE-002 is commissioned to formally grow the strategic model from 6 to 7 bounded contexts, recognizing BC-7 and assigning it CAP-14, following the ADR-AIP-03 decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The seven-context strategic model is the authoritative architecture model ... ADR-AIP-01's frozen six-context table is hereby amended
a_rows_sample.statement: The PO/ARB formally accepts the seven-context strategic model (Landscape v2, Context Map v2, Capability Map v2), which amends ADR-AIP-01's previously frozen six-context table, recognizing BC-7 as a Supporting Subdomain with CAP-14.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The platform's strategic model grows from six declared bounded contexts to seven: BC-7 Governed Session Orchestration — the context the platform was already organized around
a_rows_sample.statement: The Architecture Landscape v2's central statement: BC-7 is recognized as the context the platform was already organized around, receiving its declared boundary, capability (CAP-14), and relationships, while all physical component placement remains unchanged (a model-level change only).

a_rows_sample.anchor: DDD-as-analysis: bounded-context/aggregate identification is candidate-only, derived from language · ownership · invariants · lifecycle · authority · consistency · dependency direction — never from folders/containers/repos/deployment units. No formal DDD validation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Bounded-context and aggregate identification in this archaeology is candidate-only, derived from language, ownership, invariants, lifecycle, authority, consistency, and dependency direction -- never from folder/container/repository/deployment-unit structure -- and constitutes no formal DDD validation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ownership discipline (recorded): BC-1 owns knowledge governance but is not built
a_rows_sample.statement: BC-1..BC-7 to CAP-01..14 ownership table: BC-1 Knowledge Governance/CAP-03 (NOT BUILT, convention only); BC-2 Implementation Guidance/CAP-05-06 (A); BC-3 Verification & Evidence/CAP-07-09 (C, guard surface, gate execution planned); BC-4 Adversarial Review/CAP-11 (E, deferred); BC-5 Design & Decision Support/CAP-10,12,13 (A); BC-6 Session Continuity/CAP-01-02 (A); BC-7 Governed Session Orchestration/CAP-14 (A, workflow engine). The six-role model's Knowledge Engineer and Communication Engineer are adopted as operating-model roles, not proof that knowledge/communication contexts exist.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Where do different models, invariants, ownership and lifecycles actually emerge? ... this remains a DDD hypothesis, not an architectural fact. The current implementation would have to prove the boundaries.
a_rows_sample.statement: Candidate (explicitly unproven) bounded-context landscape: Evidence Context (observations, sources, measurements, provenance), Reasoning Context (causal inference, assumptions, uncertainty), Decision Context (actions, recommendations, policies, consequences) under KnowledgeOS, flagged as a DDD hypothesis the implementation must still prove.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We now move from system boundary to the inside of the system. Component=Responsibility+Data+Behavior+Interface+Dependency+Evidence. A component is therefore not defined merely by its directory or class name.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Component=Responsibility+Data+Behavior+Interface+Dependency+Evidence, stating a component is not defined merely by its directory or class name.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 111.1 — Component reconstruction principle ... C=(Identity,Purpose,Responsibilities,Data,Commands,Queries,Dependencies,Interfaces,Invariants,Tests,Runtime,Owner). Only after these are established can we decide whether two components are separate, overlapping, duplicates, parts of one bounded context
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the full component reconstruction tuple C=(Identity,Purpose,Responsibilities,Data,Commands,Queries,Dependencies,Interfaces,Invariants,Tests,Runtime,Owner), a precondition for classifying inter-component relationships.

type_signature.codomain: Identity x Purpose x Responsibilities x Data x Commands x Queries x Dependencies x Interfaces x Invariants x Tests x Runtime x Owner

b_rows_sample.anchor: 111.2 — First question: what is a component? ... Class, Module, Package, Service, Application, DeploymentUnit, BoundedContext. They are not equivalent.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes seven frequently-confused units of analysis: Class, Module, Package, Service, Application, DeploymentUnit, BoundedContext.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 111.3 — Experiment 1 ... Repository contains KnowledgeService.java. Can we conclude KnowledgeService=KnowledgeBoundedContext? No. It may simply be an application service. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 1: a KnowledgeService.java class does not by itself establish a KnowledgeBoundedContext; it may be merely an application service; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 111.4 — Component levels ... System→BoundedContext→{Application,Domain,Infrastructure}, plus Supporting Systems. This prevents accidental conflation of implementation structure and domain structure.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a multi-level reconstruction tree (System->BoundedContext->{Application,Domain,Infrastructure}, Supporting Systems) preventing conflation of implementation and domain structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 111.5 — Component identity ... ComponentID should not depend solely on ClassName. Because names change.
b_rows_sample.statement: States component identity must be stable and independent of class naming, since names change.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 111.6 — Experiment 2 ... Class KnowledgeService becomes EngineeringKnowledgeService. Expected: potentially the same logical component. Result: PASS. This is why logical identity and implementation naming must be separated.
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 2: a renamed class (KnowledgeService to EngineeringKnowledgeService) may remain the same logical component; result PASS, motivating separation of logical identity from naming.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 111.7 — Responsibility reconstruction ... What responsibility does this component actually own? Not what does its README claim? We inspect Commands+Queries+DataMutations+Dependencies.
b_rows_sample.statement: States responsibility must be reconstructed from actual Commands+Queries+DataMutations+Dependencies, not from README claims.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 111.8 — Experiment 3 ... Component named KnowledgeManager actually reads Git, parses Markdown, creates embeddings, writes vector data. Expected: observed responsibility closer to KnowledgeIngestion/Indexing than KnowledgeAuthority. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 3: a KnowledgeManager's actual behavior (reads Git, parses Markdown, creates embeddings, writes vector data) reveals its real responsibility as KnowledgeIngestion/Indexing rather than KnowledgeAuthority; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 111.9 — Responsibility is more important than naming ... ObservedBehavior > ComponentName for determining actual responsibility.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the central rule ObservedBehavior>ComponentName for determining actual component responsibility.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 111.10 — Data ownership ... Which data does the component own? We distinguish Reads(Data) from Owns(Data). A service can read data without owning it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Reads(Data) from Owns(Data): a service reading data does not thereby own it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 111.11 — Experiment 4 ... Component A reads Decision. Component B creates and changes Decision. Expected: B is the stronger candidate for ownership. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 4: the component that creates and changes Decision (B) is the stronger ownership candidate over one that merely reads it (A); result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 111.12 — Data ownership graph ... Component-owns->Data and separately Component-reads->Data. This becomes crucial for determining bounded-context boundaries.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the data-ownership graph with separate owns and reads edge types, crucial for bounded-context boundary determination.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 111.13 — Experiment 5 ... Two services directly modify the same decision table. Expected: potential shared-data coupling. Result: OBS. This does not yet prove architectural failure, but it is an important finding.
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 5: two services directly mutating the same decision table is potential shared-data coupling, classified OBS (an important finding, not yet a proven failure).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 111.14 — Aggregate ownership ... Aggregate→Invariant→Owner. Decision may own invariants such as Approved⇒AuthorityPresent.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the aggregate-ownership model Aggregate→Invariant→Owner, illustrated by Decision owning Approved⇒AuthorityPresent.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 111.15 — Experiment 6 ... Two unrelated services can independently set decision.status=APPROVED without passing through a common invariant boundary. Expected: potential aggregate-boundary violation. Result: OBS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 6: two independent services both able to set decision.status=APPROVED without a shared invariant boundary is a potential aggregate-boundary violation, classified OBS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 111.16 — Command ownership ... Command→OwningComponent. CreateEvidence, ApproveDecision, RegisterAgent, RecordObservation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines command ownership Command→OwningComponent, with example commands CreateEvidence/ApproveDecision/RegisterAgent/RecordObservation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 111.17 — Experiment 7 ... Both Service A and Service B implement ApproveDecision. Expected: potential duplicate business responsibility. Result: OBS. This is exactly the kind of issue the actual inventory should expose.
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 7: two services both implementing ApproveDecision is potential duplicate business responsibility, classified OBS, exemplifying the inventory's diagnostic purpose.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 111.18 — Query ownership ... Query→OwningSource. But multiple read models may legitimately expose the same information. DuplicateReadModel≠DuplicateDomainOwnership.
b_rows_sample.statement: States DuplicateReadModel≠DuplicateDomainOwnership: multiple read models exposing the same information may be legitimate rather than duplicated ownership.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 111.19 — Experiment 8 ... Two APIs expose GET /decisions. One is a UI projection. The other is the authoritative domain API. Expected: not automatically a duplicate domain capability. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 8: a UI-projection GET /decisions endpoint alongside an authoritative domain API endpoint is not automatically duplicate domain capability; result PASS.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'knowledgeos-actual-component-inventory-methodology' POSSIBLY relates to 'bounded-context-map' (batch B0024). Note: Step 111: the methodology for reconstructing ACTUAL KnowledgeOS components (as opposed to bounded-context target proposals). Full component tuple C=(...); Class/Module/Package/Service/Application/DeploymentUnit/BoundedContext distinction; ObservedBehavior>ComponentName rule; Reads(Data)!=Owns(Data) and data-ownership graph; Aggregate->Invariant->Owner; command/query ownership with DuplicateReadModel!=DuplicateDomainOwnership; Inbound/Outbound interface taxonomy; sync/async classification; four-way dependency classification with semantically-interpreted DependencyDirection; DomainConcept vs TechnicalCapability; ubiquitous-language extraction with semantic collisions (SameTerm->DifferentMeaning) and semantic duplication (DifferentTerms->SameMeaning); Cohesion/Coupling metrics and HighCohesion+HighCoupling bounded-context-candidate heuristic; the crucial sequencing rule ComponentInventory!=BoundedContextMap (inventory precedes any bounded-context claim, and prior candidates like Evidence/Voting/Appointment-Mandate/Contestation/Adjudication must not be assumed to apply automatically); runtime identity, lifecycle status, ownership, criticality, test-coverage/AssuranceGap; the 16-field Component Evidence Card; the 8-relationship-type component graph G_C and five architecture-smell patterns (Hub/Circular/Shared-DB/Orphan/Duplicate) as signals not violations; agent-component relationship mapping (Claude/Codex) with concrete governance-bypass and assurance-fragmentation OBS/DRIFT findings; seven-value inventory status model (avoiding premature deletion); Confidence(C) formula; and the central CoherentBoundaries diagnostic yielding three outcomes (Coherent/Fragmented/Monolithic) plus a strict anti-premature-redesign discipline. Extends evidence-based-architecture-reconstruction-methodology (S1008) and knowledgeos-actual-system-boundary-model (S1009); previews Step 112 semantic ownership reconstruction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A C-10 receipt claims that governed knowledge delivery occurred and acknowledgement was recorded.
a_rows_sample.statement: D1's decided receipt claim boundary, consumed verbatim by E2: delivery occurred (a world-fact) and acknowledgement was recorded (a record-fact), asymmetrically.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Twelve fields. Five parts each: (1) semantic meaning · (2) classification · (3) claim limitation · (4) evidence relationship · (5) ownership + C-10 responsibility.
a_rows_sample.statement: A twelve-field completeness model for C-10 receipts (receipt_id, issuer, session_reference, actor_reference, knowledge_reference, knowledge_version, delivery_timestamp, acknowledgement_timestamp, acknowledgement_method, external_correlation_reference, lifecycle_state, invalidation_reference), each classified REQUIRED/SUPPORTING/CORRELATION ONLY/FORBIDDEN with an ownership four-part model (semantic/data/invariant/authority).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Anti-corruption rules — seven, all binding on §5–§8
a_rows_sample.statement: Seven anti-corruption rules bind the receipt model: Recording ≠ Asserting; Reference ≠ Ownership; Correlation ≠ Authority; Evidence ≠ Proof; Receipt Identity ≠ Receipt Authority; Acknowledgement Recorded ≠ Knowledge Understood ≠ Applied ≠ Compliance Achieved; Receipt Evidence ≠ Independent Proof of Underlying Event.

a_rows_sample.anchor: receipt_id makes a receipt referable. It does NOT make it authoritative. A receipt is an evidence record, not a certificate.
a_rows_sample.statement: Receipt identity (a receipt is distinguishable from every other receipt) is distinguished from receipt authority (the receipt's assertions are binding); C-10 holds none of the latter beyond D1's claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Test: orthogonal ∧ necessary ∧ sufficient.
a_rows_sample.statement: The four-part ownership model (semantic/data/invariant/authority owner) is justified by testing it against orthogonality (fields diverge and converge across the same dimension set), necessity (without the split 'C-10 stores it' collapses into 'C-10 owns it'), and sufficiency (no field required a fifth dimension; NONE is a legal, informative authority-owner value).

a_rows_sample.anchor: actor_reference ... FORBIDDEN as a C-10-owned field.
a_rows_sample.statement: An actor_reference field is forbidden as C-10-owned because it would invite the identity-binding inference D1 disallows, would import C-5 (identity attestation, an open capability) into C-10, and because self-declared identity is only evidential (INV-ATTR-1/INV-ATTR-2); if the estate ever needs 'who acknowledged', it must arrive through C-5 attestation or as external_correlation_reference content, never as a C-10-owned field.

a_rows_sample.anchor: session_reference is simultaneously REQUIRED and NON-ATTESTING.
a_rows_sample.statement: session_reference is defined as a recorded association between the acknowledgement and an execution context — status RECORDED, NOT ATTESTED — and explicitly does not mean identity attestation, actor verification, or execution authority.

a_rows_sample.anchor: For each at-risk field: intended meaning · permitted inference · forbidden inference · the five-way misreading test (AUTHORITY · IDENTITY · APPLICABILITY · COMPLIANCE · VERIFICATION)
a_rows_sample.statement: A semantic-inflation discovery over five at-risk fields (receipt_id, issuer, actor_reference, session_reference, external_correlation_reference) each tested against a five-way misreading test (AUTHORITY/IDENTITY/APPLICABILITY/COMPLIANCE/VERIFICATION) with a recorded prohibition per field, e.g. 'a receipt exists, therefore the act was warranted' is explicitly forbidden.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Divergence 1 is the one with lasting cost: AMD6 called the rename bounded-context protection, not style.
a_rows_sample.statement: Four verified divergences between the delivered, AMD6-corrected E2 and a re-sent assignment: (1) field renamed to drop 'applicability' vs reverting to 'applicability_reference'; (2) field classification vocabulary present vs absent; (3) D1 asymmetry preserved vs restated symmetrically (a weaker delivery claim); (4) seven vs six anti-corruption rules. Restoring 'applicability' to a field name is flagged as reintroducing exactly the ownership implication the anti-corruption rule forbids.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This review does not evaluate architectural correctness... It checks completeness · provenance · decision-boundary preservation only.
a_rows_sample.statement: A Governance completeness/provenance review is explicitly bounded: it does not redesign the artifact, change field decisions, approve adoption, verify implementation correctness, or replace Architecture reasoning, and per AMD1 Flag H must never be cited as independent verification of the artifact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: §5.1 states 'four of them are classified SUPPORTING.' Mechanical count of the §5.1 table: 7 REQUIRED · 3 SUPPORTING · 1 CORRELATION ONLY · 1 FORBIDDEN = 12.
a_rows_sample.statement: INFO-1: the E2 artifact's own summary sentence miscounts its own field-classification table (claims four SUPPORTING fields; the table mechanically counts three); no field classification is wrong, only the summary sentence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the same process shaped both sides of the E2 ↔ D5 interface.
a_rows_sample.statement: INFO-2: the producing process of E2 also authored the D5 establishment-criteria proposal and the canonical C-10 analysis, meaning the same process shaped both sides of the E2↔D5 interface; recorded as non-blocking but as a residual for future acts to weigh.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Fourth occurrence of substantive input reaching a governed decision from outside the governed channel
a_rows_sample.statement: INFO-3: the Flag-O resolution and the seventh anti-corruption rule are consumed by E2 from a PO/ARB act absent from any registered instrument, marking the fourth recorded instance of substantive input reaching a governed decision from outside the governed channel within this work item; recorded as OBSERVED evidence under ES-006.1, not promoted to a standard.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Seventh Rule: Receipt Evidence ≠ Independent Proof of Underlying Event.
a_rows_sample.statement: The seventh anti-corruption rule, registered by this act rather than left unregistered: a receipt's delivery element is evidence toward a world-fact, and its acknowledgement element is evidence of a record-fact — without this rule the delivery element could be read as self-sufficient proof that delivery occurred, which D1 does not claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This is the fourth recorded instance of substantive input reaching a governed decision from outside the governed channel...Four occurrences within one work item is EVIDENCE, NOT A STANDARD.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit governance note that a repeated pattern (four occurrences) is recorded as OBSERVED evidence under ES-006.1 and that no methodology is promoted by the registration nor is the pattern converted into a rule.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ACCEPT WITH RECORDED FOLLOW-UP ITEMS (Option B) ... E2 STATUS: ADOPTED
a_rows_sample.statement: PO/ARB adopts the E2 receipt completeness model with recorded follow-up items (Option B chosen over plain accept, return-for-clarification, or reject) because none of the review's findings has architectural impact or requires reopening the artifact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Adopting a completeness model is not evidence of capability existence — under D5's own scheme a definition is Class C (future/architectural) evidence, which cannot establish existence by itself.
a_rows_sample.statement: Adopting a completeness/design model for a capability is explicitly distinguished from establishing that the capability exists; such adoption is Class C (future/architectural) evidence under the D5 scheme and cannot by itself establish existence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Four capabilities have NO OWNER: C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition. INFERRED: these four, not the six roles, are the substance of ADR-AIP-04.
b_rows_sample.statement: Headline finding: of a 20-capability inventory (C-1..C-20) derived from evidence of what the platform actually does, four capabilities (C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition) have no declared owner -- proposed as the real substance of ADR-AIP-04, in contrast to the six proposed roles.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EKS-01: the HANDOFF token's tokenRef acted as the de-facto knowledge channel and taught a lane the superseded path. A lane was taught the old path by its workflow record's tokenRef.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding F-5/F-5a: BC-7's HANDOFF tokenRef is performing de-facto knowledge distribution it does not own, evidenced by EKS-01 where a lane was taught a superseded path via its own workflow record's tokenRef -- the strongest evidence for a distinct C-10 (Knowledge Distribution) capability rather than 'Communication' in the ordinary sense.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Communication is two capabilities wearing one name. C-10 Knowledge Distribution -- a genuine, evidenced, unowned MECHANISM ... C-19 Communication Composition -- a STEWARDSHIP
b_rows_sample.statement: 'Communication' as commonly discussed is proposed to be two distinct capabilities: C-10 Knowledge Distribution (a genuine unowned mechanism, evidenced by EKS-01) and C-19 Communication Composition (a stewardship, failing the bounded-context test on language and reason-to-change); a single 'Communication Engineer' role would wrongly bind a mechanism gap and a reporting duty into one actor.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Distinguish, explicitly: ContextPublished, ContextSelected, ContextDelivered, ContextAvailable, ContextAcknowledged, ContextApplied, ContextVerified. Receipt is not proof of application or compliance.
b_rows_sample.statement: C-10's knowledge-distribution lifecycle is to be modelled as seven distinguished states (ContextPublished, ContextSelected, ContextDelivered, ContextAvailable, ContextAcknowledged, ContextApplied, ContextVerified); a receipt is never proof of application or compliance, only of a narrower claim.

type_signature.codomain: one of seven distinguished lifecycle states

b_rows_sample.anchor: that recurrence is itself evidence bearing on C-10 -- governed knowledge arriving outside the governed channel -- and the analysis may note it, but per AMD1 must not assume C-10 owns it.
b_rows_sample.statement: A pattern of substantive external input (a cited review, a 925-line brainstorming document, external research) repeatedly arriving outside the governed channel is recorded as evidence potentially bearing on C-10, but explicitly not assumed to be owned by C-10 without further decision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-5: YES existence, control-plane function category. C-10: NOT YET ESTABLISHED, deferred category. C-14: CONTESTED, deferred. C-19: YES, stewardship/cross-cutting category. The forbidden collapse is absent.
b_rows_sample.statement: Independent verification confirms the existence/category split was applied without the forbidden collapse for all four capabilities: C-5 exists (control-plane function), C-10's existence is NOT YET ESTABLISHED (category deferred), C-14's existence is CONTESTED (category deferred), C-19 exists (stewardship/cross-cutting), each argued from positive properties rather than derived from the other axis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The four are not four candidate contexts. They are one CONTROL LOOP with four distinct capabilities in it. policy/knowledge DEFINED (BC-1) -> C-10 DELIVERS it to the gated session -> C-14 GATES the act -> C-19 EXPRESSES the outcome <- C-5 ATTESTS who acted
b_rows_sample.statement: Structural finding: C-5, C-10, C-14, C-19 are not four independent candidate bounded contexts but four capabilities within one control loop -- BC-1's policy/knowledge is delivered by C-10 to a gated session, C-14 gates the act, C-19 expresses the outcome, and C-5 attests who acted and how separately -- while still having four distinct reasons to change, so the relationship, not a merged boundary, is what explains them.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-10 is NOT the whole path. Its smallest coherent boundary is APPLICABILITY + RECEIPT. ... What nothing owns is: (a) deciding WHICH governed knowledge is applicable to THIS assignment, and (b) evidencing that the executing session actually holds the CURRENT version.
b_rows_sample.statement: C-10's smallest coherent capability boundary is proposed to be applicability determination plus receipt (not the whole created->published->selected->retrieved->delivered->acknowledged->applied->verified path), since creation/publication is BC-1's, retrieval/bootstrap is BC-6's, and only applicability-determination and receipt-evidencing are genuinely unowned.

b_rows_sample.anchor: fails on 6 of 10 => a STEWARDSHIP / cross-cutting expression concern ... the only state that could make a Communication context real -- delivery-with-acknowledgement -- is C-10's receipt, not C-19's. building C-10 would REDUCE the case for a Communication context.
b_rows_sample.statement: C-19 fails a ten-part bounded-context test on six of ten criteria (own language, independent lifecycle, independent authority, authoritative state, distinct reason to change, audience/consent/channel concepts) and is classified a stewardship/cross-cutting expression concern; the one property that could give it authoritative state (delivery-with-acknowledgement) actually belongs to C-10, so realizing C-10 reduces rather than increases the case for a Communication bounded context.

b_rows_sample.anchor: two independent grounds: an ADOPTED invariant (INV-ATTR-2) that presupposes the capability, and the capability has been PERFORMED. C-10 satisfies neither limb.
b_rows_sample.statement: A two-limb existence test emerges from Amendment 1's C-5 analysis: a capability's existence is supported by (1) an ADOPTED invariant presupposing it, and/or (2) the capability having been PERFORMED at least once; C-5 satisfies both limbs (INV-ATTR-2 adopted; SB-1 clearance is a performed instance), while C-10 satisfies neither.

b_rows_sample.anchor: receipt <= application <= understanding <= compliance ... A receipt can only ever evidence ContextAcknowledged. ContextApplied and ContextVerified are different claims requiring different evidence, and no receipt can supply them.
b_rows_sample.statement: C-10's seven-state receipt model is elaborated with an explicit ceiling: a receipt can only ever evidence ContextAcknowledged, never ContextApplied or ContextVerified, and OQ-J is reformulated from a yes/no 'is the receipt authoritative' question into five separately-tested claims (delivery, possession, applicability, execution, compliance authority), of which a receipt can carry at most the first two.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Option C binds the receipt to an act the estate has never performed, that nobody owns, and that the analysis says a receipt cannot carry.
b_rows_sample.statement: Option C for C-10 receipt semantics is found unsatisfiable as worded, because it would require the receipt to reference an 'applicability decision' (ContextSelected) that never occurs and has no owner in the estate -- the same referent-gap defect noticed independently in several later documents.

b_rows_sample.anchor: establishes an applicability reference -- a pointer to decision A. does NOT establish the correctness of applicability -- whether A was right. A pointer to a judgement is not an assertion that the judgement was sound.
b_rows_sample.statement: C-10 Decision 1 (Option C) resolves OQ-J's authority defect by distinguishing an applicability REFERENCE (a pointer, which the receipt may carry) from applicability CORRECTNESS (whether the referenced judgement was sound, which the receipt does not establish) -- 'AUTHORITY IS CLAIM-SCOPED' is recorded as the invariant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The decision commits the receipt to reference an applicability decision that the estate never produces. ... This is no longer an authority problem -- it is an existence problem about the referent.
b_rows_sample.statement: A distinct 'referent gap' (as opposed to the already-solved authority gap) is identified: the decided receipt is required to reference an applicability decision (ContextSelected) that the estate never actually produces and nobody owns, so a conforming receipt is not presently populatable -- left as PO/ARB's to decide (optional/null reference, vs. a standing obligation to build ContextSelected).

b_rows_sample.anchor: No typed KnowledgeDeliveryReceipt structure is adopted -- and, verified: no such type exists anywhere in the estate
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit confirmation that no typed receipt data structure (e.g. KnowledgeDeliveryReceipt) exists anywhere in the estate's code or docs; schema design is deferred to Architecture and is not created by this semantic decision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Recommended: YES -- C-10 exists as a capability, with realization NONE and its outer boundary OPEN. The load-bearing argument is D1 itself. ... A decision fixing the authoritative claim boundary of C-10's artifact presupposes a subject for that artifact.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governance recommends C-10 existence = YES, arguing that D1's decided receipt-claim boundary presupposes a subject for that claim, supported by a distinct reason to change, a distinct outcome, and two genuinely unowned stages sharing one purpose (applicability + receipt) -- this recommendation is later overturned by the PO/ARB (S0120 D2) as conflating a decided semantic with a performed capability.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Of five activities: one occurs and is owned elsewhere; four do not occur at all. Evidence of C-10 having occurred: none
b_rows_sample.statement: Applying the ten-question existence test to the estate's evidence: of C-10's five constituent activities (applicability, delivery, acknowledgement, claim-scoped receipt, invalidation/reconciliation), only one occurs and it is owned by other contexts (BC-6/BC-7), while four never occur at all and have no owner -- the counter-evidence supporting the later NOT YET ESTABLISHED verdict.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The platform cannot attest a specified session execution. identity binding must NOT be placed inside C-10's authoritative state, because C-10 cannot establish it. It is C-5-shaped
b_rows_sample.statement: The sharpest finding in the D3 prep: a C-10 receipt's binding to a specific session execution can never be stronger than what INV-ATTR-1/INV-ATTR-2 permit (self-declared, not attested), so identity binding cannot be placed inside C-10's authoritative state -- it is C-5-shaped, and C-5 owns no attestation record either.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Adopting the receipt as authoritative state would supply limb one of the estate's existence test. A decision framed as constitutive would decide existence by the back door -- which this act forbids. Framed as a boundary specification, it does not.
b_rows_sample.statement: A distinction between a 'constitutive' decision (which would establish existence as a side effect) and a 'boundary specification' decision (which defines a candidate scope without establishing existence) is drawn, warning that D3 must be framed as the latter to avoid silently satisfying the D2 existence test.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C -- SPLIT. Fits every decided constraint. It matches OQ-J's 2-of-5 result ... applicability / transport / execution are already owned or already excluded
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommendation: Option C (SPLIT) for D3 -- C-10 would own only the receipt/attestation lifecycle and state (receipt identity, lifecycle state, invalidation, completeness), explicitly excluding applicability determination, delivery transport, session execution, identity binding, dispute adjudication, execution authority, and compliance/application.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'c10-e2-receipt-completeness-model' POSSIBLY relates to 'capability-c10-knowledge-distribution' (batch B0004). Note: The twelve-field receipt completeness model (S0122), its governance review, Flag-O registration, and adoption decision (S0123-S0126); a distinct sub-artifact of the C-10 discovery chain, closely coupled to but not identical with C-10 existence itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Logical status L(P) ∈ {T,F,B,N} ... Confidence C(P) ∈ [0,1] ... This is one of the most important architectural separations we've found.
a_rows_sample.statement: Separates four distinct claim dimensions that must not be confused: Logical status L(P) in {T,F,B,N}, Confidence C(P) in [0,1], Evidence quantity E(P)=n, Evidence quality Q(P) in [0,1], explicitly warning against confusing four-valued logic with four confidence levels; called one of the most important architectural separations found so far.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Audit A → compliant, Audit B → non-compliant ... the real state may be L(P)=B ... Logical state: CONFLICTED. Confidence: 52%. This tells us far more than "52% true."
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: two independent compliance audits disagree; a naive Bayesian system collapsing this to P(compliant)=0.52 loses the fact that the real logical state is B (genuinely conflicting evidence), whereas reporting Logical state=CONFLICTED and Confidence=52% separately conveys far more.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K(P) = (L,C,E,Q,U,D,T) ... strong conflicting evidence -> B, .50 | insufficient evidence -> N, .50 ... could both have 50% confidence while representing radically different epistemic situations.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a seven-component knowledge vector K(P)=(L,C,E,Q,U,D,T) (logical state, confidence/support, evidence, evidence quality, uncertainty, defeaters/conflicts, temporal validity), with a worked table showing strong-support->T/.98, strong-refutation->F/.97, strong-conflict->B/.50, insufficient-evidence->N/.50 -- the last two sharing 50% confidence yet representing radically different epistemic situations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: we should not automatically equate philosophical categories such as mithyā with formal three-valued logical semantics ... SOURCE CLAIM -> possible conceptual analogy -> research hypothesis, not SOURCE CLAIM -> KnowledgeOS fact.
a_rows_sample.statement: Cautions against treating the article's association of Vedanta's satya/asatya/mithya with three-valued logic, or its claim that quantum mechanics/Schrodinger's cat exemplifies three-valued logic, as established; both are oversimplifications, and the correct extraction discipline is SOURCE CLAIM -> possible conceptual analogy -> research hypothesis, never SOURCE CLAIM -> KnowledgeOS fact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Multi-valued logic: T,F,B,N ... Fuzzy logic: μ(P) ∈ [0,1] ... P = (L,μ)
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes multi-valued logic (discrete states T/F/B/N) from fuzzy logic (degree of membership mu(P) in [0,1]) as solving different problems that must be represented independently, proposing a combined P=(L,mu), e.g. Logical state=CONFLICTED with Support degree=0.78, richer than a single scalar.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Forward: E → K. Inverse: K → E* where E* is the minimum required evidence. ... one of the most important mechanisms for KnowledgeOS governance.
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses an inverse problem alongside the usual forward E->K inference: given a desired/current claim or state K, what is the minimum required evidence E* that would legitimately justify it (K->E*)? Illustrated by asking what evidence would be necessary to legitimately reach a VERIFIED state; proposed as one of the most important potential KnowledgeOS governance mechanisms.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D(K_current, K_required) ... What knowledge is missing? That is much more actionable.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines an epistemic distance D(K_current,K_required) measuring how far the current knowledge state is from the state required to make a decision, illustrated by Current=UNDETERMINED, Required=VERIFIED, Gap={missing independent evidence, missing reproducibility, missing provenance}, concluding the system can answer 'what knowledge is missing?' rather than merely 'not enough knowledge.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Can we construct a measurable Knowledge State Space? ... logical state × evidence strength × uncertainty × provenance × model dependence × temporal validity × contradiction × invariance ... rather than adding more philosophical sources immediately.
a_rows_sample.statement: Freezes a provisional thirteen-lens research stack (Pramana, Ganesha, Leonardo, Krishna, Shani, Dhatu, Zero, Logic, Time, World Model, Statistical, Inverse, Hofstadter) with one defining question each, and poses the next concrete research question -- can a measurable Knowledge State Space be constructed with axes {logical state, evidence strength, uncertainty, provenance, model dependence, temporal validity, contradiction, invariance} -- explicitly deciding to formalize and test the accumulated theory rather than add more philosophical sources.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would not adopt the claim from the Medium article that Wittgenstein's Tractatus itself establishes Hindu four-valued logic or quantum logic. The uploaded book does not support that interpretation. ... S(P,t,c)
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly rejects a Medium article's claim that Wittgenstein's Tractatus establishes Hindu four-valued or quantum logic, stating the primary source does not support that interpretation; independently proposes KnowledgeOS learn an eight-value epistemic-state set (TRUE, FALSE, UNKNOWN, UNRESOLVED, CONTRADICTED, CONTEXTUAL, OUTDATED, NOT-APPLICABLE) modeled as S(P,t,c) depending on proposition, time, context and available evidence, rather than binary true/false.

a_rows_sample.anchor: TruthValue enum is potentially dangerous ... TruthStatus: TRUE, FALSE, UNDETERMINED, NOT_APPLICABLE. KnowledgeStatus: KNOWN, UNKNOWN, UNCERTAIN, DISPUTED, UNEXPLORED. ConflictStatus: CONSISTENT, CONFLICTING, INCONSISTENT.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the original model's single TruthValue enum {TRUE,FALSE,UNKNOWN,BOTH,NEITHER} as dangerously conflating unrelated scales (TRUE/FALSE concern semantic/model-theoretic evaluation, UNKNOWN concerns knowledge availability, BOTH/NEITHER reflect a paraconsistent/incomplete logic, and unsupported/disputed concern evidence/assertion state), splitting it into three independent enums: TruthStatus{TRUE,FALSE,UNDETERMINED,NOT_APPLICABLE}, KnowledgeStatus{KNOWN,UNKNOWN,UNCERTAIN,DISPUTED,UNEXPLORED}, ConflictStatus{CONSISTENT,CONFLICTING,INCONSISTENT}, with BOTH/NEITHER retained only as values within an explicitly chosen four-valued logic regime, not as universal kernel values.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero = Neutral starting condition ... It begins as: UNKNOWN
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero as neutral knowledge state: Zero != Nothing, it is a neutral starting condition. A new knowledge object begins without authority, evidence, validation or interpretation -- it begins as UNKNOWN.

b_rows_sample.anchor: UNKNOWN != False. UNKNOWN != Missing. UNKNOWN = Known unresolved state
b_rows_sample.statement: UNKNOWN is proposed as a first-class state, distinct from False and from Missing: UNKNOWN = a known, unresolved state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: UNKNOWN != False. UNKNOWN != Missing. UNKNOWN = Known unresolved state
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero lens: UNKNOWN restated as a first-class known-unresolved state, distinct from False and Missing.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS should not force: Unknown -> False / Unknown -> Guess / Unknown -> Empty. Instead: Unknown -> Known Unknown
b_rows_sample.statement: Combining Zero ('unknown is a valid state') with ECS ('failure does not destroy truth, failure pauses advancement'): Unknown should be preserved and later resolved, never forced into False/Guess/Empty.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Different observations may represent different projections of the same underlying object.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reinterprets the elephant-and-blind-men story (cited by the source) not as 'everyone is equally right' but as 'different observations may represent different projections of the same underlying object', formalized as perspectives A/B/C/D undergoing structural comparison to yield a common invariant = ZERO.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge is perspective dependent, but structure may be perspective invariant.
b_rows_sample.statement: Abstracts the source's citation of Subhash Kak's six-darsanas-as-cube-walls metaphor into the principle 'knowledge is perspective dependent, but structure may be perspective invariant', with the research question 'what survives when we rotate the perspective?' answered by ZERO = invariant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z_M(K) = invariant across plausible worlds ... The technology disappears. The invariant remains.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces modal Zero Z_M(K) = invariant across plausible worlds, alongside a claimed prior representation Zero Z_R(K)=invariant across representations and temporal Zero Z_T(K)=invariant across time; illustrated by four possible event-bus technology choices (Kafka/RabbitMQ/sync API/another event bus) all preserving the invariant requirement 'evidence publication must remain replayable' -- the technology disappears, the invariant remains.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z = ⋂_i Structure(I_i) ... What structure remains invariant across competing models, representations, times, and perspectives? That may be one of our strongest candidates for robust knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the Zero lens as Z=intersection_i Structure(I_i) over interpretations generated from multiple world models W1..Wn (not necessarily literal set intersection in implementation), asking what structure remains invariant across competing models, representations, times and perspectives, proposed as one of the strongest candidates for robust knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: O_i = π_i(R) ... O1 ≠ O2 doesn't necessarily mean R1 ≠ R2. It may simply mean π1 ≠ π2. This gives us a very useful projection lens.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the elephant analogy as a projection: observation Oi=pi_i(R) for underlying reality/object R and observer perspective pi_i, concluding that differing observations O1!=O2 need not imply differing underlying realities R1!=R2 -- it may simply reflect differing perspectives pi1!=pi2 -- named the 'projection lens'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z = Invariant(O1,...,On) ... Zero is not "nothing." It is the minimum invariant structure that survives changes in representation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Given observations O1..On, defines Z=Invariant(O1,...,On) and explicitly corrects a possible misreading: Zero is not 'nothing', it is the minimum invariant structure that survives changes in representation -- called one of the strongest concepts in the entire exploration.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Dhātu = transformation structure ... Zero = invariant structure ... what changed? / what remained?
b_rows_sample.statement: States a Dhatu/Zero duality: given O1 --T1--> O2 --T2--> O3, Dhatu asks what transformation generated the new state (Dhatu = transformation structure) while Zero asks what remained (Zero = invariant structure).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge itself should not be reduced to its representations.
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens result on Williamson: after removing beliefs, documents, language, databases, probabilities, possible worlds, embeddings, topics, LLMs, what survives is minimal: 'A participant is related to a proposition/content in a world/context/time such that the proposition is true and the participant is in a factive state of knowing.' Knowledge itself should not be reduced to its representations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Participants make commitments. 2. Commitments have inferential consequences. 3. Some commitments are supported/entitled...
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens extraction on Brandom (removing language/English/sentences/speech/Frege/Wittgenstein/philosophy) yields ten survivor claims: participants make commitments; commitments have inferential consequences; some commitments are supported/entitled; commitments can conflict; participants assess one another's commitments; new actions alter the state; implicit relations can become explicit; concepts are characterized partly by inferential roles; objectivity can emerge within social assessment; a claim is not merely a string but a position in a normative/inferential structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Unknown is not simply an error state. It is a legitimate epistemic condition.
b_rows_sample.statement: ASP answer-set semantics give TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN query results and ground at least three distinct kinds of 'unknown': unknown because alternatives remain (P and ¬P both possible), unknown because the agent is unaware (neither represented), and unknown because a default was blocked (an exception/missing condition prevented an otherwise-applicable default). The earlier flat UNKNOWN category should become an Epistemic Status taxonomy: true/false/unresolved-alternatives/not-represented-unaware/defeasibly-inferable-but-blocked/etc; the exact taxonomy remains a research question but the distinction itself is now strongly grounded.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Absence must not silently become an epistemic state.
b_rows_sample.statement: Danger flagged in the Projection model: 'If Projection P2 doesn't contain X, therefore X is false' would be wrong, since absence from a projection could mean not relevant, not visible, not assessed, outside scope, unavailable, superseded, or genuinely no longer justified — these are different meanings. This connects to the ZERO lens: absence must not silently become an epistemic state, giving another reason to preserve ZERO discipline within the Projection idea.

b_rows_sample.anchor: U(e) ∈ {alternative, unrepresented, blocked-default, outside-scope, computationally-unresolved}
b_rows_sample.statement: Unknownness U(e) is proposed not as a Boolean but a classification (alternative / unrepresented / blocked-default / outside-scope / computationally-unresolved), with the exact taxonomy left empirical and countable for future statistical analysis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. There is an underlying world/domain. 2. A participant has beliefs/knowledge about it. 3. Only part of that knowledge may be explicitly represented...
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens extraction on Brachman & Levesque (removing FOL/Prolog/frames/description logic/SAT/default logic/Bayesian networks/STRIPS/GOLOG) yields twelve survivor claims: an underlying world/domain exists; a participant has beliefs/knowledge about it; only part is explicitly represented; representation is a mapping between domains; reasoning derives implicit content from explicit content; meaning depends on interpretation/context; different representation languages have different expressive power; reasoning capability is resource-limited; knowledge changes and can be revised; uncertainty/vagueness require richer representations; the same knowledge may have different representations; action depends on knowledge — described as extraordinarily close to the current model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: what survives across *both* phases is: **a knower/participant · something known · a ground · and a record that the two were connected.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens applied across both phases: after stripping optional attributes, what survives universally is a knower/participant, something known, a ground, and a record that the two were connected — every phase and nearly every model retains those four; nothing else survives universally. The corpus distinguishes 'nothing exists' from 'we do not know' (0258: 'Knowledge is not only about what exists'; formal law §9: unknown≠absent≠false). Whether UNKNOWN is the absence of Knowledge or a state of an identified object is NOT resolved by the corpus: formal law (⟨Z-1⟩) says UNKNOWN/ABSENT/FALSE/REJECTED are states of an identified epistemic object, while kernel document 125708 §17 pushes the other way ('UNKNOWN must not be a single epistemic state', eight readings) — no new state proposed here.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AF-004 · Zero's chronology inverts CF-005's apparent ordering
b_rows_sample.statement: The repository's 'third sense' of Zero (Z-KOS-001 meta-principle) and the absence-lens sense are BOTH dated 2026-08-22; the goal-gap function sense is the LATEST (2026-08-27 era) — inverting an apparent ordering implied by CF-005.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CF-005 · Zero naming collision — a third sense
b_rows_sample.statement: Repository Zero (Z-KOS-001) is a foundational meta-principle explicitly refused as kernel article and implementation object ('Zero is the name for that prevention', 'Zero != Component = Property of the boundaries'), whereas v0.2 Zero is the computable goal-gap function Zero(K, EC); same term, incompatible senses, extending the CON-01 lineage with an implementation-side third sense; no repository counterpart of the goal-gap function exists, and the eta-totality/G-residual question (T-9) stays open.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'catuskoti-multivalued-epistemic-logic-lens' POSSIBLY relates to 'zero-neutral-state-lens' (batch B0013). Note: S0500's and S0504's extraction of catuskoti (Buddhist/Jain four-valued logic T/F/Both/Neither) as a KnowledgeOS logic layer: EpistemicState(P) in {T,F,B,N} kept strictly separate from scalar Confidence C(P), an epistemic-entropy measure, the 'both' state reinterpreted as possible scope/time/interpretation difference rather than true contradiction, an elephant-analogy projection formalization Oi=pi_i(R), and (in S0504) a tightened K(P)=(L,C,E,Q,U,D,T) knowledge vector plus a Forward(E->K)/Inverse(K->E*) evidence-sufficiency problem; recorded here as UNKNOWN-OBJECT-CANDIDATE in individual contributions pending resolution against zero-neutral-state-lens and other Zero variants.

a_rows_sample.anchor: causal inference compares outcomes in the same population under different interventions, whereas association compares different subsets of the population based on what actually happened.
a_rows_sample.statement: Observational Knowledge (X correlated with Y) and Causal Knowledge (intervention on X changes Y) must never have the same epistemic status; 'Teams using architecture reviews had fewer production incidents' is not equivalent to 'Introducing architecture reviews reduces production incidents', the latter requiring causal assumptions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: an effect requires specifying the outcome, the actions being compared and the population. ... CausalQuestion: population, intervention, comparator, outcome, time horizon, estimand
a_rows_sample.statement: CausalQuestion object formalized with population/intervention/comparator/outcome/time_horizon/estimand fields, replacing an unconstrained 'Does X affect Y?' question, illustrated with an example (projects using KnowledgeOS; mandatory architecture review vs none; architecture-related production defects; 12 months; average causal risk difference); called 'an epistemic schema', not merely a statistical method.

a_rows_sample.anchor: individual causal effect through the difference between Y1 = outcome if intervention happens and Y0 = outcome if intervention does not happen ... normally only one of these outcomes is observed for each individual.
a_rows_sample.statement: Counterfactual Lens: KnowledgeOS should represent causal claims as counterfactual claims (observed evidence + counterfactual estimand + identifying assumptions), not ordinary observations, since the counterfactual outcome (what defect rate a project would have had without an intervention) is never directly observed; proposed for first-class representation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: causal diagrams to identify common causes/confounding, conditioning on common effects/selection bias, measurement bias, effect modification ... KnowledgeOS should distinguish semantic relationships from causal relationships.
a_rows_sample.statement: Causal Graph Lens: a causal graph (directed edges with confounding/selection/measurement structure) differs fundamentally from an ordinary semantic knowledge-graph 'related_to' edge; proposes a distinct CausalGraph construct with explicit edge semantics rather than adding a bare 'causes' edge to the existing graph.

a_rows_sample.anchor: confounding as arising when treatment and outcome share common causes. ... CAUSAL CLAIM REVIEW ... Exchangeability: NOT ESTABLISHED ... Causal conclusion: ABSTAIN
a_rows_sample.statement: Confounding Lens as a first-class anti-false-inference mechanism, illustrated by 'experienced teams' confounding an architecture-review-vs-quality relationship; a CAUSAL CLAIM REVIEW output lists observed association, potential confounders (team maturity, project size, engineering leadership), exchangeability status, and a resulting ABSTAIN conclusion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: conditioning on common effects can produce selection bias, and even randomization does not protect against selection bias occurring after randomization. ... Why are these observations present in the evidence set?
a_rows_sample.statement: Selection-Bias Lens: selecting evidence (e.g. only successful projects) before inference can bias conclusions ('Architecture practice X works') even without explicit randomization failure; KnowledgeOS should ask why observations are present in the evidence set at all.

a_rows_sample.anchor: measurement error can make the observed association differ from the causal effect ... The observation mechanism itself becomes part of the evidence model.
a_rows_sample.statement: Measurement-Bias Lens maps to observation provenance: Reality -> Observation mechanism -> Stored evidence -> Statistical inference, with the observation mechanism itself becoming part of the evidence model, since exchangeability/positivity/consistency alone are insufficient when variables are measured incorrectly.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the relevant combinations of treatment and covariates actually occur in the population. ... Claim scope = ALL teams / Evidence support = narrow population -> POSITIVITY / GENERALISABILITY WARNING
a_rows_sample.statement: Positivity/Coverage Lens becomes an Evidence Coverage Check: a claim's scope (e.g. 'all teams') must be checked against actual evidence coverage (e.g. only large Java teams), producing a positivity/generalisability warning when scope exceeds coverage.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the observed outcome under the treatment actually received corresponds to the relevant counterfactual outcome. ... If 'treatment X' has multiple uncontrolled versions, the causal question itself may be ill-defined.
a_rows_sample.statement: Consistency Lens: the intervention must be sufficiently well-defined that 'X happened' has a single meaning (contrast vague 'AI governance' with a precisely versioned 'AI governance policy v1.3 + mandatory architecture review + defined approval workflow + defined enforcement mechanism'), connecting causal consistency to ubiquitous-language/bounded-semantics concerns.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Intervention: DO(X) ... OBSERVE -> HYPOTHESIZE -> INTERVENE -> OBSERVE OUTCOME -> UPDATE CAUSAL EVIDENCE ... KnowledgeOS becomes capable of supporting organizational learning, not merely document retrieval.
a_rows_sample.statement: Intervention Lens: represent claims as do(X) interventions with expected outcome and counterfactual, enabling an OBSERVE->HYPOTHESIZE->INTERVENE->OBSERVE OUTCOME->UPDATE CAUSAL EVIDENCE loop that supports organizational learning rather than mere document retrieval.

a_rows_sample.anchor: time-varying treatments, time-varying confounders, treatment-confounder feedback ... treatment-confounder feedback can make traditional adjustment methods biased even when the relevant confounders are measured.
a_rows_sample.statement: Time-Varying Knowledge Lens: KnowledgeOS is inherently longitudinal (X0->Y0->X1->Y1->X2->Y2, earlier decisions affecting later evidence), so a naive single-step X->Y model is often insufficient, echoing the book's warning that treatment-confounder feedback can bias traditional adjustment even with measured confounders.

a_rows_sample.anchor: variable selection for causal inference is difficult and recommend multiple sensitivity analyses rather than pretending there is one universally correct selection procedure. ... ROBUST CAUSAL CONCLUSION or CAUSAL CONCLUSION SENSITIVE TO ASSUMPTIONS
a_rows_sample.statement: Sensitivity/Triangulation Lens (called 'one of the strongest principles in the entire book'): run multiple methods/alternative assumptions/alternative causal graphs over the same evidence and check convergence, yielding either a ROBUST CAUSAL CONCLUSION or a CAUSAL CONCLUSION SENSITIVE TO ASSUMPTIONS, rather than a single model producing a single answer.

a_rows_sample.anchor: predictive ML variable selection is not equivalent to causal variable selection ... ML can be combined with causal inference through doubly robust estimators, but ML does not magically solve confounding or uncertainty.
a_rows_sample.statement: Machine Learning Lens correction: 'Prediction != causal inference' proposed as a KnowledgeOS architectural invariant, because predicting treatment well is not the same as including variables necessary for exchangeability, and unnecessary variables can increase variance or create positivity problems.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS SHALL NOT promote an associational finding to a causal claim without an explicit causal question, identified intervention and comparator, declared causal assumptions, an identifiability assessment, and an appropriate uncertainty/sensitivity assessment. ... KnowledgeOS SHALL preserve the distinction between predictive validity and causal validity.
a_rows_sample.statement: Two proposed KnowledgeOS constitutional principles synthesizing both books: (1) no promotion of an associational finding to a causal claim without explicit causal question/intervention/comparator/assumptions/identifiability assessment/uncertainty-sensitivity assessment; (2) preserve the distinction between predictive validity and causal validity, since predictive and causal models serve different purposes and predictive variable selection can be inappropriate for causal inference.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Before choosing a statistical method, determine what question you are actually trying to answer and whether that question is identifiable from the available evidence under explicit assumptions. ... KnowledgeOS needs a formal taxonomy of claim types and corresponding inference obligations.
a_rows_sample.statement: Synthesizes both source books into a single QUESTION -> {Descriptive|Associational|Causal} -> (for Causal) Identification -> {Estimation|Abstain} -> Uncertainty -> Robustness -> Sensitivity Analysis -> Epistemic Status decision hierarchy; concludes KnowledgeOS should become an 'Evidence Reasoning System with explicit statistical and causal epistemics' rather than a generic AI/ML analytics engine, and flags a formal taxonomy of claim types with corresponding inference obligations as the next architectural research step.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not automatically turn every noun into a domain object. ... conceptual richness does not prove a software bounded context.
a_rows_sample.statement: DDD warning applied to the causal vocabulary extracted from the book (Causal Question, Intervention, Comparator, Outcome, Population, Time Zero, Counterfactual, Causal Effect, Assumption, Exchangeability, Positivity, Consistency, Confounder, Mediator, Collider, Selection, Measurement, Estimand, Identification, Estimation, Sensitivity, Evidence): ownership, lifecycle, invariants, decisions, consistency boundaries, language and dependencies must be discovered before any noun becomes a domain object.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Book of Evidence tells us HOW observations become evidence ... Causal Inference tells us HOW evidence supports causal claims ... Statistical methods tell us HOW evidence is quantified ... DDD tells us HOW to model the domain ... Wisdom tells us HOW to determine what evidence is needed.
a_rows_sample.statement: Combines all four books+lenses into one epistemic operating loop: Decision -> Evidence Need -> Evidence Question -> Acquisition Design -> {Selection Procedure, Measurement Procedure, Context Conditions} -> Observation -> Acquisition Audit -> Candidate Evidence -> Evidence Assessment -> Statistical Analysis -> Causal Assessment -> Knowledge -> Wisdom -> Decision, described as 'starting to look like the actual KnowledgeOS epistemic operating loop.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: We should not conclude: 'Everything in KnowledgeOS should be Bayesian.' ... Also: Bayesian ≠ causal. ... They interact ... But they are not the same thing.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit scope limits: Bayesian updating complements but does not replace deduction/causal inference/statistical estimation/formal verification/empirical testing/domain rules/logical constraints/governance/human judgment; and Bayesian belief-updating ('how should belief change given evidence?') is distinct from causal inference ('what would happen under intervention?') even though they interact in a chain Evidence->Bayesian update->belief in causal model->causal inference->decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Correlation between action and outcome does not establish causation (transition to Step 43)
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a missing dimension beyond State/Evidence/Decision/Action/Outcome: correlation between action and outcome does not establish causation. If KnowledgeOS observes Action=A followed by Outcome=B, it cannot automatically conclude A->B -- especially important if KnowledgeOS is expected to learn from its own decisions. Opens Step 43 (Causal Reasoning, Intervention, Counterfactuals and Learning from Outcomes) with the central principle that an outcome following an action does not prove the action caused the outcome, framed as essential for KnowledgeOS to 'learn from engineering decisions rather than merely record them'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(Y|A) is not generally equal to P(Y|do(A))
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces the causal layer by formalizing the central distinction between Correlation and Causation as P(Y|A) not generally equal to P(Y|do(A)) -- called one of the most important mathematical foundations for an intelligent KnowledgeOS. Motivated by the premise that observing Action=A followed by Outcome=Y does not license concluding A->Y ('temporal sequence and correlation are not sufficient to establish causation').

b_rows_sample.anchor: NotIdentified as a distinct epistemic state from Unknown; ComputationalDifficulty != EpistemicNonIdentifiability
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines identification: a causal effect is identified if available assumptions and observed data determine the estimand; otherwise NotIdentified. States KnowledgeOS needs Unknown and NotIdentified as distinct concepts -- Unknown may mean insufficient information, NotIdentified means the desired quantity cannot be uniquely inferred under the current model/data/assumptions even with more information. Gives the crucial distinction ComputationalDifficulty != EpistemicNonIdentifiability: a problem may be Identified but computationally expensive (e.g. O(n^3) or worse), or NotIdentified even with unlimited computation -- 'no amount of computation can recover information that the assumptions/data do not identify'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Causal assumptions as first-class modeling knowledge; seven-item non-conflatable epistemic-object taxonomy
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires an explicit Assumption(A) object (e.g. NoUnmeasuredConfounding), 'not a fact about the world... a modeling assumption'. Consolidates a seven-item epistemic classification that must not be conflated: ObservedFact, DerivedClaim, StatisticalEstimate, CausalHypothesis, CausalEstimate, Assumption, CounterfactualEstimate -- each with different lifecycle, invariants, provenance, validation, authority, and failure modes, 'extremely aligned with DDD... they should not necessarily become one giant Knowledge aggregate', suggesting possible bounded contexts (Evidence, Knowledge, Inference, CausalAnalysis, Decision, Governance) whose exact boundaries remain an architectural hypothesis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Four new causal invariants: I_Causal, I_Intervention, I_Counterfactual, I_Identification
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces four named invariants: I_Causal (ObservedAssociation cannot be promoted to CausalRelation without an explicit causal basis); I_Intervention (P(Y|X) cannot be used as P(Y|do(X)) without justified causal assumptions); I_Counterfactual (unobserved potential outcomes must be represented as inferred/estimated, not observed facts); I_Identification (a causal estimate cannot be marked identified unless its identification assumptions are satisfied). Gives the causal provenance chain CausalEstimate -> Estimand -> CausalModel -> Assumptions -> Data -> Evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 63 verdict: four refinements; consolidated K=(E,K,I,C,D,A,O,L) tuple; opens Step 64 on model uncertainty and self-validation
