a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t=(X_t,M_t) ... a state machine with mode-dependent transition semantics
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects modeling Sattva/Rajas/Tamas as three separate kernels K_S,K_R,K_T; instead K_t=(X_t,M_t) where X_t is the knowledge/epistemic state and M_t in {S,R,T} the current operational mode, with K_t --O_{M_t}--> K_{t+1} and the mode itself able to change M_t->M_{t+1}, giving K_{t+1}=T(K_t,o_t,M_t) -- a state machine with mode-dependent transition semantics.

a_rows_sample.anchor: O_S=\{Observe,Compare,Discriminate,Corroborate,Qualify,Resolve,Validate\} ... O_R=\{Search,Acquire,Transform,Investigate,Generate,Execute\} ... O_T=\{DetectBlock,ExposeUnknown,Suspend,Flag,Invalidate,RequestEvidence\}
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes mode-dependent admissible operator sets O_{M_t} subset O = full operator set: O_S (Sattva, clarification/discrimination mode) = {Observe,Compare,Discriminate,Corroborate,Qualify,Resolve,Validate}; O_R (Rajas, activity/acquisition mode) = {Search,Acquire,Transform,Investigate,Generate,Execute}; O_T (Tamas, obscuration mode) = diagnostic operators {DetectBlock,ExposeUnknown,Suspend,Flag,Invalidate,RequestEvidence}, not productive operators. Warns Rajas is not inherently bad (a system with zero Rajas would never investigate anything); the problem is uncontrolled Rajas (activity does not imply knowledge) -- 'more operations do not necessarily produce more knowledge'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: T \xrightarrow{\text{Detect ignorance}} Zero \xrightarrow{\text{Buddhi}} S
a_rows_sample.statement: Connects Tamas to Zero: Zero -> representation/detection of epistemic absence; Tamas can trigger a transition toward Sattva via: T --Detect ignorance--> Zero --Buddhi--> S -- proposed as a very interesting mode-transition hypothesis.

a_rows_sample.anchor: B_t: (E_t,K_t,M_t) \rightarrow \{\text{accept},\text{reject},\text{investigate},\text{suspend},\text{transform}\} ... DO NOTHING ... is itself a Buddhi decision.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Buddhi as mode-sensitive: B_t:(E_t,K_t,M_t)->{accept,reject,investigate,suspend,transform}. The same evidence E can lead to different actions depending on mode: in Sattva, E->B_S->investigate carefully; in Rajas, E->B_R->act/acquire immediately; in Tamas, E->B_T->ignore/suspend/block. Refines the earlier 'kernel always busy determining right and wrong' into: the kernel continuously evaluates the epistemic condition of its current state and determines which transitions are admissible under its current operational mode; a kernel may legitimately decide DO NOTHING because evidence is insufficient, and that itself is a Buddhi decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Guṇa mode is NOT another knowledge dimension ... Guṇa mode = a control/state variable governing how the kernel operates on knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Central hypothesis: Guna mode is NOT another knowledge dimension (i.e. not a sixth axis of Sigma); rather Guna mode = a control/state variable governing how the kernel operates on knowledge -- assessed as potentially much cleaner than adding another dimension to Sigma=(A,S,R,V,C). Proposes next research direction: derive a formal Kernel Operator Algebra from the combined Chapters 6-17 model with Buddhi as discriminator and Sattva/Rajas/Tamas as candidate operational modes, without canonizing Gita terminology.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Can S,R,T be defined without relying on Sanskrit theology? ... Is mode another axis, or is it a control variable over the axes?
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses a 10-question research checklist for the Mode-Conditioned Epistemic State Machine hypothesis: can S,R,T be defined without Sanskrit theology; can each mode be given measurable properties; are modes mutually exclusive, overlapping, or mixtures; can a kernel transition between modes; does every operator have a mode-dependent admissibility condition; can a Tamas-like state be detected computationally; can Buddhi be represented as an actual decision function; does this improve the existing Sigma=(A,S,R,V,C) model; is mode another axis or a control variable over the axes; can the resulting algebra be independently derived from KnowledgeOS requirements (marked as the crucial distinction).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Is "epistemic quality" actually a sixth dimension? ... If those five dimensions already capture the relevant distinctions, then Q\notin\Sigma
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a concrete falsifiability test for whether guna/quality is a sixth Sigma dimension: check each existing axis against the candidate quality distinctions -- Acquisition (was knowledge acquired via identifiable observation), State (is epistemic state appropriately represented), Relation (are relationships correctly represented), Verification/Validation (is evidence sufficient), Context (is interpretation appropriate to context). If the five axes already capture the relevant distinctions, then Q notin Sigma (quality is a derived property); if they cannot, that is evidence for a missing dimension -- explicitly framed as the mathematical discipline wanted, before adding a sixth axis.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \operatorname{Distortion}(K_t)\rightarrow 0 ... M may be a derived property of (K,B,Z,\delta,\Sigma,C)
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects Moksha=maximum knowledge and Moksha=|K|->infinity; proposes instead Moksha ~ a limiting condition of epistemic purification, potentially Distortion(K_t)->0, explicitly a research hypothesis not an established theorem. Proposes candidate minimal kernel M=(K,B,Z,delta,Sigma) and states the current mathematical/DDD expectation: mode M={Sattva,Rajas,Tamas} may be a DERIVED property of (K,B,Z,delta,Sigma,C) rather than an additional primitive component -- explicitly framed as the kind of result wanted from the Gita programme (force every proposed concept through typing, independence, falsification, minimality, DDD boundaries). Proposes composed transition K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,x_t,B_t,M_t,C_t) as a hypothesis pending this determination.

a_rows_sample.anchor: S,R,T=\text{different modes of operation} ... Rajas \rightarrow useful acquisition ... Sattva \rightarrow incorrect conclusion
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit correction against a crude reading: NOT Sattva=good knowledge, Rajas=bad knowledge, Tamas=bad knowledge. Instead S,R,T = different modes of operation (operational tendencies, not truth labels); the quality of resulting knowledge is evaluated separately. Concrete counterexamples: Rajas -> useful acquisition is possible; Sattva -> incorrect conclusion is possible if underlying evidence/model is defective; Tamas can produce a legitimate stop (insufficient evidence -> do not act).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge State \neq Kernel State ... A kernel can contain excellent knowledge while operating in a poor mode.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit separation: Knowledge State K_t answers 'what does the system currently represent/know', Kernel State (fraktur K)_t = (K_t,M_t,B_t,Z_t,Pi_t) answers 'in what condition is the system currently processing that knowledge'. K_t != (fraktur K)_t: a kernel can contain excellent knowledge while operating in a poor mode, or hold incomplete knowledge with excellent discrimination/qualification behaviour -- assessed as very important for the Sattva/Rajas/Tamas model. Candidate kernel transition: (fraktur K)_t --Buddhi--> o_t --Purify--> (fraktur K)_{t+1}. Final consolidated formula: K_{t+1}=Purify(Execute(Buddhi(K_t,O_t,C_t))). Concluding principle: the Kernel is not the Knowledge; the Kernel is the smallest active unit that operates on Knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Neither branch is free. The flag is not lifted — it is converted from a vague caution into a two-branch question with named costs.
a_rows_sample.statement: Sharpens the Guna flag (open since REFINED-STEP-286 sec4, which required Guna to declare a scale type before being opened, touching the untyped Threshold/theta gap) into a two-branch fork P1': Branch 1, G_t derived from Sigma (e.g. mode=goodness when support is strong) -- the theta/scale-type gap returns, since a derivation rule over S's ordinal bands is exactly what sec4 flagged; Branch 2, G_t independent of Sigma -- a new state component with no carrier, and K_t=(Sigma_t,G_t,...) becomes another open-ended tuple that 258.35 warns against. Neither branch is free; sec4's gate still binds since neither branch declares a scale type. Contrasts with external_research mapping Guna->Sigma directly, which artifact 19's E2 finding already showed produces a type error.

a_rows_sample.anchor: o_t = \Omega_{G_t} \left( B_t,K_t,Z_t \right)
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the guna mode as selecting an operator POLICY, not merely a descriptive label: o_t = Omega_{G_t}(B_t,K_t,Z_t), giving Tamas mode o=Ignore; Rajas mode o=Search->Act->Search; Sattva mode o=Discriminate->Qualify->(Act or Stop) -- illustrated on identical K_t and O_t across modes, giving 'different modes of mind -> different operators/behaviour' a formal shape.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Buddhi(K_t,Z_t,M_t) \rightarrow D_t ... Unrecognized ignorance
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends Buddhi to include the operating mode: Buddhi(K_t,Z_t,M_t)->D_t, giving 'the same Knowledge State can produce different processing trajectories depending on the kernel's operating mode' as a testable hypothesis. Tamas failure mode: kernel encounters Z_t not-empty but behaves as though Z_t=empty, producing unrecognized ignorance; Rajas failure mode: continuous action Action_1->Action_2->Action_3 without sufficient discrimination -- the kernel needs self-regulation, connecting Chapter 6's discipline material to kernel architecture rather than mere commentary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: M_t in {Sattva,Rajas,Tamas} ... best treated initially as operating regimes, not new knowledge primitives ... Sattva: clarity, coherence, balance ... Rajas: activity, change, competition ... Tamas: inertia, ignorance, obscuration ... classified Guna as a quality/state heuristic rather than automatically putting it into the kernel.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gunas -> kernel operating modes, M_t in {Sattva, Rajas, Tamas}, best treated initially as operating regimes rather than new knowledge primitives: Sattva (clarity, coherence, balance, discrimination, reliable evaluation), Rajas (activity, change, competition, action pressure, rapid transformation), Tamas (inertia, ignorance, obscuration, corruption, failure to discriminate). Earlier research is noted to have deliberately classified Guna as a quality/state heuristic rather than putting it directly into the kernel, and that caution is preserved here.

a_rows_sample.anchor: B_{Sattva}(K) ... clear discrimination ... B_{Rajas}(K) ... action-biased interpretation ... B_{Tamas}(K) ... failure to recognize relevant evidence ... Decision = f(K,B,M,Gamma) rather than Decision = f(K) ... a major conceptual expansion of the Kernel model.
a_rows_sample.statement: The same knowledge state K can behave differently under different operating modes: B_Sattva(K) may yield clear discrimination, B_Rajas(K) an action-biased interpretation, B_Tamas(K) a failure to recognize relevant evidence -- yielding Decision = f(K,B,M,Gamma) rather than Decision = f(K), described as a major conceptual expansion of the Kernel model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: M_t in {Sattva,Rajas,Tamas} as modes of Kernel operation, not as permanent identities ... O_t = f(M_t,B_t,C_t) ... M_t -> M_{t+1} independently from K_t -> K_{t+1} ... Knowledge state and Kernel mode are different state dimensions ... high knowledge + poor mode ... little knowledge + high discrimination ... These are not equivalent.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gunas modeled as Kernel operation modes (not permanent identities), M_t in {Sattva, Rajas, Tamas}, giving O_t = f(M_t,B_t,C_t) -- the same candidate operation can behave differently under different modes. Proposes an independent mode state machine M_t -> M_{t+1} running alongside the knowledge state machine K_t -> K_{t+1}: knowledge state and Kernel mode are different state dimensions, so 'high knowledge + poor mode' and 'little knowledge + high discrimination' are not equivalent conditions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G_t in {Sattva,Rajas,Tamas} ... B_{G_t}: K_t -> D_t ... mode-dependent operators, rather than treating the three Guṇas as static labels.
a_rows_sample.statement: Models Sattva/Rajas/Tamas as G_t in {Sattva,Rajas,Tamas} sitting above the eight primitives, with mode-dependent Buddhi B_{G_t}: K_t -> D_t (Sattva: clarity/discrimination/consistency/evidence/balanced judgement; Rajas: activity/change/pursuit/intervention/rapid transformation; Tamas: inertia/ignorance/unresolved contradiction/refusal to inspect) -- emphasized as giving mode-dependent operators rather than static labels.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G_t in {Sattva,Rajas,Tamas} ... B_G: K -> Op* where Op* is the set of admissible operations ... B_Sattva -> {verify, qualify, reconcile, discriminate} ... B_Rajas -> {act, transform, pursue, propagate} ... B_Tamas -> {defer, retain, expose uncertainty} ... These are hypotheses, not yet canonical operations. The mathematical operator itself remains well-defined.
a_rows_sample.statement: Refines the Guna-mode hypothesis so mode influences which operators are admissible/preferred (B_G: K -> Op*, the set of admissible operations) without changing the operators' own mathematical definitions: B_Sattva -> {verify, qualify, reconcile, discriminate}; B_Rajas -> {act, transform, pursue, propagate}; B_Tamas -> {defer, retain, expose uncertainty} -- explicitly hypotheses, not yet canonical operations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G_t in {Sattva,Rajas,Tamas} ... O_i^(G) rather than assuming every operator behaves identically in every mode ... Tamas: concealment, stagnation, refusal to distinguish, failure to expose Zero ... Rajas: excessive transformation, action, acquisition, movement ... Sattva: discrimination, clarity, qualification, balanced transformation ... We should test whether these philosophical distinctions correspond to measurable operator behaviour. If not, they remain philosophical interpretation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the three Guna modes as operator-selection hypotheses to be experimentally tested: G_t in {Sattva,Rajas,Tamas} gives mode-specific operator variants O_i^(G) rather than uniform behavior, with hypothesized tendencies (Tamas: concealment/stagnation/refusal to distinguish/failure to expose Zero; Rajas: excessive transformation/action/acquisition/movement; Sattva: discrimination/clarity/qualification/balanced transformation), and an explicit falsifiability condition: test whether these philosophical distinctions correspond to measurable operator behaviour; if not, they remain philosophical interpretation only.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Remove G_t from the formal kernel state for now. G_t in {Sattva,Rajas,Tamas} and mode-dependent operators is an excellent experimental hypothesis. But it should sit in the PHILOSOPHICAL RESEARCH LAYER (Gītā -> Guṇa hypothesis -> measurable behavioural hypothesis -> experiment -> correspondence?) not in K_t=(...,G_t,...) until independently justified.
a_rows_sample.statement: Removes G_t (Guna) from the formal kernel state, relegating it to an explicit philosophical research layer (Gita -> Guna hypothesis -> measurable behavioural hypothesis -> experiment -> correspondence?) rather than embedding it directly in K_t=(...,G_t,...) until independently justified -- an excellent experimental hypothesis, but not yet a kernel-state component.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge existence \neq Knowledge availability
b_rows_sample.statement: From Gita 14.8-9 (Tamas covers/obscures knowledge rather than removing it; Sattva enables understanding): a proposition in K_t may exist yet the system may fail to retrieve, recognize, connect, discriminate, or act upon it. Hence Knowledge existence != Knowledge availability, and potentially Knowledge State = Content + Epistemic Accessibility -- assessed as more architecturally interesting than calling Tamas 'bad knowledge'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: High epistemic quality \not\Rightarrow epistemic freedom
b_rows_sample.statement: Correction to the earlier simple mapping 'Sattva=good knowledge': Gita 14.6 says Sattva illuminates and is associated with knowledge but also binds through attachment to happiness and knowledge (one can become proud of being knowledgeable and remain conditioned). Hence High epistemic quality does not imply epistemic freedom; a system can have excellent knowledge and still be epistemically trapped. Proposes distinguishing Knowledge Quality from Knowledge Attachment from Epistemic Freedom -- a stronger model than 'confidence = quality'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel operates under changing conditions ... Buddhi discriminates within those conditions
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly corrects a possible direction before it becomes architectural: if Kernel=Mind, the Gita does not suggest Kernel=Sattva. Instead the Kernel operates under changing conditions and Buddhi discriminates within them; the gunas describe the condition in which the kernel operates, not kernel components -- assessed as a cleaner DDD model. Formalizes G_t=(s_t,r_t,m_t) with s_t,r_t,m_t >= 0, optionally normalized s_t+r_t+m_t=1 giving G_t in the 2-simplex Delta^2 -- explicitly flagged as the researchers' own mathematical abstraction, not a Gita-derived numerical value or normalization (Gita -> qualitative dynamics; Mathematics -> possible quantitative representation).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Tamas \rightarrow poor discrimination \rightarrow bad operation \rightarrow worse knowledge state \rightarrow more Tamas
b_rows_sample.statement: Interprets 'without governance mind can become its own enemy' via a self-reinforcing epistemic degradation feedback loop: G_t -> B_t (Buddhi) -> o_t (chosen operation) -> K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,o_t) -> G_{t+1}, with worked examples Tamas->poor discrimination->bad operation->worse knowledge state->more Tamas, and Rajas->excessive activity->attachment to outcomes->more activity->more Rajas. Proposed as a possible mathematical model of self-reinforcing epistemic degradation, a candidate KnowledgeOS research direction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge \neq Knowledge Quality \neq Epistemic Freedom
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three previously conflated concepts: Knowledge ('what do we know?'), Knowledge Quality ('how clearly/reliably do we know it?'), and Epistemic Freedom ('are we conditioned by what we know?') -- the third layer described as the chapter's surprising contribution. Even Sattva (maximal knowledge/clarity) is not the final state: 14.20 describes freedom only after transcending all three modes, so epistemic quality != ultimate epistemic freedom.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Moksha \sim transcendence of the conditioning regime ... G_t\rightarrow G_{\perp}
b_rows_sample.statement: Revises the earlier Moksha formulation (Delta_t -> 0) given Chapter 14: Moksha != maximum K and Moksha != maximum Sattva; instead Moksha ~ transcendence of the conditioning regime, formalized as the research placeholder G_t -> G_perp meaning 'outside the three-mode conditioning model' -- explicitly flagged as a KnowledgeOS mathematical placeholder, not a Gita term. Proposes a purification trajectory Tamas-dominant -> (discrimination/clarification) -> Rajas-dominant -> (disciplined activity) -> Sattva-dominant -> (transcendence) -> Guna-atita, and a candidate epistemic-state model E_t=(K_t,Sigma_t,G_t,N_t) with N_t -Buddhi-> o_t and K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,o_t).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Is G_t actually an independent KnowledgeOS state variable, or merely a derived quality measure? ... Does the kernel itself have a formally definable "transcendence" operation
b_rows_sample.statement: Closes by keeping three questions explicitly open as candidates for the next mathematical/DDD research step: (1) is G_t an independent KnowledgeOS state variable or merely a derived quality measure; (2) can the three gunas be operationalized without importing arbitrary numerical semantics; (3) does the kernel have a formally definable 'transcendence' operation, or is transcendence only a philosophical limit concept. Reaffirms the Step 286 discipline: correspondence does not imply primitive does not imply canonical architecture -- the Gita generates research hypotheses; mathematics and DDD must test them.

b_rows_sample.anchor: we should not conclude Sattva=correct, Rajas=incorrect, Tamas=false ... high-quality knowledge \neq freedom
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit warning against oversimplifying Sattva=correct, Rajas=incorrect, Tamas=false; the philosophical model is subtler since even Sattva can bind through attachment to knowledge/happiness, giving high-quality knowledge != freedom -- a system could be highly knowledgeable yet epistemically constrained, assessed as one of the most interesting findings for KnowledgeOS and deserving serious investigation.

a_aliases: Guna as mode/state model, not metaphysics
b_aliases: Chapter 14 Three Modes of Material Nature reading

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'gita-guna-mode-conditioned-state-machine-hypothesis' POSSIBLY relates to 'hpa-gita-chapter14-guna-conditioning-regime-theory' (batch B0054). Note: Reformulates guna (Sattva/Rajas/Tamas) explicitly as a MODE/STATE model (not Gita metaphysics): K_t=(X_t,M_t) with M_t in {S,R,T} a control/state variable governing which kernel operators are admissible (O_S, O_R, O_T subset O), rather than a fourth Sigma dimension. Gives mode-specific operator sets (O_S={Observe,Compare,Discriminate,Corroborate,Qualify,Resolve,Validate}; O_R={Search,Acquire,Transform,Investigate,Generate,Execute}; O_T={DetectBlock,ExposeUnknown,Suspend,Flag,Invalidate,RequestEvidence}), a mode-sensitive Buddhi discriminator B_t:(E_t,K_t,M_t)->{accept,reject,investigate,suspend,transform} (same evidence yields different actions per mode), and a Tamas->Zero->Buddhi->Sattva mode-transition hypothesis. Explicitly distinguishes this from the earlier per-chapter guna-conditioning-regime object by treating mode as a control variable rather than a fourth Sigma dimension, and poses a 10-question research checklist (can S/R/T be defined without theology, can modes be detected computationally, is mode another axis or a control variable over axes, etc).

explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'gita-guna-mode-conditioned-state-machine-hypothesis' POSSIBLY relates to 'hpa-gita-chapter14-guna-conditioning-regime-theory' (batch B0055). Note: The Guna-as-kernel-operating-mode hypothesis, first proposed in B0054 and substantially extended in B0055 (mode-dependent Buddhi, an independent mode state machine, later reframed as a falsifiable experimental control variable).

a_rows_sample.anchor: False \neq Unknown \neq Unqualified
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three epistemic outcomes that must not be conflated: False (evidence contradicts p, p->R); Unknown (insufficient evidence, p->Z, i.e. Zero); Unqualified (evidence exists but the system cannot yet establish it satisfies required criteria, p->Q). Zero given a precise role: B(x)=G means 'insufficient knowledge to determine this' distinct from B(x)=R ('rejected') and B(x)=U ('evidence does not determine the result'). Proposed as potentially fundamental to the KnowledgeOS epistemic kernel.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Qualify(x)\rightarrow \{Qualified,\ Unqualified,\ Undetermined,\ Terminus\}
a_rows_sample.statement: Refines Qualify beyond a binary Qualified=True/False into Qualify(x)->{Qualified, Unqualified, Undetermined, Terminus}, connecting to the Cavell insight (justification may legitimately terminate). Qualify != prove everything; Qualify = determine whether the available basis is sufficient for the intended epistemic act; the correct result is sometimes Terminus rather than another investigation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Claim Strength \leq Evidence Strength
a_rows_sample.statement: From the divine-vs-destructive qualities discussion, proposes an 'epistemic restraint' operator: the kernel must ask not only 'what can I conclude' but 'what am I permitted to conclude from what I have', giving the candidate invariant Claim Strength <= Evidence Strength -- e.g. E(x)=weak must not produce C(x)=certain without an additional legitimate transformation. Proposed as a powerful candidate KnowledgeOS assurance rule.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge growth ... Knowledge expansion ... Knowledge purification ... These are not equivalent.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly rejects Purification=increase-in-dimensions-and-values as the canonical mathematical definition (confidence 0.95->0.55 can represent improvement if the original confidence was unjustified): Purification != monotonic increase; P(K_t,K_{t+1}) = improvement in epistemic quality, with quality itself still needing formal definition. Distinguishes three non-equivalent concepts: Knowledge growth (K_t->K_{t+1}, a state change occurs); Knowledge expansion (dim(K_{t+1})>dim(K_t), new dimensions represented); Knowledge purification (P(K_t,K_{t+1})=true, epistemic quality improves) -- more information does not imply better knowledge, and knowledge expansion != knowledge purification, assessed as an important theoretical safeguard. Also reformulates purification against Sigma as Sigma_t --B,Q,delta--> Sigma_{t+1} with P(Sigma_t,Sigma_{t+1}) rather than a scalar purity score, given Step 287's problem with total ordering.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Accepted(K) \cap Rejected(K) = \varnothing ... Unknown(K)\not\equiv Rejected(K) ... Unqualified(K)\not\equiv Unknown(K)
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a serious candidate kernel invariant: a KnowledgeOS kernel must preserve the distinction between what is established, what is rejected, and what remains epistemically unresolved, formalized as Accepted(K) cap Rejected(K) = empty-set, Unknown(K) not-equiv Rejected(K), and Unqualified(K) not-equiv Unknown(K) -- assessed as more promising formal properties than trying to encode the Gita directly. Also gives four-way kernel decomposition: kernel primitives {Represent, Discriminate, Qualify, DetectGap, Transform}; kernel state K_t; kernel control properties {Restraint, Consistency, Provenance, Uncertainty}; external governance {Authority, Policy, Authorization, Action} -- explicitly warning that Authority must not be placed inside Buddhi merely because Buddhi can determine what appears right, preserving the Steps 285-287 architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_{t+1} = \delta \left( Q \left( B \left( M(O_t,K_t) \right) \right), K_t \right)
a_rows_sample.statement: Consolidated candidate kernel tuple K=(K_t,M,B,Q,Z,delta) with status column (K_t established corpus concept; M Manas-like representation, philosophical hypothesis; B Buddhi/discrimination, strong hypothesis; Q qualification, existing unresolved architecture gap; Z explicit epistemic boundary/gap, strong Zero correspondence; delta state transition, existing formal direction, commit case still incomplete), yielding one central candidate kernel equation K_{t+1} = delta(Q(B(M(O_t,K_t))), K_t) -- explicitly candidate only, but assessed as testable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Should Buddhi be idempotent? ... Can B(x)=Accept later become B(x)=Reject after new evidence?
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a Kernel Algebra Research programme testing candidate operator set O_K={Represent,Discriminate,Qualify,DetectGap,Accept,Reject,Suspend,Revise,Transform} against 12 questions: which are genuinely distinct; which are compositions of others; which are state transitions vs observations; which require provenance; which require authority; which operate on K_t vs Sigma; which are already covered by the 8 primitives; which introduce genuinely new primitives; can the kernel operate without Action/Policy/Event as the verification lane claims; can Qualify be total/partial or must have a legitimate terminus; what algebraic properties Buddhi must satisfy (e.g. is B idempotent, B(B(x))=B(x); is discrimination monotonic; can B(x)=Accept later become B(x)=Reject after new evidence, requiring revision not simple classification). Frames the deepest question as: how does a kernel transform K_t into K_{t+1} without corrupting epistemic truth -- proposed as where the next major theoretical breakthrough is likely, rather than adding more Sanskrit terminology.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Unqualified is NEW — the basis was insufficient to admit it ... A fourth missingness mode beyond M1–M3
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms three [H] distinctions from S2244: T1 False != Unknown != Unqualified, with Unqualified assessed as genuinely NEW -- a fourth missingness mode beyond the corpus's existing M1-M3 (MNAR) modes, and Qualify's negative outcome; T2 growth (K_t->K_{t+1}) != expansion (dim K_{t+1}>dim K_t) != purification, using artifact 21's dimensional structure D_t and reinforcing negative constraint C8 (purification != monotonic accumulation); T3 Manas and Buddhi must not be collapsed, and Buddhi is non-Boolean (B(x) notin {true,false}) -- assessed as a sixth rival decision-codomain shape, reinforcing Step 291 sec12's point that a procedure answering 'Unknown' is total without deciding.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge quality depends not only on what K_t contains, ... but also on how the kernel transforms K_t.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes daivi/asuri as two classes of epistemic OPERATING BEHAVIOUR, not people-types: daivi-like kernel behaviour (truthfulness, clarity, self-control, non-deception, discipline, fearlessness examining reality, absence of destructive attachment, willingness to acknowledge what is not known, responsible action) vs asuri-like kernel behaviour (distortion, arrogance, false certainty, uncontrolled desire, attachment to a preferred result, denial, rationalization, destructive action, inability to recognize error). Conclusion: Knowledge quality depends not only on what K_t contains, but also on how the kernel transforms K_t.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero is the kernel's ability to represent the boundary between knowledge and non-knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: A dangerous kernel is not merely one that contains wrong information; it is one that cannot recognize that something is wrong: epistemic danger = error + failure of discrimination. An even worse condition, false certainty, occurs when the kernel believes unknown=known -- nearly the exact opposite of the Zero principle. Reframes Zero: not merely absence of knowledge, but the kernel's ability to represent the boundary between knowledge and non-knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence\rightarrow Discrimination\rightarrow Qualification\rightarrow Knowledge ... Desire\rightarrow Selection\rightarrow Rationalization\rightarrow False Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a kernel pathology model: a healthy kernel performs K_t+E_t --Buddhi--> K_{t+1} while preserving uncertainty and contradictions (pipeline Evidence->Discrimination->Qualification->Knowledge); a pathological kernel instead performs K_t+E_t --bias--> K'_{t+1}, selectively accepting confirming information (pipeline Desire->Selection->Rationalization->False Knowledge). Proposed as an important candidate KnowledgeOS research hypothesis distinguishing the two transformation modes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: confidence: 0.9\rightarrow0.4 could actually represent epistemic improvement ... Purification \neq monotonic increase of every metric
b_rows_sample.statement: Sharpens the non-monotonicity of purification with a concrete numeric example: confidence going from 0.9 to 0.4 could represent epistemic improvement if new evidence shows the previous certainty was unjustified. Hence Purification != monotonic increase of every metric; Purification = progress toward a better-qualified epistemic state. Proposes P(K_t,E_t,B_t)=K_{t+1} performing: remove unsupported claims, resolve contradictions, separate observation from interpretation, identify missing evidence, reduce unjustified certainty, preserve provenance, incorporate valid new evidence, identify new dimensions. Also defines a transformation-quality functional Q_B(K_t,K_{t+1}) assessing whether a transition reduces contradiction, reduces unsupported assertions, makes uncertainty explicit, improves provenance, increases justified knowledge, detects hidden gaps, or avoids introducing unsupported claims -- assessed as more promising than trying to mathematically encode 'good' and 'evil'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The kernel must not transform uncertainty into unjustified certainty. ... U(x)\rightarrow C(x) must require sufficient justification.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a candidate kernel invariant: the kernel must not transform uncertainty into unjustified certainty (U(x)->C(x) must require sufficient justification, otherwise the kernel is epistemically corrupting the state) -- proposed as a candidate for an eventual KnowledgeOS assurance property.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Buddhi = discrimination ... Governance = legitimate constraint/authority over action ... knows what is right \Rightarrow authorized to act.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reinforces (not replaces) the existing governance theory: a system that can discriminate but is not constrained in how it acts can still produce harmful transformations. Separates Buddhi=discrimination from Governance=legitimate constraint/authority over action, explicitly warning against the fallacy 'knows what is right => authorized to act', consistent with the existing principles Guidance != Authority and 'mechanism records authority; it does not grant authority'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal K_{\text{kernel}} = (K_t,\;B_t,\;Z_t,\;Q_t,\;\delta_t)
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate kernel tuple K_kernel=(K_t,B_t,Z_t,Q_t,delta_t) [current knowledge state, Buddhi discrimination/transformation capability, Zero explicit epistemic boundary/gap detection, qualification state/justification boundary, state transition], with O_t --Qualify--> K_t externally and K_t --B_t--> K_{t+1} -- explicitly not yet canonical, the strongest candidate architecture emerging from the philosophical analysis so far. Reframes the research question from 'what is the KnowledgeOS kernel' to 'what must a kernel be capable of doing to prevent knowledge from becoming distorted while transforming state over time', proposing Kernel = State + Discrimination + Qualification + Boundary Detection + State Transformation, and a next step of deriving a minimal algebra of kernel operations (observe, discriminate, qualify, accept, reject, retain, revise, discover-gap, transform) tested against the eight primitives and five-axis Sigma.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'gita-refined-kernel-model-false-unknown-unqualified-triad' POSSIBLY relates to 'hpa-gita-chapter16-combined-quality-control-pathology-model' (batch B0054). Note: A deliberate model-refinement pause (explicitly before adding Chapter 17) consolidating the batch's Buddhi/Zero/Qualify/purification threads. Introduces the False != Unknown != Unqualified triad (p->R vs p->Z vs p->Q), refines Qualify to {Qualified,Unqualified,Undetermined,Terminus}, gives a restraint invariant Claim Strength <= Evidence Strength, a partition invariant set (Accepted(K) cap Rejected(K) = empty; Unknown(K) not-equiv Rejected(K); Unqualified(K) not-equiv Unknown(K)), a four-way kernel decomposition (primitives {Represent,Discriminate,Qualify,DetectGap,Transform}; state K_t; control properties {Restraint,Consistency,Provenance,Uncertainty}; external governance {Authority,Policy,Authorization,Action}), and a single central candidate kernel equation K_{t+1}=delta(Q(B(M(O_t,K_t))),K_t). Proposes a 12-question Kernel Algebra Research checklist including whether Buddhi is idempotent (B(B(x))=B(x)) and whether it can be non-monotonic under revision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the philosophical structure is that **Buddhi/intelligence must discriminate and govern the lower mental/sensory tendencies**
a_rows_sample.statement: Correction of a prior KnowledgeOS wording: the Gita does not literally say 'the mind is always busy determining what is right and wrong'; rather, in Gita 3.40-43 the philosophical structure is that Buddhi (intelligence) must discriminate and govern the lower mental/sensory tendencies (Senses < Mind < Intelligence/Buddhi < Self, concluding at 3.43 with instruction to use the higher faculty to control the lower forces).

a_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Observed activity} \neq \text{correct interpretation of activity}
a_rows_sample.statement: From Gita 4.17-18 (the intricacies of action are hard to understand; action-in-inaction/inaction-in-action paradox): observed activity is not equal to the correct interpretation of that activity, so the kernel cannot merely ask 'what happened?' but must also ask 'what does this mean?' and possibly 'was this the right action?'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The KnowledgeOS kernel is conceptually analogous to a mind whose discriminative faculty must continuously evaluate the current epistemic state and possible transformations of that state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Refinement of the prior hypothesis 'the KnowledgeOS kernel is always busy determining right and wrong' into: the KnowledgeOS kernel is conceptually analogous to a mind whose discriminative faculty must continuously evaluate the current epistemic state and possible transformations of that state, formalized as K_t --Buddhi--> {accept, reject, qualify, revise, defer}.

a_rows_sample.anchor: an ungoverned state-transition mechanism can repeatedly transform K_t in the wrong direction
a_rows_sample.statement: Interprets the idea that 'without governance, the mind/kernel can become its own enemy' as meaning an ungoverned state-transition mechanism can repeatedly transform K_t in the wrong direction, connecting the Buddhi/discrimination hypothesis to a governance-failure warning.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would therefore mark this as a **candidate R5/R6 hypothesis**, not canonical yet
a_rows_sample.statement: The Buddhi-governs/discriminates-rather-than-accumulates hypothesis is explicitly marked as a candidate R5/R6 hypothesis, not canonical; next test is to determine whether the function is independently derivable from the KnowledgeOS corpus (without the Gita lens) and whether 'right/wrong' should technically become 'valid/invalid', 'admissible/inadmissible', 'qualified/unqualified', or another precise DDD distinction. Explicit warning: moral vocabulary ('right/wrong') should not be imported into the kernel until the corresponding KnowledgeOS predicate is established.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel \neq Buddhi ... Kernel contains/hosts the operations of Buddhi
a_rows_sample.statement: Kernel != Buddhi; rather, the Kernel contains/hosts the operations of Buddhi. Translation table: Mind/Manas -> continuously changing internal processing/state (philosophical lens); Buddhi -> discrimination: distinguish/evaluate/decide (strong candidate); Jnana -> acquired/recognized knowing (theoretical); Kshetra -> the field/state being processed (theoretical); Kshetrajna -> knower/observer of the field (theoretical); Karma -> operation/action (candidate correspondence); Phala -> consequence/result (candidate correspondence); Dharma -> correctness/order per governing principles (candidate correspondence); Sankalpa -> commitment/intention toward a decision (candidate); Viveka -> discrimination between alternatives (particularly relevant to Buddhi); Moksha -> limiting/transcendent epistemic condition (theoretical only).

a_rows_sample.anchor: B(K_t,x)\rightarrow d ... d \in \{\text{supported},\text{refuted},\text{contradictory},\text{unknown},\text{unqualified},\text{inadmissible}\}
a_rows_sample.statement: Mathematical correction to 'the kernel should always be busy determining right and wrong': right/wrong should not initially be binary. Buddhi should implement a discrimination function B(K_t,x) -> d with d in {supported, refuted, contradictory, unknown, unqualified, inadmissible}, not a Boolean truth oracle. Hence Buddhi = epistemic discrimination, not Buddhi = truth; the kernel does not create truth, it evaluates what can legitimately be concluded from its current state and evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel \neq K_t ... The kernel is the **persistent processing mechanism**, whereas K_t is the **current epistemic state**
a_rows_sample.statement: Kernel != K_t: since K_t != K_{t+1} (knowledge state changes with time), the Kernel is not any particular knowledge state; the Kernel is the persistent processing mechanism operating on successive knowledge states, analogous to Mind != one particular thought.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_{t+1}=F(K_t,\;O_t,\;B_t) ... A defective B_t can therefore systematically produce defective future states.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reinterprets 'the mind can become its own enemy': under the philosophical lens the danger is not the kernel disappearing but the kernel's discrimination becoming misdirected, corrupted, or dominated by an invalid internal process (bad qualification -> bad discrimination -> bad decision -> K_{t+1} -> future reasoning built on bad state), i.e. the kernel becomes its own enemy through epistemic feedback. Formalized as K_{t+1}=F(K_t,O_t,B_t) where B_t is the Buddhi/discrimination operation; a defective B_t can systematically produce defective future states.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Philosophical correspondence \not\Rightarrow primitive
a_rows_sample.statement: DDD discipline (following Steps 285-287): do not yet create 'Buddhi' as a domain object or primitive. Ask instead whether the KnowledgeOS kernel already contains a necessary capability whose philosophical abstraction is best described as Buddhi -- if so the Gita is naming an existing architectural property, not inventing one. Required pipeline: Gita -> hypothesis -> existing KnowledgeOS requirement -> formal operation -> independent derivation -> architecture. Reframes the research question from 'Is Buddhi a KnowledgeOS primitive?' to 'Does KnowledgeOS necessarily require a discrimination capability that operates over its changing epistemic state, and does Buddhi provide a useful philosophical model for that capability?'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal B: (K_t,O_t,E_t,C_t) \rightarrow D_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes B:(K_t,O_t,E_t,C_t)->D_t (discrimination/decision result), enumerating what B must do: distinguish, compare, validate, detect contradiction, assess evidence, qualify, reject, accept, defer, update the knowledge state, preserve provenance, determine what remains unknown. Central hypothesis: KnowledgeOS Kernel ~philosophically~ Mind; Buddhi ~philosophically~ Kernel's discrimination capability; K_t = changing Knowledge State; K (calligraphic) = Knowledge Space. Four-level picture: Knowledge Space K -> Knowledge State K_t -> KnowledgeOS Kernel -> Buddhi -> epistemic operations -> K_{t+1}. Explicitly marked as hypothesis pending testing against actual Gita passages and the existing KnowledgeOS corpus, not yet canonical.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Buddhi is a critical control point
a_rows_sample.statement: The kernel/mind 'enemy' danger is not only bad data but can arise from: (1) incomplete observation, (2) overwhelming observation, (3) incorrect interpretation, (4) defective discrimination, (5) incorrect decision, (6) state transition based on that decision -- pipeline O_t -> B_t -> D_t -> K_{t+1}. Hence Buddhi is a critical control point in the kernel architecture. Observation != Understanding and Understanding != Discrimination.

a_rows_sample.anchor: B(x)= \begin{cases}\text{admissible}\\\text{inadmissible}\\\text{unknown}\\\text{conflicting}\\\text{requires qualification}\end{cases}
a_rows_sample.statement: Buddhi modelled as B: E -> D (epistemic alternatives to distinguishable outcomes) with candidate codomain {admissible, inadmissible, unknown, conflicting, requires qualification}; the 'requires qualification' category connects directly to the unresolved Qualify/G1 problem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel operates under changing conditions ... Buddhi discriminates within those conditions
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly corrects a possible direction before it becomes architectural: if Kernel=Mind, the Gita does not suggest Kernel=Sattva. Instead the Kernel operates under changing conditions and Buddhi discriminates within them; the gunas describe the condition in which the kernel operates, not kernel components -- assessed as a cleaner DDD model. Formalizes G_t=(s_t,r_t,m_t) with s_t,r_t,m_t >= 0, optionally normalized s_t+r_t+m_t=1 giving G_t in the 2-simplex Delta^2 -- explicitly flagged as the researchers' own mathematical abstraction, not a Gita-derived numerical value or normalization (Gita -> qualitative dynamics; Mathematics -> possible quantitative representation).

a_rows_sample.anchor: we should not say Buddhi=\delta ... B_t(K_t,o_t,G_t,R_t) \rightarrow d_t ... \delta(K_t,d_t)=K_{t+1}
a_rows_sample.statement: Careful mathematical separation: Buddhi != delta. B_t is Evaluation/Discrimination, delta is State Transition. Formalized as B_t(K_t,o_t,G_t,R_t) -> d_t, followed by delta(K_t,d_t)=K_{t+1}. Candidate (non-canonical) Buddhi decision codomain d_t in {Accept, Reject, Qualify, Defer, Transform, Escalate}; notes the philosophical lens does not solve the unresolved Qualify problem but may explain why qualification is a distinct act of discrimination.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Buddhi \neq unrestricted inference ... Governance becomes structurally distinct from the kernel
a_rows_sample.statement: Explains the 'kernel can become its own enemy' worry: if the kernel transforms its own state without constraints (K_t ->F-> K_{t+1} ->F-> K_{t+2}...), it can create self-reinforcing errors, circular reasoning, confirmation loops, unjustified certainty, loss of provenance, and contradiction propagation. Therefore Buddhi != unrestricted inference; it needs constraints, and this is where Governance becomes structurally distinct from the kernel. Also refines Buddhi's codomain away from TRUE/FALSE toward {supported, contradicted, unknown, insufficient evidence, conflicting}, framed as more compatible with the Zero/uncertainty/qualification theory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \delta = \text{discrimination operator}
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly states delta = discrimination operator (i.e. Buddhi approx delta), proposing delta:X->D where D={accept,reject,uncertain,contradictory,needs evidence,needs qualification} -- an architectural hypothesis, not canonical. This directly conflicts with the same-session file S2233's explicit warning 'we should not say Buddhi=delta' (Buddhi is Evaluation/Discrimination B_t, delta is State Transition, with B_t(...)->d_t feeding a SEPARATE delta(K_t,d_t)=K_{t+1}); neither file cites or reconciles the other's position on whether Buddhi and delta are the same function or two composed functions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: B: K\times O\times C \rightarrow \{\text{Permit},\text{Reject},\text{Defer}\}
a_rows_sample.statement: From the divine quality dama (self-control): the kernel should not execute every available operation. Proposes a gatekeeper: B:KxOxC->{Permit,Reject,Defer} evaluated BEFORE delta(K,o)=K' executes (rather than delta:KxO->K' being unconditional), so delta(K,o) is applied only if permitted -- assessed as a very serious candidate for the formal kernel.

a_rows_sample.anchor: B_t: (E_t,K_t,M_t) \rightarrow \{\text{accept},\text{reject},\text{investigate},\text{suspend},\text{transform}\} ... DO NOTHING ... is itself a Buddhi decision.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Buddhi as mode-sensitive: B_t:(E_t,K_t,M_t)->{accept,reject,investigate,suspend,transform}. The same evidence E can lead to different actions depending on mode: in Sattva, E->B_S->investigate carefully; in Rajas, E->B_R->act/acquire immediately; in Tamas, E->B_T->ignore/suspend/block. Refines the earlier 'kernel always busy determining right and wrong' into: the kernel continuously evaluates the epistemic condition of its current state and determines which transitions are admissible under its current operational mode; a kernel may legitimately decide DO NOTHING because evidence is insufficient, and that itself is a Buddhi decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Having an evaluation mechanism \neq having correct discrimination ... B_t \neq \text{truth oracle}
a_rows_sample.statement: From Chapter 18's distinction between understanding that correctly distinguishes proper/improper action and understanding that fails to (per the modes): having an evaluation mechanism != having correct discrimination. Therefore B_t != truth oracle; Buddhi is an epistemic discriminator, not an omniscient truth machine -- assessed as much more compatible with KnowledgeOS than treating Buddhi as infallible.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel = the smallest unit capable of epistemic state transition
b_rows_sample.statement: Central hypothesis: KnowledgeOS Kernel = the smallest unit capable of epistemic state transition, not merely the smallest unit that stores knowledge. Kernel = (State, Transition Capability): the state is what the kernel currently holds, the transition capability determines what can legitimately happen to that state. Gita lens (analytical, not DDD names): Mind -> evolving epistemic state, Buddhi -> discriminative capability, Karma -> action/transition, Phala -> resulting state/outcome.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K = (K_t,\Omega_K)
b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate kernel K=(K_t,Omega_K) with 11 candidate operations, each carrying a load-bearing distinction: (1) Observe(O_t) with O_t != K_t (observation is not automatically knowledge, preserving W->O->E and Qualify); (2) Discriminate(K_t,O_t)->{d_1..d_n} = the Buddhi operation, meaning 'distinguish', not yet 'decide truth'; (3) Qualify(x,E,C,t,Pi), the G1 unresolved operation, whose result may be {admit,reject,defer,qualify} rather than binary {true,false}; (4) Incorporate: K_{t+1}=Incorporate(K_t,p), a state transformation not simple insertion; (5) Reject(K_t,p) with Reject != Prove False (a proposition can be rejected as insufficiently qualified without being established false); (6) Contradict: recognizing p _|_ q via the corpus's Relation primitive; (7) Revise(K_t,p,E) for evidence-conflicting knowledge, with explicit warning not to import AGM revision theory merely because it exists, per Step 287; (8) Supersede: p_1 supersedes p_2 while preserving lineage; (9) Recall(K_t,h)/Remember distinguishing currently-known from historically-known, with K_t != H_K (history of states/transitions); (10) Withdraw(p): K_t -> K_{t+1} with withdraw != delete history (the historical fact of having held it may remain, important for auditability); (11) Act/Transform(a), external to the epistemic state per Command != Transformation != Result and Step 285's finding that Action, Event, Policy were external to the verification projection.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \delta:(K_t,O_t,C_t)\rightarrow K_{t+1} ... only when the transition satisfies the kernel's invariants
b_rows_sample.statement: The kernel should not be an unrestricted machine: reject delta:KxO->K as an unrestricted transition function; instead delta:(K_t,O_t,C_t)->K_{t+1} only when the transition satisfies the kernel's invariants. Kernel operation = candidate transition + discrimination + qualification + state transition, subject to constraints. Motivated by the 'mind can become its own enemy' observation made mathematically useful.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \Omega_K = \{\operatorname{Discriminate},\operatorname{Qualify},\operatorname{Transition}\}
b_rows_sample.statement: Speculative minimal-algebra hypothesis: Omega_K = {Discriminate, Qualify, Transition} might suffice, with Accept/Reject/Revise/Supersede as specialized transition types -- explicitly flagged 'we should not assume this minimality', proposed as a mathematical question to attack rather than an established result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel: the smallest bounded epistemic mechanism that maintains a time-indexed knowledge state and can discriminate and perform legitimate transitions of that state under the applicable constraints.
b_rows_sample.statement: Provisional formal kernel definition: K = (K_t, Omega_K, I) where K_t = current knowledge state, Omega_K = permitted kernel operations, I = kernel invariants; K_t --omega in Omega_K--> K_{t+1} only if I(K_t,omega,K_{t+1})=true. Gita gives only the philosophical lens Mind~Kernel, Buddhi~discriminative capability; the mathematical/DDD investigation determines the actual kernel. Key research hypothesis: Kernel != Knowledge Store, but potentially Kernel = Epistemic State + Discrimination + Legitimate State Transition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 291 — KnowledgeOS Kernel and Operation Algebra
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes next research step 'Step 291 -- KnowledgeOS Kernel and Operation Algebra' with 12 questions: minimal kernel definition; whether K_t is the kernel state or the kernel holds additional state; minimal Omega_K; which operations are genuinely epistemic vs belong outside (Governance, Authority, Action, Replay); whether Discriminate is primitive or composite; what Qualify consumes/produces; whether every legitimate K_t->K_{t+1} transition can be classified; determinism of the transition; which invariants must never be violated; whether the operation algebra can be proven minimal; which parts are independently derivable vs merely Gita-correspondences.

b_rows_sample.anchor: B(K_t,x)\rightarrow d ... d \in \{\text{supported},\text{refuted},\text{contradictory},\text{unknown},\text{unqualified},\text{inadmissible}\}
b_rows_sample.statement: Mathematical correction to 'the kernel should always be busy determining right and wrong': right/wrong should not initially be binary. Buddhi should implement a discrimination function B(K_t,x) -> d with d in {supported, refuted, contradictory, unknown, unqualified, inadmissible}, not a Boolean truth oracle. Hence Buddhi = epistemic discrimination, not Buddhi = truth; the kernel does not create truth, it evaluates what can legitimately be concluded from its current state and evidence.

b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes B:(K_t,O_t,E_t,C_t)->D_t (discrimination/decision result), enumerating what B must do: distinguish, compare, validate, detect contradiction, assess evidence, qualify, reject, accept, defer, update the knowledge state, preserve provenance, determine what remains unknown. Explicitly marked as hypothesis pending testing against actual Gita passages and the existing KnowledgeOS corpus, not yet canonical.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal K \overset{\Omega}{\longrightarrow} O_t \overset{\mathcal B}{\longrightarrow} D_t \overset{\delta}{\longrightarrow} K_{t+1}
b_rows_sample.statement: The central kernel question evolves from 'what operations does the Kernel perform?' to 'what can a bounded KnowledgeOS Kernel legitimately know, observe, discriminate, and conclude about a knowledge space larger than its current state?'. Final research-model pipeline: K (Knowledge Space) --Omega (observation/projection)--> O_t (observation) --B (Buddhi/discrimination)--> D_t (discrimination result) --delta (state transition)--> K_{t+1} (new Knowledge State). Explicitly not yet canonical architecture; identifies convergence of existing open questions about Observation, Proposition, State, Event, Buddhi, Qualify, delta, and the five-axis Sigma.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Can the existing KnowledgeOS eight primitives and the five-axis \Sigma=(A,S,R,V,C) express the proposed Mind–Buddhi–Kernel behavior without introducing a new primitive?
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes pausing philosophical interpretation after Chapter 12 to test mathematically: can the existing eight primitives and five-axis Sigma=(A,S,R,V,C) express the proposed Mind-Buddhi-Kernel behavior without a new primitive? Specifically test whether Buddhi = an operation over existing primitives, Mind = a state/orientation over existing primitives, and Kernel = (K_t, operations, invariants, transition rules) -- framed as the first real mathematical/DDD test of the 'KnowledgeOS Kernel = Mind' interpretation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: E_d(K_t)=K_{t+1} ... R_d(K_t)=K_{t+1} ... C(K_t,o)=K_{t+1} ... X(K_t)\rightarrow \text{conflict-qualified state} ... Z(K_t)\rightarrow G_t
b_rows_sample.statement: Six candidate (not canonical) operators: E (Expansion) discovers a new relevant dimension d not-in D_t, now in D_{t+1}; R_d (Refinement) improves an existing dimension, v_t(d) prec_d v_{t+1}(d); C (Correction) changes an existing value because new evidence shows the previous state was wrong -- explicitly Purification != monotonic accumulation, since a purified state may contain less due to removed erroneous knowledge; X (Contradiction resolution) given p and not-p, the kernel must not arbitrarily select one, producing a conflict-qualified state until Buddhi/evidence/qualification can discriminate; Q (Qualification), the unresolved G1 operator, determining sufficient justification for the intended epistemic purpose, reframed via the recent Cavell-derived reconsideration so purification can mean correctly recognizing a gap cannot currently be resolved rather than resolving it; Z (Zero detection) detects epistemic absence, Z(K_t)->G_t (recognized gaps), with G_t transformable via E,R,C,Q into G_{t+1} -- the system becomes more purified partly by knowing more accurately what it does not know.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \{\operatorname{Discriminate},\ \operatorname{Qualify},\ \operatorname{Transition}\}\ \cong\ \{\equiv,\ G1,\ \delta\}
b_rows_sample.statement: The philosophically-proposed minimal kernel algebra Omega_K={Discriminate,Qualify,Transition} (from S2219, the kernel-definition-from-evidence-maths-DDD file) maps exactly onto the formal lane's independently-established blockers: Discriminate = the equality/distinguishability relation equiv (the unique minimal cycle cut per Steps 289/291, unique over both graph universes); Qualify = the corpus's own Qualify:Observation x Policy -> Evidence, i.e. G1, named/typed/no body, irreducible; Transition = K_t --delta--> K_{t+1}, i.e. delta, commit case unspecifiable, executed as K1 is K0. This is a genuine independent arrival (derived from 'what must a kernel be able to do', not from the dependency graph, 261.23, or the G1 register) but a NEGATIVE convergence: it solves none of the three, and is a restatement of the blocker set, not a kernel. Registered as new gap G-90 (derived, raises confidence, closes nothing). Sharp consequence stated: any minimal kernel algebra containing Qualify inherits G1 -- since Qualify is the one irreducible gap, a genuinely minimal kernel cannot be closed without closing G1.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A correctly shaped triple whose three components are EXACTLY the three open items. It states the problem well. It populates nothing.
b_rows_sample.statement: Tests the proposed kernel shape K=(K_t,Omega_K,I) slot by slot against the formal lane: K_t (the state) is OPEN (per Step 285; 258.35 says it may not be a tuple at all); Omega_K (permitted operations) is OPEN (N-4 mandatory membership open, 0 of 22 operations has a body/identity/ratification per 291); I (invariants) has 0 of 7 established (per REFINED-STEP-287-INVARIANTS), and I is downstream of equiv in 261.30's chain. Conclusion: a correctly-shaped triple whose three components are exactly the three open items -- a well-posed problem statement, not progress toward closure; must not be mistaken for populating the kernel (per 291's 'shape -> content requires a derivation, and none exists').

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Perceive / receive ... 5. Orient
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes the KnowledgeOS kernel may need five fundamentally different classes of work: (1) Perceive/receive O_t; (2) Represent O_t->K_t; (3) Discriminate B_t(K_t,O_t)->d_t; (4) Transform delta(K_t,d_t)->K_{t+1}; (5) Orient rho_t(K_t,Omega). The fifth (Orient) is said to become much more visible once Chapter 11 (the horizon Omega) is added to the model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \Omega = \{ Observe,\; Discriminate,\; Relate,\; Validate,\; Qualify,\; Transform,\; Reject,\; Accept,\; Revise \}
b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate (non-canonical) operator family from Chapters 10-15 combined: Omega={Observe, Discriminate, Relate, Validate, Qualify, Transform, Reject, Accept, Revise}, with Buddhi approx delta as the mechanism selecting/executing several of these, e.g. delta(Observation,Context)->Decision and delta(K_t,E_t)->K_{t+1}, connecting to the unresolved Qualify problem from Steps 285-287.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal K \neq K_t \neq \mathcal M
b_rows_sample.statement: Formal first principle: K (Knowledge Space, potentially unbounded) != K_t (Knowledge State at time t, what the system currently represents) != M (KnowledgeOS Kernel, the smallest persistent computational unit that evaluates and transforms knowledge states). The Gita's language helps interpret M as Mind, but the software kernel is not literally the philosophical mind. Defines M = the smallest unit capable of epistemic state transition, i.e. capable of K_t->K_{t+1} under some evidence/observation/proposition/event/operation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z:\boxed{K_t\rightarrow G_t} ... \delta: \boxed{(K_t,G_t,E_t,C_t)\rightarrow D_t} ... \tau: \boxed{(K_t,D_t)\rightarrow K_{t+1}}
b_rows_sample.statement: Full typed operator pipeline: Z:K_t->G_t (gap/boundary discovery, internal inspection); delta:(K_t,G_t,E_t,C_t)->D_t (discrimination/Buddhi, taking gaps, evidence, and context); tau:(K_t,D_t)->K_{t+1} (transition/transformation). Composition tau o delta o Z is type-correct given matching interfaces; for external input f_x(K_t)=tau(K_t,delta(x,E,C)); for internally discovered gaps f_Z(K_t)=tau(K_t,delta(Z(K_t))). The kernel therefore performs two fundamentally different activities: external epistemic input (x->delta) and internal epistemic inspection (K_t--Z-->G_t).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Level 0 — Primitive kernel mechanisms ... Level 1 — epistemic operations ... Level 2 — higher-order processes
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a three-level operator hierarchy to address the concern that not all candidate operators should be primitive: Level 0 primitives {delta,Z,tau} (smallest candidates); Level 1 epistemic operations built from primitives (Observe, Compare, Validate, Qualify, Revise, Accept, Reject), e.g. Accept(x)=tau(K_t,delta(x,E,C)=accepted), Reject(x)=tau(K_t,delta(x,E,C)=rejected); Level 2 higher-order processes as compositions (Purification, Learning, Investigation, Knowledge evolution), P = O_1 o O_2 o ... o O_n, assessed as important for DDD (avoiding conflating primitive operations with their compositions).

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal M=(Q,\mathbb O,\delta,\tau,\mathbb I)
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes formalizing the kernel as a state machine M=(Q,O,delta,tau,I) where Q=kernel control states (renamed from S to avoid collision with Sigma's S axis), O=kernel operations, delta=discrimination function, tau=transition function, I=invariants. Also proposes the kernel invariant M != K_t must hold (otherwise K_t->K_{t+1} would mean the kernel becomes a different object every time); formalized as Identity(M_t)=Identity(M_{t+1}) while K_t != K_{t+1} is permitted -- 'persistent kernel identity + mutable epistemic state' proposed as a fundamental candidate architectural invariant, worth testing against the corpus.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Qualify: X\rightarrow \{Qualified,\;Unqualified,\;Terminated\} ... Kernel determines the admissible epistemic status of a state transition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Refines Qualify (still classified G1) via the Cavell insight (justification may legitimately terminate rather than being infinitely extended) into Qualify:X->{Qualified, Unqualified, Terminated}, rather than assuming qualification is always a total true/false decision -- candidate only. Reframes the kernel's deeper job away from 'determine truth' toward 'Kernel determines the admissible epistemic status of a state transition', assessed as much closer to what the corpus actually supports; enumerates the kernel's operative questions (what do we have, what evidence supports it, what is missing, what conflicts, what relationship exists, what can legitimately be concluded, where must qualification stop, what state transition is admissible).

a_rows_sample.anchor: INV-ATTR-2/G-2: separation is Declared, NOT attestable. No mechanism can establish who performed an act; assurance rests entirely on where the human starts the session.
a_rows_sample.statement: Finding F-4: role separation between producer, verifier, and approver is Declared, not attestable (INV-ATTR-2/G-2); no mechanism in the estate can establish who actually performed an act, so assurance rests entirely on where the human starts a session -- a capability described as C-5, separation attestation, with no owner today.

a_rows_sample.anchor: this is the first recorded instance of it failing in the FALSE-BAR direction. INV-ATTR-2 anticipated that a process could wrongly claim independence; this event shows the same mechanism can make a process wrongly claim to be barred
a_rows_sample.statement: INV-ATTR-2 ('separation is declared, not attestable') is extended by observed evidence to a second failure direction: not only can a process wrongly claim independence (the failure the invariant was framed against), but the same unverified-self-declaration property can make a process wrongly claim to BE barred, harming an assignment rather than assurance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The platform cannot attest a specified session execution. identity binding must NOT be placed inside C-10's authoritative state, because C-10 cannot establish it. It is C-5-shaped
a_rows_sample.statement: The sharpest finding in the D3 prep: a C-10 receipt's binding to a specific session execution can never be stronger than what INV-ATTR-1/INV-ATTR-2 permit (self-declared, not attested), so identity binding cannot be placed inside C-10's authoritative state -- it is C-5-shaped, and C-5 owns no attestation record either.

a_rows_sample.anchor: One prohibition, three surfaces: an unresolved status may never be laundered into a resolved one.
a_rows_sample.statement: A single cross-cutting prohibition is observed recurring in three independent places in the estate's governance (independence classification, C-5 separation dimensions, D4.1 compensating controls, later a fourth at D4.3 M4): an unresolved epistemic status must never be laundered into a resolved one -- recorded as an observation bearing on, but distinct from, the canonical unifying-invariant candidate.

a_rows_sample.statement: Full process-disclosure practice: a producing process discloses its own prior participation and interest in the outcome (having authored the canonical analysis, D5, and prior governance registrations) and binds itself out of later verifying or accepting its own work (R-34/P-2).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Article I.1 ... Article I.2 ... Article I.3 -- Mathematics describes, never defines.
b_rows_sample.statement: Chapter I, the Constitutional Identity: Article I.1 the character (KnowledgeOS governs how knowledge is created/justified/transformed/challenged/evolved while preserving identity/context/evidence/authority/reasoning/uncertainty/agency/historical evolution); Article I.2 the three clause refinements (existence, reasoning, identity) are constitutionally absorbed as phrasing refinements, not supersessions; Article I.3 the governing maxim 'Mathematics describes, never defines' -- topology, type theory, graphs, TMS, AGM, LLMs are mechanisms/explanatory lenses, never kernel law by virtue of being mathematical or computational.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONSTITUTIONAL KERNEL <- the eleven articles (PRESERVE) ... Engine Layer (GOVERN) ... Mechanisms (GOVERN) ... Representations (ENABLE) ... Implementation (ENABLE)
b_rows_sample.statement: Chapter III, the Kernel Boundary: a 5-tier diagram -- Constitutional Kernel (the 11 articles, PRESERVE) served by Engine Layer (validation engines, fallacy detection, debate pipeline, intent classification, verdict vocabulary, GOVERN), Mechanisms (epistemic-inquiry lifecycle, reasoning pipelines, GOVERN), Representations (evidence records, context tuples, epistemic state model, absence taxonomy, epistemic graph, typed encodings, ENABLE), and Implementation (storage, interfaces, systems, deliberately unconstrained, ENABLE). III.1 the kernel does not do the reasoning -- it states what must be preserved/never collapse; engines execute governed transformations realizing those constraints. III.2 no engine/mechanism/representation may violate an article -- evolution that violates an article is a corruption, not an evolution, subject to Chapter V. III.3 implementation is deliberately out of constitutional scope.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Graph = Representation. KnowledgeOS Theory = Epistemic Computation. ... Representation layer G=(V,E) ... Epistemic computation layer K_t, Q, E, S, R, Zero, Determination... Execution/governance layer Decision -> Authorization -> Action -> Observation. ... Representation -> Epistemic Comput
a_rows_sample.statement: Refines the Knowledge Graph / KnowledgeOS separation into a three-layer architecture: (1) Representation layer G=(V,E), asking what entities/relations/claims/evidence structures are represented; (2) Epistemic computation layer (K_t, Q, E, S, R, Zero, Determination, etc. -- KnowledgeOS theory proper), asking what may be inferred/challenged/determined/retained/revised/attributed; (3) Execution/governance layer (Decision->Authorization->Action->Observation), asking what may actually be done -- giving Representation->Epistemic Computation->Decision/Action rather than a graph-only system; proposes a representation relationship K_t-representation->G_t and potentially G_t-interpretation/reconstruction->K_t, with the exact mapping left as an open architectural research question; applies this to the Nexus example, concluding 'the graph represents the result; KnowledgeOS determines what the result means epistemically.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Graph: Represents entities, claims and relations. Zoom-in: Changes inquiry focus / traversal scope. Zero Lens: Tests what can be removed without violating the preservation contract. Evidence Assessment: Evaluates claims/relations. Determination: Determines what the inquiry supports. Zoom-o
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a 7-role architectural table distinguishing Knowledge Graph (entities/claims/relations), Zoom-in (inquiry focus/traversal scope), Zero Lens (removability under the preservation contract), Evidence Assessment (claim/relation evaluation), Determination (what the inquiry supports), Zoom-out (integrating the result back into broader context), and K_t (current epistemic state) as separate mechanisms with separate responsibilities, argued to be far more coherent than immediately making Zoom-in and Zoom-out kernel operators.
