a_rows_sample.anchor: We should not search for one universal scalar called "amount of knowledge." We should define a knowledge element mathematically and then quantify different properties of that element under an explicitly declared epistemic regime.
a_rows_sample.statement: Central conclusion: a knowledge element is e=(p,a,c,τ,r,E,D,σ) where p=proposition/content, a=participant, c=context+boundary+LoA, τ=temporal scope, r=epistemic/reasoning regime, E=evidence/input references, D=derivation/inferential structure, σ=current epistemic status (itself possibly multidimensional, not scalar). A knowledge state K_t^{a,R,C} is the set of such elements for a given participant/regime/context up to time t, supporting K_t^A≠K_t^B without different underlying realities. Not yet a Kernel schema, but a mathematical research model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K(e)=(L,P,U,T,I,X,S,M,C,G)
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a ten-dimensional Knowledge Measurement Vector K(e)=(L,P,U,T,I,X,S,M,C,G) — logical support, probabilistic support, unknownness, provenance/traceability, inferential relevance, conflict, stability, margin, scope coverage, explanatory/information gain — kept as separate dimensions, never collapsed into one scalar. A scalar Score(e)=Σw_i q_i(e) is allowed only when a specific purpose determines the weights (e.g. audit weights provenance heavily, troubleshooting weights explanatory gain, research weights uncertainty, governance weights authority+provenance+conflict); Pareto-frontier analysis is preferred over a weighted scalar because weighting can hide dimensions like 'high evidence, high conflict, high importance, low stability'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: L(p)= 1 if p belongs to every A_i; 0 if ¬p belongs to every A_i; ? otherwise
a_rows_sample.statement: Logical entailment status L(p) derived directly from ASP answer-set semantics (1 if p in every answer set, 0 if ¬p in every answer set, unresolved otherwise) — a genuinely mathematical quantity stronger than an LLM confidence score. A related but explicitly-labeled-as-proposed (not from the source book) model-support ratio S_model(p)=|{A_i:p∈A_i}|/n is flagged as a modelling choice, not automatically a probability, distinct from P-log's genuinely probabilistic P_R(p|KB).

a_rows_sample.anchor: U(e) ∈ {alternative, unrepresented, blocked-default, outside-scope, computationally-unresolved}
a_rows_sample.statement: Unknownness U(e) is proposed not as a Boolean but a classification (alternative / unrepresented / blocked-default / outside-scope / computationally-unresolved), with the exact taxonomy left empirical and countable for future statistical analysis.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Stability(p) = Pr[status(p) remains unchanged under relevant perturbation]. ... Margin(p) = |{K'∈N(K):p remains supported}| / |N(K)|
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes formal candidates for revision stability (Stability(p)=1-E[d_p(K,K')]/d_max, or Pr[status unchanged under relevant perturbation]) and epistemic margin (Margin(p)=|{K' in neighborhood N(K): p remains supported}|/|N(K)|), giving a mathematical form to the Williamson-derived knowledge-margin concept; notes margin requires defining what counts as a 'nearby' state, which is where topology/perturbation theory/statistics enter.

a_rows_sample.anchor: IG(E;H) = H(H)-H(H|E)
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes an information-theoretic explanatory-value/information-gain measure IG(E;H)=H(H)-H(H|E) over a hypothesis/explanation space H given evidence E, and AnswerGain(Q,A)=H(Hypotheses|Q)-H(Hypotheses|Q,A) as a candidate answer to 'how concrete is an answer to a question' — explicitly flagged as the document's own proposed statistical extension, not a claim from Gelfond & Kahl (who provide only the computational explanation framework).

a_rows_sample.anchor: We cannot quantify "how much of the infinite Knowledge Space we know." We can quantify: **coverage of a declared finite inquiry boundary.**
a_rows_sample.statement: Coverage(K,C)=|relevant elements represented/assessed|/|Ω_C| is only meaningful relative to a declared finite scope Ω_C; since the full Knowledge Space Ω is infinite, |K|/|Ω| is explicitly stated to be useless — coverage of a declared finite inquiry boundary is the defensible quantity, not coverage of the infinite space itself.

type_signature.domain: knowledge state K, declared scope C

a_rows_sample.anchor: ### External adequacy ... ### Predictive adequacy ... ### Refinement stability
a_rows_sample.statement: Since d(K,Ω) cannot be computed directly (Ω is not a finite reference set), proposes three orientation-toward-the-infinite-Knowledge-Space proxies: External adequacy (independent verification success), Predictive adequacy (Pr[prediction correct]), and Refinement stability (as scope C1⊂C2⊂C3 expands, does d(Projection(C1), Restriction(Projection(C2),C1))→0?) — called a candidate formalization of 'serve the nature of the Knowledge Space'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A. Representation measurements ... B. Epistemic measurements ... C. Task measurements
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three fundamentally different measurement families: Representation measurements (coverage, provenance, completeness, semantic consistency, traceability — how well is knowledge represented), Epistemic measurements (entailment, uncertainty, probability, conflict, stability, margin, entrenchment — how strong is the current epistemic position), Task measurements (answer resolution, prediction accuracy, explanation gain, diagnostic accuracy, planning success, decision utility — how useful is the knowledge) — described as much better than one 'knowledge score'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Store the substrate; compute the measure.
a_rows_sample.statement: Core architectural rule: 'Store the substrate; compute the measure' — a metric is an assessment of the preserved substrate, not a property permanently attached to the knowledge itself; the Kernel must not be contaminated with numbers like confidence=0.83, PageRank=0.67, entropy=1.42, stability=0.91 unless explicitly recorded as assessments produced by named regimes. Consistent with Gelfond & Kahl's representation/reasoning-algorithm separation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KS=(V,E,\tau,\Gamma,\Pi)
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes an overall model KS=(V,E,τ,Γ,Π) — typed knowledge-bearing entities V, typed relations E, temporal structure τ, preserved histories/provenance Γ, projection specifications Π — with Projection_{R,P,C,t}(KS)->K_t^{P,R,C} and a metric M_R(...)->R^n. Proposes a typed vertex vocabulary (Entity, Event, Observation, Proposition, Assertion, Commitment, Rule, Assumption, Evidence, Question, Explanation, InstitutionalStatus, KnowledgeAttribution) rather than one undifferentiated 'knowledge element', and a small universal relation vocabulary (represents, observed-from, asserted-by, supported-by, derived-from, implies, contradicts, qualifies, supersedes, questions, answers, explains, causes, counts-as, authorized-by, valid-at), noting not all relations are necessarily Kernel primitives.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A knowledge element is a context- and time-bounded epistemic unit consisting of a proposition or meaningful content attributed to a participant...
a_rows_sample.statement: Final working (not philosophically final) definitions: a knowledge element is a context/time-bounded epistemic unit (proposition/content attributed to a participant, with provenance, evidential basis, inferential/deontic relationships, assumptions, current epistemic assessment under a declared regime); a knowledge state is the evolving collection/relational configuration of such elements available at a point in time; the Knowledge Space is the unbounded space toward which finite states are oriented, which KnowledgeOS does not contain but preserves structures to reconstruct/compare finite projections of; the Kernel is the minimal preservation substrate for those projections and histories, with mathematical/statistical quantification belonging to external epistemic/analytical regimes. Recommends stopping the search for a single 'knowledge quantity' in favor of designing a Knowledge Measurement Vector + Knowledge State Distance + Projection Refinement test.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We must not combine coverage, evidence, confidence, stability and information gain simply because all happen to produce numbers.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extensive measurement requires associativity, ordering, monotonicity, and Archimedean conditions for f(a⊕b)=f(a)+f(b) to be legitimate — so a proposed EvidenceTotal=E1+E2+...+En is not automatically meaningful without first demonstrating the empirical operation supports additive measurement. Conjoint measurement gives conditions under which u(a,b)=u1(a)+u2(b) has meaning, so the multidimensional Knowledge Vector Q_K=(C,E,U,S,IG,...) may only be collapsed into Score(Q_K) if the empirical preference/ordering structure supports an additive conjoint representation — otherwise keep the vector.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the real ownership map is the space map
b_rows_sample.statement: Where ownership DOES change, the boundary is a SPACE, not a viewpoint: platform (DA) -> EKP (nab.raj.sharma) -> product (the producing track). This claim is downgraded from finding to hypothesis in REV 2 because it was observed on one platform instance only; generalizing it as an architectural property requires KnowledgeOS applied elsewhere (the second-adopter gate).

b_rows_sample.anchor: U-VO-4 | Whether space-ownership (platform/EKP/product) is the platform's REAL context map
b_rows_sample.statement: Unknown U-VO-4: whether space-ownership (platform/EKP/product) is the platform's real context map — the strongest candidate reading of Finding 1 — deliberately left as a strategic-DDD question for humans, not answered by the author.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R-4 | Space —generates→ Projection —attested→ authoritative | HIGH
b_rows_sample.statement: Relationship R-4: Space generates Projection, attested to become authoritative. External support: CQRS (read models rebuildable, non-authoritative) plus audit/signature practice and data-product certification. No challenge — the corrected form IS the standard model. Confidence: HIGH.

b_rows_sample.statement: Relationship R-9: a Knowledge Space has a declared boundary and spaces nest (deployment = nested space). External support: bounded contexts (CANONICAL), data-mesh domains (boundary+owner). Challenge: nesting is less standardized than bounding. Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH overall (boundary HIGH, nesting MEDIUM).

b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge Space as declared boundary + owner + constitution is supported by bounded contexts (Evans), data-mesh domain ownership, and SKOS concept schemes. Confidence: HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Canonical concept glossary — the 14 examined, plus 3 the corpus forces in
b_rows_sample.statement: A 17-row glossary assigns each term (KnowledgeOS, PKS, Engineering Knowledge, Engineering Capability, Engineering Method, Engineering Governance, Engineering Runtime, Runtime Adapter, Engineering Evidence, Engineering Ontology, Documentation Ontology L-A, Platform Ontology L-B, Product Ontology L-C, Knowledge Graph, Engineering Kernel, Knowledge Space, Design Policy DP-n, Execution Asset AST-nnn) one meaning, owner, protected invariant, place, and verdict (KEEP/REJECTED-MERGED/SPLIT/CANDIDATE). Success criterion: every major engineering term gets one meaning, one owner, one place.

b_rows_sample.anchor: REV 2 — review 2026-08-03 (1420), three amendments annotated, none rewritten
b_rows_sample.statement: Three amendments: (1) the 'nine kinds' are held as candidate archetypes, not frozen primitives, until MM-1 resolves whether KIND is itself a dimension; (2) CONTAINER is demoted from CONFIRMED to CANDIDATE, since its distinguishing edge ('generates Projections') is observed in only one space (the EKP) and nesting is unevidenced (H-3); (3) PURPOSE is flagged for its own investigation (U-MM-4, waits on D-5).

b_rows_sample.statement: Three additional kinds were repeatedly found by the passes but missing from the A-G candidate list: PURPOSE (mission/vision, found twice in the Relationship Ontology), CONTAINER (Knowledge Space — declared boundary, nesting), and PROJECTION (derived, operating in production).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Classification — every gap from the projection ... G-1..G-5
b_rows_sample.statement: Five gaps classified by category (Structural/Behavioral/Evolutionary) and cause: G-1 (I-4/ATTESTS/PROJECTION inert-vs-attested) is EVOLUTIONARY, caused by a missing lifecycle, belongs to LIFECYCLE. G-2 (SPECIALIZES, Engineering Knowledge -> product knowledge) is EVOLUTIONARY, a missing relationship, belongs to ONTOLOGY. G-3 (external authority/CONSTRAINS) is BEHAVIORAL, a missing relationship (obligation != ownership), belongs to GOVERNANCE. G-4 (PRODUCT vs DEPLOYMENT/INSTANTIATES) is STRUCTURAL but dissolves: a deployment is a nested Knowledge Space, so it belongs to ONTOLOGY as resolved, no new concept. G-5 (Runtime Adapter disappeared in both new domains) is STRUCTURAL but is a confirmation of Hexagonal behaving correctly, not a failure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: G-4 answers H-3 — the nesting question — using evidence rather than preference: Knowledge Spaces NEST, and a deployment is the nested case
b_rows_sample.statement: H-3 (the nesting question) is answered by G-4: Knowledge Spaces nest, and a deployment is the nested case. No new concept was introduced; the ontology already explained the evidence, which is the test the commission set.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 2. CANDIDATE — supported by evidence, awaiting ruling or more evidence (K-1..K-15)
b_rows_sample.statement: Fifteen candidate concerns, each citing its supporting commission and what it waits on: K-1 dimensional-with-archetypes meta-model; K-2 the archetype set (strong: DOMAIN/PROCESS/CAPABILITY/KNOWLEDGE/ARTIFACT/RUNTIME ASSET/PROJECTION; weaker: CONTAINER; weakest: PURPOSE); K-3 the four partial orders (authority, production, realization, containment); K-4 11 invariant relationships vs 8 implementation choices; K-5 DP-n as capability anchor; K-6 Knowledge Space = declared boundary+owner+constitution; K-7 authority = provenance x standing, four progression kinds; K-8 the strategic domain set PD-1/2/3/5; K-9 viewpoints as presentation; K-10 decision-readiness as the platform's product; K-11 FREEZE/RETIRE as insufficiency evidence; K-12 PKS extends context-engineering with governance; K-13 the canon-track reference artifacts themselves; K-14 the mission is enacted via 8 artifacts; K-15 ownership splits (candidate-unowned=ladder working, operating-unowned=defect, sole instance Runtime Adapter).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 3. HYPOTHESIS — plausible, insufficient evidence (H-1..H-9)
b_rows_sample.statement: Nine hypotheses with evidence state: H-1 the space map is the platform's real ownership/context map (n=1, downgraded); H-2 GOVERNANCE as a fifth viewpoint (asset found, framing undecided); H-3 PURPOSE more fundamental than CONTAINER (n=0); H-4 KnowledgeOS as a 'Knowledge Architecture Platform' (n=1); H-5 'generates -> PKS', the loop's head edge and the platform's distinctive bet (n=0 inside and outside); H-6 capability may read across a space boundary, never own (n=1 capability); H-7 space nesting (unevidenced); H-8 DOMAIN's decision-silence is dormant not permanent (untestable at n=1); H-9 EVIDENCE-STATUS/OPERATIONAL-STATE as meta-model dimensions (proposed, undocketed).

b_rows_sample.anchor: ANNOTATED 2026-08-02 — THREE CORRECTIONS ... LEVEL MIXING — my third instance of that error class
b_rows_sample.statement: Three annotated corrections (recorded in KnowledgeOS_Relationship_Ontology.md): (1) section 2's six concepts are not siblings but four ontological layers (Purpose/Mission, Platform/Capability+Knowledge, Representation/Artifact, Application/PKS+Product) listed as one set — a third instance of level mixing; (2) PKS is a CONTAINER, not a layer below ARTIFACT — a PKS contains artifacts, and KNOWLEDGE SPACE is admitted as the container concept, defined by a declared boundary (scope.include), not a folder; (3) the document itself conflates two levels — section 1 (dimensions) is a meta-model, section 2 (concepts) is an ontology, both named rather than the whole renamed. The chain in section 2 is completed by naming DP-n (DESIGN POLICY) as the anchor stopping capabilities from floating, observable in the Capability Catalog's 1:1 CAP->DP binding.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Concepts × kind × owner (C-1..C-13)
b_rows_sample.statement: Thirteen concepts classified by kind and owner: C-1 VISION (purpose, sponsor); C-2 MISSION (purpose, sponsor, enacted-unratified); C-3 ENGINEERING STRATEGY (purpose->governance bridge, ARB/sponsor); C-4 ENGINEERING PRINCIPLE (governance, DA/sponsor+ARB/platform depending on series); C-5 DESIGN POLICY DP-n (governance, DA via Catalog); C-6 ENGINEERING CAPABILITY (capability, its DP-n not a domain); C-7 ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE (knowledge, DA/sponsor+ARB); C-8 ENGINEERING ARTIFACT (representation, its owner field); C-9 KNOWLEDGE SPACE (container, the space's own owner); C-10 PKS (container, product team); C-11 PRODUCT (application, product team); C-12 RUNTIME ADAPTER (runtime element, no owner found); C-13 PROJECTION (projection, the generating space).

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-9 KNOWLEDGE SPACE — admitted, and the evidence is a boundary, not a folder ... A Knowledge Space is not a folder. It is a DECLARED SCOPE with an owner and a governing constitution
b_rows_sample.statement: KNOWLEDGE SPACE is admitted, evidenced by: knowledge-schema.yaml's declared scope.include; three registered documentation roots (knowledgeos, pks, publicdigit); ES-005.1's three concerns (Product, Platform, Runtime mount); the EKP having its own constitution and owner. A Knowledge Space is a declared scope with an owner and a governing constitution, not a folder — which is why the '13% coverage' question was a scope decision, not a bug.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The relationship model — the commission's seven questions ... contains = a container relation · references = a pointer · generates = produces a new instance · depends on = cannot be understood without
b_rows_sample.statement: A full relationship table across all thirteen concepts, using four typed relations (contains = container relation, references = a pointer, generates = produces a new instance, depends on = cannot be understood without). Notable entries: KNOWLEDGE SPACE may contain artifacts and other knowledge spaces, generates PROJECTIONS; PKS may contain product artifacts but never reusable Method, references Engineering Knowledge, generates Product Projections; ARTIFACT is a leaf (contains nothing) but depends on the Knowledge it represents; KNOWLEDGE generates nothing, being represented rather than generative.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Missing concepts — recorded as hypotheses, not admitted (H-1..H-4)
b_rows_sample.statement: Four candidate concepts recorded as hypotheses, none admitted: H-1 'I-12', a Capability may read across a space boundary but never own what it reads (n=1 capability, needs a second cross-boundary reader); H-2 Engineering Domain as owner of Capabilities (no artifact binds a CAP to a PD; DP-n already fills the slot); H-3 Knowledge Space nesting, does the EKP contain the PKS or sit beside it (containment vs adjacency unevidenced); H-4 whether OPERATIONAL-STATE attaches to the Artifact or the Knowledge it carries (would change I-1's granularity).

b_rows_sample.anchor: RO-2 | Are Knowledge Spaces nested or adjacent?
b_rows_sample.statement: RO-2: are Knowledge Spaces nested or adjacent (H-3) — authority: ARB.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The three challenges — accepted, and one is settled by my own evidence rules ... CONTAINER demoted CONFIRMED → CANDIDATE ... my own admission rule decides it, not deference
b_rows_sample.statement: Three reviewer challenges: (1) 'Archetype' replaces 'nine kinds' until MM-1, since 'archetype' already exists in the corpus (RQ-002) so the rename mints nothing — a ubiquitous-language decision, decided with governance (MM-1), not unilaterally; (2) CONTAINER is demoted from CONFIRMED to CANDIDATE by the author's own admission rule: 'Containers generate Projections' is observed in exactly one space (the EKP's knowledge-graph.php), n=1, and nesting is unevidenced (H-3) — the settling test is a second generating space (confirms) or a capability-plus-scope reduction (refutes); (3) PURPOSE, possibly more fundamental than Container, is flagged not resolved, since the mission is enacted and unratified (D-5 pending), and deepening PURPOSE before ratification would model ahead of the domain expert — recorded as hypothesis U-ONT-2, n=0.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What exists instead ... FOUR DISTINCT PARTIAL ORDERS, one per relationship type: AUTHORITY · PRODUCTION · REALIZATION · CONTAINMENT
b_rows_sample.statement: Four evidenced partial orders replace the refuted single stack: AUTHORITY (who justifies whom) PURPOSE->STRATEGY->PRINCIPLE->DP-n->CAPABILITY; PRODUCTION (who produces whom) PROCESS->Knowledge/Artifacts/Evidence, CAPABILITY->Evidence, CONTAINER->Projection (n=1); REALIZATION (concept -> executable/persistent form) KNOWLEDGE->ARTIFACT (I-1), CAPABILITY->RUNTIME ASSET (R-7, SC-6 gap); CONTAINMENT (what moves together) CONTAINER contains Artifacts (contains other spaces? H-3 open). The intuition underneath the stack survives: relations are directional, with DOMAIN/KNOWLEDGE conceptual and RUNTIME/ARTIFACT realized; but 'which is above' is only answerable per relation, not for the stack as a whole.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 3 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: **`[EXP]` The theory is executable and its distinctions survive — with one exception, and the exception is structural rather than incidental.** All 10 scenario families (A–J) execute the full lifecycle. 19 of 20 properties hold across the deterministic suite. **`P11` (factivity) fails, and it fails necessarily.**
a_rows_sample.statement: States the overall simulation result: the theory is executable and its distinctions survive across all 10 scenario families and 19 of 20 tested properties, with the single exception of P11 (factivity), which fails not incidentally but necessarily -- a structural finding, not a bug.

a_rows_sample.anchor: (1) Knows(a,p,c,t) -> True(p,c,t) DEF-1, factivity (2) K_{a,c,t} = Gamma(E_{a,c,t}, Q_t, C_t, EC_t) v1.1 attribution ... **These are jointly unsatisfiable for any total `Γ` that attributes anything.** Witness: two worlds whose truths differ ... produce a **bit-identical epistemic state** ... Since Γ is a function of E, it returns an identical K. The attribution is true in one world and false in the other.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proves by explicit witness that v1.0's DEF-1 factivity (Knows(a,p,c,t)=>True(p,c,t)) and the v1.1 attribution equation K=Gamma(E,Q,C,EC) are jointly unsatisfiable for any total Gamma that attributes anything: two worlds with different ground truth (os=RHEL9.8 vs RHEL8.6) produce a bit-identical epistemic state E (verified by fingerprint over observations/evidence/interpretations/assessments/determinations/hypotheses/rejections), so any function of E alone must return the identical attribution K regardless of which world is actually true -- Gamma's domain structurally excludes truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Policy sweep — the only `Γ` that escapes is the one that attributes nothing: justified-unique yes/yes, justified-any yes/yes, none no/no. Randomized confirmation over 10 000 trials: **420 factivity violations**, conditional failure rate **0.1237** given that an attribution was made. Diagnosis: **414 / 665** violations when a source the admission policy rated reliable reported a false value, **0 / 2 607** otherwise.
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms the factivity impossibility across every tested attribution policy (justified-unique and justified-any both violate factivity whenever they attribute anything; only the trivial policy 'attribute nothing' escapes), and via a 10,000-trial randomized run: 420 factivity violations, a 0.1237 conditional failure rate given an attribution was made, with the failure concentrated entirely (414 of 665, vs 0 of 2,607) in cases where a policy-trusted reliable source reported a false value that the agent had no signal to distinguish from a true one.

a_rows_sample.anchor: S3 anti-fabrication ... S4 unresolved competition ... S5 target-relative assessment ... S6 evidence dependence ... S7/S8 explicit standards & models ... S10 inquiry-relative adequacy ... S11 history ... S14 no information creation ... S15 decision lane ... S17 unknown taxonomy
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms ten major theory-level successes against the protocol's success criteria: anti-fabrication (incomplete evidence never invents a value), unresolved competition (Reject(H1) never becomes Accept(H2), determination stays set-valued), target-relative evidence weighting (never a bare scalar strength), correct evidence dependence handling (dependence-aware run drops a duplicate that the naive run double-counts), standards and models producing genuinely different determinations from identical evidence/reality, inquiry-relative adequacy (same K_t, different I_t/Delta_t/Zero across two inquiries), history preservation (K_1!=K_2 with stable identity and recoverable K_1), no unsupported information creation (an injected unsupported conclusion is caught), a fully separable four-stage decision lane (Determination->Proposal->Decision->Authorization->Action), and a non-collapsing four-way unknown taxonomy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **What object is `K_t`, if it cannot be factive?** ... **`Adequate` and `Zero` are extensionally identical** — `DEF-20` and `DEF-22` both reduce to Delta_t = empty. One does no independent work. ... **Semantic equivalence remains circular** ... **Revision without retraction produces permanent underdetermination**
a_rows_sample.statement: Names four major unresolved questions the experiment surfaced: what K_t even is if it cannot be factive; DEF-20 (Adequate) and DEF-22 (Zero) are extensionally identical (both reduce to Delta_t=empty), meaning one definition does no independent work; semantic equivalence remains circular since behaviour is compared only under an experimenter-chosen projection; and Revision without retraction produces permanent underdetermination since the theory models only one of the corpus's seven revision verbs.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The factivity result is the first genuinely **negative structural theorem** the programme has produced about its own definitions, and it is *sharp*: it does not say the theory is wrong, it says **exactly two of its clauses cannot both hold**, and it names the three repairs available
a_rows_sample.statement: Names the factivity finding the programme's first genuinely negative structural theorem about its own definitions: sharp in that it does not claim the theory is wrong overall, only that exactly two specific clauses (DEF-1 factivity and the v1.1 attribution equation) cannot both hold, with three named repairs available elsewhere in the artifact set.

a_rows_sample.anchor: `definitional = true` marks a property whose oracle necessarily restates a theory definition: its pass is a **logical consequence of the implementation**, not independent evidence. ... P3 Rejection != Acceptance **yes** -- Reject removes one member by construction. P4 Gap != Zero ... **yes** -- Zero := (Delta=empty) is DEF-22.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes a definitional-vs-independent classification discipline for every tested property, flagging P3 (Rejection != Acceptance, true by construction since Reject removes one member) and P4 (Gap != Zero, true by definition since DEF-22 literally defines Zero as Delta=empty) as definitional -- their passing is a logical consequence of the implementation, never independent evidence that the theory works.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **P11** Knowledge attribution respects factivity Knows(a,p,c,t) -> True(p,c,t) **no — the only fully oracle-independent property** ... Only **P11** is fully oracle-independent: its evaluator reads World.truth, which no agent transition can access (verified by static audit). Every other property compares the agent's state against itself under a definition supplied by the theory.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies P11 (factivity) as the ONLY fully oracle-independent property among all 20 tested: its evaluator reads World.truth, structurally inaccessible to any agent transition, whereas every other property merely compares the agent's own state against itself under a theory-supplied definition -- explaining why P11's failure carries far more evidentiary weight than any pass among the other 19.

a_rows_sample.anchor: `P7` is marked non-definitional but is **partly circular** — see `I-circularity-register.md` CIRC-5.
a_rows_sample.statement: Flags P7 (representation equality is not required for semantic equality) as partly circular despite being marked non-definitional, cross-referencing an unread-in-this-batch circularity register entry CIRC-5.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A Simple determination ... K is a *record with status, provenance, weight* — **not a copy of the observation**. B Incomplete evidence ... status=cannot-determine, A=empty, Zero=false, Delta!=empty, **nothing invented**. C Competing hypotheses ... A={RHEL9.8,RHEL8.6} underdetermined ... Reject(H1) did **not** become Accept(H2).
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports scenarios A-C executed results: A confirms Knowledge is a structured record (status/provenance/weight), not a copy of observation; B confirms incomplete evidence produces cannot-determine/empty-A/Zero-false/non-empty-Gap with nothing invented; C confirms Reject(H1) does not become Accept(H2), leaving the determination genuinely underdetermined between two surviving hypotheses.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D Different standards ... S-lenient -> **unique**; S-strict (corroboration) -> **cannot-determine**. Evidence and truth verified byte-identical across arms. ... E Different inquiries ... same K_t; I_1!=I_2; Delta_1=empty, Delta_2={r2}; Zero_1=true, Zero_2=false.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports scenario D (holding evidence and truth byte-identical while varying only the epistemic standard S^epi flips the determination from unique to cannot-determine, confirming standards do real work) and scenario E (a fixed E_t under two different inquiries produces identical K_t but different Ideal States, Gaps, and Zero values, confirming inquiry-relative adequacy).

a_rows_sample.anchor: F Conflicting evidence ... A={8081,8082} underdetermined — **not averaged**, conflict preserved, no attribution. G Dependent evidence ... dependence-aware: 1 assessment dropped ... corroboration requirement unmet. Naive: counts both. H Model mismatch ... M1: beta=1.852, R2=0.899, causal_status = not-identified; true effect 0. **No causal knowledge attributed**.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports scenario F (conflicting equal-reliability evidence is preserved as conflict, never averaged, and produces no attribution), G (a dependence-aware run correctly drops a derived duplicate and finds the corroboration requirement unmet, while a naive run incorrectly double-counts it), and H (a confounded model with excellent statistical fit, R^2=0.899, is correctly classified causal_status=not-identified against a true zero causal effect, so no causal knowledge is attributed despite the fit).

a_rows_sample.anchor: I Retrospective revision ... K_1!=K_2, identity stable, pre-revision determination stored in history. J Unobservable property ... classified **UNOBSERVABLE** — not observed-false, not probability zero, not a rejected hypothesis.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports scenario I (reality change plus revision produces K_1!=K_2 with stable identity and the pre-revision determination preserved in history) and J (a property with no channel at all is correctly classified UNOBSERVABLE, never conflated with observed-false, probability-zero, or a rejected hypothesis).

a_rows_sample.anchor: UNOBSERVED a channel exists, never queried ... UNINTERPRETED observation held, no semantic content assigned ... UNDERDETERMINED evidence present, |A_t|>1 ... UNOBSERVABLE no channel exists ... P13 confirms UNOBSERVABLE != UNDERDETERMINED in both the deterministic and randomized layers (guard active in 37.4% of 10 000 trials, 0 failures).
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms the four-way unknown taxonomy (Unobserved: channel exists but never queried; Uninterpreted: observation held with no assigned semantic content; Underdetermined: evidence present with |A_t|>1; Unobservable: no channel exists) did not collapse across both deterministic scenarios and the randomized layer, with P13 (Unobservable!=Underdetermined) confirmed active in 37.4% of 10,000 randomized trials with zero failures.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D is the only scenario that holds **reality, observation, evidence and inquiry fixed** and varies a single theory object. It therefore isolates `S^epi` cleanly, and it is the one place the experiment shows an epistemic standard doing real work rather than decorating the model.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies Scenario D as the methodologically strongest of the ten scenarios: the only one holding reality, observation, evidence, AND inquiry all fixed while varying a single theory object (S^epi), cleanly isolating epistemic standards and showing them doing real work rather than merely decorating the model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 26 types declared **before** execution. ... Evidence | Observation x Policy | admitted datum | Observation, Interpretation ... KnowledgeState | EpistemicState x Q x C x EC | K_t = Gamma(...) | EpistemicState, IdealState
a_rows_sample.statement: Presents the complete 26-type formal type table declared before execution (RealityState through Identity), each specified with its input types, carrier, and forbidden substitutions -- e.g. Evidence typed as Observation x Policy -> admitted datum, forbidden to substitute for Observation or Interpretation; KnowledgeState typed as EpistemicState x Q x C x EC -> K_t=Gamma(...), forbidden to substitute for EpistemicState or IdealState.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **`P`** Proposition (DEF-5) . Probability (DEF-18) . Preservation vector 𝒫 (§66) — **worst, 3-way** ... **`E`** Evidence (DEF-7) . EpistemicState E_t (v1.1) . Expectation ... `E` is the most dangerous: **the v1.1 correction reuses `E` for the epistemic state while `DEF-7` already uses it for Evidence** — and the correction's whole point is that those two must not be confused.
a_rows_sample.statement: Finds ten notation collisions across the v1.0/v1.1 theory's symbol vocabulary (worst: P used three ways for Proposition, Probability, and the Preservation vector), and flags the E collision as the most DANGEROUS: the v1.1 correction reuses E for EpistemicState while DEF-7 already uses E for Evidence -- precisely the two objects the v1.1 correction's entire point is to keep from being confused, an ironic self-undermining notation clash.

a_rows_sample.anchor: `[OPEN]` The theory should rename one of them; this experiment did not, in order to avoid silently changing the theory. ... No **type collision** was found: no two types share a carrier with interchangeable substitution.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly declines to silently rename the colliding E notation, preserving the theory's exact wording per the protocol's discipline and flagging it [OPEN] for the theory document itself to resolve; separately confirms zero genuine type collisions were found (no two declared types share a carrier with interchangeable substitution), distinguishing notation-symbol collisions from actual type-system collisions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **1. Instance-level, not reachability-level.** The prior lane (`KR-2026-09-01`) reasoned about *which carrier kinds are reachable*; its own `THM-9` then established `Reachability ≠ Adequacy`. This simulator therefore carries **content**: tokens, readings, weights, sources, provenance. Only that makes factivity, dependence, ambiguity and fabrication testable at all.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the first of two design decisions making the v1.1 simulation's results meaningful: unlike the prior KR-2026-09-01 kernel-reduction lane (which reasoned only about reachability of carrier kinds, whose own THM-9 established Reachability != Adequacy), this simulator carries actual instance-level CONTENT (tokens, readings, weights, sources, provenance) -- only this design choice makes factivity, dependence, ambiguity and fabrication testable at all.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **2. Oracle independence is enforced structurally.** `World.truth` is read by the **evaluator only**. A static audit greps every agent-side module for `.truth` and reports any hit as smuggling. Result: **zero hits**. This is what makes `P11` an empirical test rather than a definition — and, as it turns out, it is also *why* factivity fails.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the second design decision: oracle independence is enforced STRUCTURALLY, not by convention -- World.truth is read only by the evaluator, verified by a static audit greping every agent-side module for any access, with zero hits found -- this structural guarantee is precisely what makes P11 (factivity) an empirical test rather than a mere definitional restatement, and is also directly why factivity was found to fail (the agent genuinely has no path to truth).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Every corroboration-dependent conclusion in this programme rests on a component of a concept v1.2 declares OPEN. ... Dropping the source component collapses corroboration and flips every downstream result.
b_rows_sample.statement: Details result 5 (E4): dropping the observation model's source component collapses corroboration and flips determination/attribution/Zero, showing corroboration-dependent conclusions rest on a component the theory itself calls OPEN.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The v1.2 run reuses the entire v1.1 pipeline unchanged, and replaces only the evaluation layer ... any difference between the v1.1 and v1.2 results is attributable to the theory, not to the simulator.
b_rows_sample.statement: Describes the controlled-experiment design: the v1.1 pipeline (world, state, transitions) is reused byte-identical, so any difference between v1.1 and v1.2 results is attributable to the theory change, not the simulator.

b_rows_sample.anchor: E1 | Do the three Zero readings ever disagree? | Yes -- on the fully determined case. ... E5 | What kind of thing is Zero, of the seven v1.2 candidates? | 2 refuted, 1 partial, 4 surviving
b_rows_sample.statement: Tabulates the five formal experiments (E1 Zero-reading disagreement, E2 equality substitutability, E3 CE-1/CE-3 persistence, E4 OPEN-observation dependence, E5 which of seven Zero readings survive) with their one-line results.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The weakening was productive. v1.2 did not repair a single v1.1 failure -- but it made two of them better diagnosed, exposed one defect v1.1's phrasing had hidden (Zero's ambiguity), and gave the programme a vocabulary in which "we do not know" is a first-class result rather than a hedge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Delivers the comparison verdict: v1.2 repaired no v1.1 failure but improved diagnosis of two, exposed a hidden defect (Zero's ambiguity) v1.1's phrasing had concealed, and made 'unknown' a first-class result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: NOT TESTED -- and under v1.2, not testable. ... A kernel cannot be selected while its operation semantics are open, and E1 shows even the closure predicate itself is ambiguous. This is v1.2 behaving correctly, not a shortfall of the experiment.
b_rows_sample.statement: Delivers a stronger kernel-status verdict than v1.1: not merely untested but not-yet-testable under v1.2's own declared openness of operation semantics and closure predicate.

group_evidence.why_grouped: working_label token overlap Jaccard=0.57 (shared tokens: ['knowledgeos', 'simulation', 'theory', 'v1'])

a_rows_sample.anchor: This is an EXPERIMENT. Do NOT modify the canonical theory merely to make the simulation pass. Do NOT silently repair definitions. Do NOT introduce undocumented assumptions. Do NOT treat a successful simulation as proof of the theory. Do NOT treat a failed simulation as proof that the theory is false.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the protocol's foundational experimental discipline: the theory must never be silently repaired or modified merely to make the simulation pass, no undocumented assumptions may be introduced, and neither a successful nor a failed simulation may be treated as proof or disproof of the theory -- the purpose is only to determine whether the theory is internally executable, semantically coherent, well-typed, and behaviorally stable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Reality, Observation, Information, Evidence, Interpretation, Hypothesis, Hypothesis Space, Evidence Assessment, Epistemic Standards, Model, Determination, Knowledge Attribution, Epistemic State, Knowledge State K_t, Inquiry Q, Ideal State I_t, Requirements, Gap, Zero, Proposal, Decision, Authorization, Action, History, Identity, Revision, Supersession. ... test whether these are genuinely distinct conceptual roles or whether some are accidentally redundant, circular, or impossible to operationalize.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the primary research question: whether twenty-six named conceptual roles spanning the entire epistemic lifecycle can coexist operationally in one executable simulation without collapsing, or whether some are accidentally redundant, circular, or impossible to operationalize.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t = Gamma(E_t, Q_t, C_t, EC_t) where Gamma determines which parts of the epistemic state qualify as Knowledge State content ... Knowledge remains factive: Knows(a,p,c,t) -> True(p,c,t). Do NOT operationally assume that the simulation can magically observe objective truth. If truth is externally supplied by the simulation world, explicitly label that as world-state information and keep it separate from the agent's epistemic state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the core theory-under-test's Knowledge Attribution mechanism K_t=Gamma(E_t,Q_t,C_t,EC_t) with mandatory factivity Knows(a,p,c,t)=>True(p,c,t), explicitly forbidding the simulation from assuming it can observe objective truth directly -- any world-supplied ground truth must be labelled as world-state information kept separate from the agent's own epistemic state (an oracle-vs-agent-knowledge separation).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do NOT make Bayesian likelihood ratios a universal KnowledgeOS law. Also test non-Bayesian / qualitative evidence assessment. ... Test whether changing epistemic standards can change assessment or determination while the underlying evidence remains identical. ... A model that fits simulated observations must not automatically be classified as true.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates that evidence assessment be tested with BOTH a Bayesian likelihood-ratio realization AND non-Bayesian/qualitative assessment regimes (Bayesian ratios must never become a universal KnowledgeOS law); requires an explicit test that varying epistemic standards alone (holding reality/observation/evidence/inquiry fixed) can change assessment or determination; and requires model-fit to be tested separately from causal/epistemic validity so that a well-fitting model is never automatically classified as true.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Reality != Observation, Observation != Evidence, ... Epistemic State != Knowledge State, Knowledge State != Ideal State, Gap != Zero, Gap != Innovation, Probability != Truth, Credence != Truth, Information Quantity != Evidence Weight, Evidence Weight != Knowledge Gain, Model Fit != Model Validity, History != Current State, Identity != State Equality, Completeness != Sufficiency, Rejection != Acceptance, ... Semantic Equivalence != Representation Equality, Mathematical Regime != Knowledge Ontology.
a_rows_sample.statement: Enumerates a mandatory list of roughly twenty required state separations the simulator must never accidentally collapse (Reality/Observation/Evidence/Interpretation/Hypothesis/Determination/Knowledge/Decision/Authorization/Action chain; Epistemic State/Knowledge State/Ideal State; Gap/Zero/Innovation; Probability/Credence/Truth; Information Quantity/Evidence Weight/Knowledge Gain; Model Fit/Model Validity; History/Current State; Identity/State Equality; Completeness/Sufficiency; Rejection/Acceptance; Unknown/Unobserved/Unobservable/Underdetermined; Semantic Equivalence/Representation Equality; Mathematical Regime/Knowledge Ontology), with any collapse to be reported as a failure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SCENARIO A -- SIMPLE DETERMINATION ... SCENARIO B -- INCOMPLETE EVIDENCE ... Determination = empty or unresolved ... The system must NOT invent a value. This is an anti-fabrication test. ... SCENARIO C -- MULTIPLE COMPETING HYPOTHESES ... Test explicitly: Reject(H1) != Accept(H2). ... SCENARIO D -- DIFFERENT EPISTEMIC STANDARDS ... SCENARIO E -- DIFFERENT INQUIRIES
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies ten required scenario families (A-J): A simple determination (verifying knowledge is not merely copied from observation); B incomplete evidence (anti-fabrication test: the system must not invent a value when Determination is empty); C multiple competing hypotheses (testing Reject(H1)!=Accept(H2)); D different epistemic standards holding reality/observation/evidence/inquiry fixed while varying only S_t^epi; E different inquiries over the identical K_t testing inquiry-relative adequacy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SCENARIO F -- CONFLICTING EVIDENCE ... Do NOT automatically average them. ... The system can preserve unresolved conflict. SCENARIO G -- DEPENDENT EVIDENCE ... represent dependence, avoid double counting, or explicitly state that independence is an assumption. SCENARIO H -- MODEL MISMATCH ... Fit alone does not produce Knowledge. SCENARIO I -- RETROSPECTIVE REVISION ... Do NOT rewrite history as if K_1 never existed. SCENARIO J -- UNOBSERVABLE PROPERTY ... Do NOT classify this as: observed false, probability zero, rejected hypothesis, evidence absence.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies scenario families F-J: F conflicting evidence (system must preserve unresolved conflict rather than automatically averaging); G dependent evidence (must represent dependence, avoid double-counting, or explicitly declare independence as an assumption); H model mismatch (a better-fitting but causally wrong model M1 versus a causally correct M2 -- fit alone must not produce Knowledge); I retrospective revision (K_2 != K_1, historical K_1 must remain traceable, never rewritten); J unobservable property (must be classified as Unknown/Unobservable, never as observed-false, probability-zero, rejected-hypothesis, or evidence-absence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: UNOBSERVED, UNINTERPRETED, UNDERDETERMINED, UNOBSERVABLE. Create test cases where each one occurs independently. ... Verify that the four cases do not collapse into one generic UNKNOWN.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a four-way Unknown taxonomy test with independently constructed test cases for each of Unobserved/Uninterpreted/Underdetermined/Unobservable, checking Observation/Interpretation/Evidence/Determination/Knowledge/Gap/Zero status for each, explicitly verifying the four cases do not collapse into one generic UNKNOWN.

a_rows_sample.anchor: At every transition record: input state, output state, transformation, provenance, assumptions, responsible conceptual role, whether semantic information was added, whether uncertainty changed, whether knowledge attribution changed, whether requirements changed, whether the transition was reversible.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a full 21-step epistemic lifecycle trace (Reality->Observation->Information->Evidence->Interpretation->HypothesisSpace->EvidenceAssessment->Determination->KnowledgeAttribution->K_t->Inquiry->IdealState->RequirementEvaluation->Gap->Zero->Proposal->Decision->Authorization->Action->newObservation->K_{t+1}) with eleven recorded facts at every single transition (input/output state, transformation, provenance, assumptions, responsible conceptual role, whether semantic information/uncertainty/attribution/requirements changed, reversibility).

a_rows_sample.anchor: If X -> Y -> Z and no new information enters between Y and Z, then Z must not magically contain semantic information unavailable in Y, except where explicitly introduced by: model assumptions, external information, inference rules, prior knowledge, standards. If new information appears, identify its source. Any unexplained semantic information creation is a critical failure.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates an Information Conservation test operationalizing the data-processing-inequality principle: no unexplained semantic information may appear between two steps with no new input, unless explicitly attributable to model assumptions, external information, inference rules, prior knowledge, or standards -- any unexplained semantic-information creation is a critical failure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: high probability != knowledge, strong evidence != knowledge, coherent belief != knowledge, model fit != knowledge, determination != knowledge. ... If the simulator cannot establish Truth independently, it must not silently classify the claim as Knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a Knowledge Attribution test constructing six epistemic-state cases (true/false/uncertain/rejected/highly-probable/justified-but-not-truth-verified hypotheses) and checking five non-collapse requirements (high probability, strong evidence, coherent belief, model fit, and determination all != knowledge); if the simulator cannot establish Truth independently, it must not silently classify a claim as Knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Implementation A: explicit Interpret + Represent. Implementation B: single combined semantic transformation. Implementation C: different internal data structure. ... The comparison MUST NOT be based only on operator names. ... If semantic equivalence cannot be defined independently of behavior, report the circularity.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a Semantic Equivalence test comparing three deliberately different implementations of the same conceptual operation (split Interpret+Represent, a single combined transformation, and a different internal data structure) over nine behavioral dimensions (inquiries, context, evidence, determinations, gaps, history, transitions, knowledge attribution, invariant preservation), explicitly never based on operator names alone, and mandates reporting circularity if semantic equivalence cannot be defined independently of behavior.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This is NOT the previous 13-operator counting experiment. Do NOT begin with: "How many operators are there?" Instead ask: "What semantic capabilities are required?" ... K_min = argmin Complexity(R) subject to: semantic adequacy, transition completeness, invariant preservation, capability completeness, fixed semantic carrier, fixed observable behavior contract. If the feasible set changes between representations, cardinality comparisons are invalid. Report this explicitly.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly reframes the Kernel Minimality test away from the prior 13-operator counting approach: begin with 'what semantic capabilities are required' (Capability = externally distinguishable epistemic transformation/responsibility), construct the required capability set C and a candidate representation R, and test capability-set equivalence between differently-operator-counted implementations BEFORE any minimization; formalizes K_min=argmin Complexity(R) subject to six simultaneous constraints, mandating an explicit report that cardinality comparisons are invalid whenever the feasible set changes between representations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Investigate whether: Zero = no unmet requirement can be maintained without turning Zero into a semantic notion of absolute certainty. ... test all combinations: Gap exists, Gap empty, Evidence incomplete, Evidence conflicting, Evidence unavailable, Requirement irrelevant, Requirement satisfied by negative determination, Requirement satisfied by "cannot determine".
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a Zero test evaluating Delta_t and Zero(K_t,Q_t,C_t,EC_t) across eight named combinations (gap exists/empty, evidence incomplete/conflicting/unavailable, requirement irrelevant, requirement satisfied by negative determination, requirement satisfied by 'cannot determine'), investigating whether Zero can be maintained as no-unmet-requirement without sliding into a semantic notion of absolute certainty.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Create cases where: determination is unique but multiple actions are possible. Expected: Determination does not automatically imply one Decision. ... decision exists but authorization is absent. Expected: Decision != Authorization. ... authorization exists but action does not occur. Expected: Authorization != Action.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a Decision Boundary test with three constructed cases proving Determination does not automatically imply one Decision, Decision != Authorization (decision without authorization), and Authorization != Action (authorization without resulting action).

a_rows_sample.anchor: X causes Y but an observed confounder Z creates a strong association. Also create: X and Y correlated but X does not cause Y. ... The result must distinguish: Association, Prediction, Explanation, Causal Claim. A fitted model is insufficient for causal determination.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a Causal/Statistical test with two constructed confounding scenarios (X causes Y with a confounding Z creating spurious association; X and Y correlated with no causal link), requiring the system to distinguish Association, Prediction, Explanation, and Causal Claim as four separate categories -- a fitted model is insufficient for causal determination.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1. highly probable but false claim 2. true claim with weak evidence 3. duplicated evidence 4. correlated evidence 5. misleading source ... 18. conclusion generated without supporting evidence. The simulator must prefer: "cannot determine" over fabricated certainty.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates eighteen named adversarial test cases explicitly designed to fool the simulator (highly-probable-but-false claim, true-claim-with-weak-evidence, duplicated/correlated evidence, misleading source, wrong-model-with-excellent-fit, correct-model-with-sparse-evidence, rejected-hypothesis-later-reinstated, ambiguous interpretation, representation change, changing inquiry/standard, unavailable observation, historical-vs-current state, conflicting/irrelevant evidence, false inference from correlation, unsupported conclusion), with the overriding requirement that the simulator prefer 'cannot determine' over fabricated certainty in every case.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P1: Evidence != Knowledge ... P8: Evidence dependence prevents unjustified double counting ... P11: Knowledge attribution respects factivity ... P19: Changing K_t does not imply changing identity ... P20: Zero is inquiry-relative. ... For each property define: Property ID, Formal statement, Generator assumptions, Test procedure, Observed result, Counterexamples.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates property-based testing with a required protocol per property (ID, formal statement, generator assumptions, test procedure, observed result, counterexamples), specifying twenty named minimum properties P1-P20 spanning Evidence!=Knowledge, Determination!=Knowledge, Rejection!=Acceptance, Gap!=Zero, inquiry-relative adequacy, historical-vs-current-state distinguishability, representation-vs-semantic equality, dependence-aware evidence, model-fit-vs-causal-validity, no-unsupported-information-creation, factivity-respecting attribution, standards-dependent assessment, Unobservable!=Underdetermined, Completeness!=Sufficiency, the Decision/Determination/Authorization/Action chain, CurrentState!=History, identity-preservation-under-state-change, and inquiry-relative Zero.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Use at least 10,000 trials per major property family ... But DO NOT interpret the result as a population estimate about the real world. Monte Carlo uncertainty describes the simulator/generator. ... Always audit vacuity. If: guard_active = 0 then: 100% pass means nothing.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates Monte Carlo requirements (>=10,000 trials per major property family where computationally reasonable) explicitly forbidding interpretation as a real-world population estimate (Monte Carlo uncertainty describes only the simulator/generator), and mandates an always-run vacuity audit (guard_active=0 makes a 100% pass rate meaningless) -- directly carrying forward the vacuity-audit discipline discovered in the earlier kernel-reduction experiment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: For every successful property identify exactly where the tested capability came from. Detect hidden capabilities embedded in: world generator, data structure, serializer, simulator helper, test oracle, random generator, state constructor, hard-coded labels, evaluation function. Particularly inspect: Observe, Interpret, Represent, Discriminate, Hypothesize, Determine, Select, Revise, Validate.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a No-Smuggling Audit for every successful property, tracing exactly where the tested capability actually came from and checking nine possible hidden-capability locations (world generator, data structure, serializer, simulator helper, test oracle, random generator, state constructor, hard-coded labels, evaluation function), with particular scrutiny of nine named operators (Observe, Interpret, Represent, Discriminate, Hypothesize, Determine, Select, Revise, Validate) -- directly carrying forward the semantic-smuggling discipline from the kernel-reduction experiment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 19 PASS / 1 PARTIAL / 0 FAIL in the deterministic suite ... this is the *weakest* outcome, not the strongest.
b_rows_sample.statement: Deterministic suite across 10 scenarios x 20 properties yields 19 PASS / 1 PARTIAL(CIRC-5)/2 DEFINITIONAL, but the report explicitly warns this is the weakest evidence in the paper because deterministic passes can be vacuous.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AD-1 highly probable but false claim ... FAIL — CE-1 ... AD-18 conclusion with no supporting evidence ... FAIL — CE-2 (positive control)
b_rows_sample.statement: Adversarial suite: AD-1 attributes os=RHEL9.8 against true RHEL8.6 (CE-1 factivity failure); AD-18's injected unsupported conclusion is caught by P10 yet still attributed (CE-2 positive-control failure, since attribution never checks provenance).

b_rows_sample.anchor: P11 | 0.3394 ... 420 | 0.1237 ... P3's guard never activated ... Its 100% pass is vacuous and must not be cited
b_rows_sample.statement: Randomized layer (10,000 trials, 5 seeds x 2000): P11's guard activates in 33.94% of trials with 420 failures (conditional failure rate 0.1237); P3's guard never activates so its 100% pass rate is vacuous and excluded from evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: a source rated reliable reported a **false** value | **414 / 665** | **0.6226** ... Every violation is explained by the epistemic state being unable to distinguish a reliable-looking false report from a true one.
b_rows_sample.statement: Factivity diagnosis: conditional on an attribution being made, violation rate is 0.6226 (414/665) when a policy-trusted source reported a false value versus 0/2607 otherwise, interpreted as 'the witness in A at scale' rather than a tuning problem.

b_rows_sample.anchor: No total Gamma : (E,Q,C,EC) -> K that attributes anything is factive | DERIVED PROPOSITION, witness-supported ... not yet written as a theorem in the theory document
b_rows_sample.statement: Grades the factivity-impossibility claim as a derived, witness-supported proposition whose general one-line argument (Gamma's domain excludes truth) has not yet been written as a formal theorem in the theory document.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The non-circularity and the impossibility are the same fact. Because truth never re-enters the agent's state, Gamma cannot consult it -- which is exactly why CE-1 occurs.
b_rows_sample.statement: CIRC-1 (Knowledge-via-Truth / Truth-via-Knowledge) is found NOT circular, and this non-circularity is identified as the same underlying fact that produces CE-1: World.truth is exogenous and no agent transition reads it, so Gamma structurally cannot be factive.

b_rows_sample.anchor: TG-1 | DEF-1 factivity and the v1.1 equation K = Gamma(E,Q,C,EC) are jointly unsatisfiable for any attributing Gamma | G3 epistemological | CE-1; witness; 420/10000 randomized violations | CRITICAL
b_rows_sample.statement: Registers TG-1 (CRITICAL, G3 epistemological class): the factivity/attribution-equation impossibility, evidenced by the CE-1 witness and 420/10000 randomized violations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R1 -- Rename the object ... R2 -- Make factivity external ... R3 -- Make Gamma partial ... The choice is a theory decision, not an experimental one. This lane does not make it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents three unchosen repairs for TG-1 -- R1 rename K_t to attributed knowledge, R2 make factivity an externally-verified success condition no component may assert, R3 make Gamma partial (attribute only where externally verifiable) -- explicitly declaring the choice a theory/governance decision outside this experiment's scope.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The theory executes the whole epistemic lifecycle and keeps every distinction it declares -- except that DEF-1 (factivity) and the v1.1 attribution equation K = Gamma(E,Q,C,EC) cannot both hold. Theory status: B. PARTIALLY EXECUTABLE.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the one-line headline result for the whole v1.1 simulation lane and its Theory Status verdict (B. PARTIALLY EXECUTABLE), restated from the FINAL-VERDICT artifact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DEF-1 (factivity) and the v1.1 attribution equation are jointly unsatisfiable for any total Gamma that attributes anything ... The only escaping policy attributes nothing.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the factivity-impossibility as established, adding that the only Gamma escaping the contradiction attributes nothing at all.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Factivity Repair Experiment. Implement all three repairs from L ... as three arms over the same scenarios and the same 10,000 worlds ... Do not run another large randomized simulation first.
b_rows_sample.statement: Prescribes the Factivity Repair Experiment as the mandatory next step: run R1/R2/R3 as three arms over the identical 10,000 worlds, explicitly forbidding another large randomized run before this.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the review says: Strong candidate [DEF] Sat: K x R -> {top,bot,U}. I would change that to: [PROP] Candidate common satisfaction interface ... because our latest simulation has already exposed a fundamental issue: factivity vs Gamma-determinacy.
b_rows_sample.statement: First self-review downgrades Sat from a proposed [DEF] to [PROP], citing the v1.1 factivity/Gamma-determinacy impossibility as the reason it cannot yet be mathematically closed.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
(1)  Knows(a,p,c,t) → True(p,c,t)                     DEF-1, factivity
(2)  K_{a,c,t} = Γ(E_{a,c,t}, Q_t, C_t, EC_t)         the v1.1/v1.2 attribution equation

**They are jointly unsatisfiable for any total `Γ` that attributes anything.**
b_rows_sample.statement: States the core formal impossibility result: DEF-1 (Knows(a,p,c,t)->True(p,c,t)) and the attribution equation K=Gamma(E,Q,C,EC) are jointly unsatisfiable for any total Gamma that attributes anything.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Two worlds differ in the truth of `p`. A source the admission policy rates reliable reports the same value in both. The resulting epistemic states are **bit-identical**
b_rows_sample.statement: The witness proof: two possible worlds differing only in the truth of p, with an admission-policy-trusted source reporting identically in both, produce bit-identical epistemic states (verified by fingerprint over observations/evidence/interpretations/assessments/determinations/hypotheses/rejections); since Gamma is a function of E alone it returns an identical K, yet the attribution is true in one world and false in the other.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
| `justified-unique` | yes | **yes** |
| `justified-any` | yes | **yes** |
| `none` | **no** | no |
b_rows_sample.statement: Policy sweep: both attribution policies that attribute anything (justified-unique, justified-any) violate factivity; only the 'none' policy escapes violation, and only because it attributes nothing.

b_rows_sample.anchor: **At scale:** 420 factivity violations in 10 000 paired worlds; conditional rate **0.1237** given an attribution was made. Diagnosis: **414 / 665** violations where a policy-trusted source reported a falsehood, **0 / 2 607** otherwise.
b_rows_sample.statement: Quantifies the violation at scale: 420/10000 paired worlds violate factivity (conditional rate 0.1237 given an attribution is made); localization is near-total, 414 of 665 violations occur specifically where a policy-trusted source reported a falsehood, versus 0 of 2607 otherwise.

b_rows_sample.anchor: **And the satisfaction layer confirms it independently:** **no `Sat_c` class in the eight-class family requires factivity.** A state can satisfy all eight and be false.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports an independent confirmation from a completely different direction: no Sat_c class among the eight requirement classes requires factivity, visible from the specification alone before execution -- a state can satisfy all eight classes and still be false.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 4. v1.1-simulation is identified, not inferred ... theory-v1.1-simulation simulates 20260902-004631, and postdates 00:46:31. Provenance of the document's own timestamp remains UNRECORDABLE, not ABSENT.
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes via content evidence (not internal timestamps, since none exist across all 14 files) that theory-v1.1-simulation postdates and directly simulates Theory v1.0 (matching experiment ID/scenario seed 20260902, exactly resolving citations to SS47's refined 7-state backbone and SS66's Preservation vector, using DEF numbers all within DEF-1..33). Classifies the package's own timestamp provenance as UNRECORDABLE, explicitly distinct from ABSENT.

b_rows_sample.anchor: And it contributes two objects of its own: EC is typed ... EpistemicContract(standard, requirements, attribution_policy) ... A standard/standard collision on two carriers, and it is not among the 10 collisions v1.1 registers. ... Γ is 4-argument: K = Γ(E,Q,C,EC) ... TG-1 proves it jointly unsatisfiable with DEF-1 factivity ... CE-1 is born here and cited by satc_spec.py — a verified cross-package citation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Records two objects v1.1-simulation itself contributes: a typed EC=EpistemicContract(standard,requirements,attribution_policy), whose own 'standard' sub-field (EpistemicStandard(min_weight,require_independent_sources,require_corroboration)) is a DIFFERENT type from r's 'standard' field (an acceptance criterion) -- flagged as an unregistered standard/standard collision, not among v1.1's own ten registered collisions; and a 4-argument Gamma realized as K=Gamma(E,Q,C,EC)=knowledge_attribution(E,Q,C,EC), whose TG-1 proves jointly unsatisfiable with DEF-1 factivity for any attributing Gamma (the CE-1 finding, connecting directly to the prior batch's v1-1-sim-factivity-impossibility-finding object), with three unchosen repairs R1/R2/R3 explicitly framed as 'a theory decision, not an experimental one.' Verifies CE-1 is genuinely cross-cited by a separate package (satc_spec.py's factivity_requirement note), confirming real cross-package citation rather than coincidental naming.
