a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation -> Fact -> Derivation -> Architectural Principle -> Invariant ... Invariant -> Implementation -> Test -> Evidence
a_rows_sample.statement: States the ledger's two-directional fundamental chain (forward: Observation->Fact->Derivation->Architectural Principle->Invariant; feedback: Invariant->Implementation->Test->Evidence->New Knowledge), diagrammed as the architecture's epistemic feedback loop.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge_t != Knowledge_{t+1} ... The fact that H_2 is better does not mean H_1 never existed
a_rows_sample.statement: States that the ledger must preserve chronology (when a belief was held), not only its content, since a later, better hypothesis H2 does not erase the historical fact that an earlier hypothesis H1 was held -- essential to reconstructing the real engineering journey rather than a retrospectively idealized one.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Calendar chronology ... Engineering chronology ... Epistemic chronology ... The code may exist before the architectural concept has been named
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three non-identical chronologies (calendar: when it happened; engineering: what was built before what; epistemic: when it was understood), illustrated by Implementation->Observation->Understanding, where code can precede the naming of its own underlying architectural concept.

a_rows_sample.anchor: implementation -> repeated problem -> experiment -> pattern recognized -> concept named ... The later name should not be projected backward as though it had been consciously designed from the beginning
a_rows_sample.statement: Names the 'late naming' phenomenon: a pattern can exist implicitly in the implementation before it is given a formal concept name, and warns against projecting the later name backward as if it had been consciously designed from the start, since that would distort the history.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | Field | Purpose | ... Rejected alternative | What was not chosen |
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a practical 15-field Evidence Ledger schema (Step ID, Artifact, Date/sequence, Observation, Fact, Interpretation, Derived principle, Decision, Rejected alternative, Architectural consequence, Invariant, Verification, Evidence status F/D/P/U, Confidence, Open question).

a_rows_sample.anchor: What we rejected ... as by: What we selected ... That rejection itself is architectural knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues architecture is defined as much by what was rejected as by what was selected (e.g. Alternative A rejected because SemanticLoss(A)>0), justifying a dedicated 'Rejected alternative' ledger field as architectural knowledge in its own right.

a_rows_sample.anchor: NegativeKnowledge ... knowledge about approaches, assumptions, transitions or interpretations that have been demonstrated to be unsuitable under specified conditions ... different from failure
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces NegativeKnowledge as knowledge about approaches/assumptions/transitions/interpretations demonstrated unsuitable under specified conditions, distinguished from mere failure -- a failure becomes useful (negative) knowledge only once its cause ('why it failed') is understood.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment=(Hypothesis,Setup,Observation,Result,Interpretation,Consequence) ... Result -> Knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a six-field experimental-lineage record (Hypothesis, Setup, Observation, Result, Interpretation, Consequence) intended to let the eventual book demonstrate the scientific/engineering nature of the work.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A hypothesis says: X may be true ... An invariant says: X must remain true ... Hypothesis -[evidence]-> Pattern -[validation]-> Invariant. Not every hypothesis becomes an invariant
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes hypothesis (X may be true) from invariant (X must remain true) and defines the promotion pipeline Hypothesis->(evidence)->Pattern->(validation)->Invariant, explicitly noting not every hypothesis is promoted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observed(H) does not imply Universal(H) ... AllAI -> InconsistentCode [is unwarranted from one tested workflow]
a_rows_sample.statement: States a statistical-discipline guardrail: evidence for H under tested conditions (Observed(H)) must not be generalized to Universal(H), illustrated by a prompt-strategy-specific inconsistency finding that must not be generalized to all AI.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Claim=(Proposition,Context,Conditions) ... Valid(C) should really mean: Valid(C | Context,Conditions)
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes representing every conclusion as Claim=(Proposition,Context,Conditions) so that validity is always conditioned (Valid(C|Context,Conditions) rather than bare Valid(C)), framed as a connection between DDD and statistical reasoning; extends this to bounded knowledge (Knowledge_A != Knowledge_B across DDD bounded contexts, requiring an explicit ubiquitous-language-guarded translation when a concept crosses a context boundary).

a_rows_sample.anchor: p(C_A) => p'(C_B) ... where p' is the explicitly defined interpretation in the target context. If that implication does not hold, the contract may introduce semantic loss
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a semantic-preservation condition for cross-context evidence transfer: a property p holding in context C_A after transformation T to C_B must imply the target-context-defined interpretation p' holds in C_B, or the contract introduces semantic loss; states evidence for a claim in one context does not automatically establish it in another without an explicit Mapping and evidence the property survives translation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ELG=(V,E) ... V=Artifacts∪Facts∪Observations∪Hypotheses∪Decisions∪Principles∪Invariants ... substantially richer than a conventional requirements traceability matrix
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Evidence Ledger as a graph ELG=(V,E) with seven node types (artifacts, facts, observations, hypotheses, decisions, principles, invariants) and seven edge types (supports, contradicts, derives, motivates, rejects, implements, verifies), explicitly positioned as richer than a conventional requirements traceability matrix.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C_1 <-[contradicts]-> C_2 ... We should not immediately delete one. Instead record: Contradiction(C_1,C_2) ... Sometimes the contradiction disappears once context is made explicit
a_rows_sample.statement: Treats contradiction as a first-class graph edge to be recorded rather than resolved by deletion; investigating Context(C_1) vs Context(C_2) can dissolve an apparent contradiction, and more generally an apparent contradiction (ModelA accurate vs inaccurate) can resolve into conditional coherence once Context/Population/Time/Purpose dimensions are introduced -- framed as contradiction potentially revealing a missing dimension.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Generation != Adjudication ... Candidates -> Evidence -> Adjudication -> AcceptedKnowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies the contradiction-as-evidence principle to AI-generated competing interpretations: rather than declaring one AI output true and another false, treats {AI_1,AI_2} as an explicit candidate knowledge set requiring adjudication, architecturally separating Generation from Adjudication via Candidates->Evidence->Adjudication->AcceptedKnowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KState in {Observed,Hypothesized,Derived,Corroborated,Contested,Rejected,Accepted,Deprecated} ... should not automatically be treated as a single linear lifecycle ... Accepted + Contested
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines an eight-value knowledge-item epistemic state (Observed/Hypothesized/Derived/Corroborated/Contested/Rejected/Accepted/Deprecated), explicitly not a single linear lifecycle -- states may coexist, e.g. Accepted+Contested when knowledge is operationally accepted but still scientifically disputed; reiterates the anti-Boolean discipline (verified=true is insufficient; use KnowledgeState+Evidence+Context+Time).

a_rows_sample.anchor: UnderlyingPrinciple != CurrentManifestation ... The analogy helps us ask better architecture questions. It does not prove them
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies a Gita chapter-4 analogy (enduring knowledge vs changing manifestation) to DomainInvariant!=CurrentRuntimeState and HistoricalKnowledge!=CurrentRepresentation, explicitly bounding the analogy as interpretive/heuristic ('helps us ask better questions, does not prove them').

a_rows_sample.anchor: S_{t+1} does not contain all information about S_t ... S_{t+1} ⊉ S_t ... CurrentState + HistoricalRecord -> HistoricalUnderstanding
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the 'new state does not know old state' principle as S_{t+1} not-superset-of S_t in general, requiring an additional historical mechanism H_t; concludes CurrentState alone is insufficient and CurrentState+HistoricalRecord is needed for HistoricalUnderstanding, distinguishing CurrentState, HistoricalRecord, and HistoricalInterpretation as three different things.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t=(CurrentKnowledge_t,HistoricalKnowledge,Uncertainty_t) ... Update does not necessarily erase prior knowledge ... KnowledgeVersion [distinct from] KnowledgeState ... Git commit != current working tree
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a knowledge-continuity model K_t=(CurrentKnowledge_t,HistoricalKnowledge,Uncertainty_t) with K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,E_{t+1}), where Update may supersede/qualify/contradict/preserve/deprecate rather than erase prior knowledge; proposes distinguishing KnowledgeVersion from KnowledgeState by analogy to a git commit vs the current working tree, again explicitly flagged as analogy not proof.

b_rows_sample.anchor: **VERDICT: `UNRECONCILED ALTERNATIVES` — NOT supersession** ... the ledger has now been commissioned FOUR times: steps 109 (Artifact E), 214, 218, and 219 (`MASTER EVIDENCE LEDGER v0.1`) — across 110 steps, with zero cross-references and zero rows produced.
b_rows_sample.statement: Answering the governing mandate's explicit question about Step 214 vs Step 218's Evidence Ledger relationship: they are UNRECONCILED ALTERNATIVES, not supersession (neither cites the other, different tuple arities, different scope, neither populated); the Evidence Ledger concept has now been independently commissioned four times (steps 109, 214, 218, 219) across 110 steps with zero cross-references and zero rows ever produced in any of the four.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | 218.1 | `Rᵢ = (Sᵢ,Aᵢ,Oᵢ,Fᵢ,Hᵢ,Eᵢ,Dᵢ,Pᵢ,Iᵢ,Vᵢ,Uᵢ)` — 11-tuple | **SYMBOL COLLISION** — step-215 §215.1 binds `R(Sᵢ)` to a **5-tuple** ... Same glyph, different arity, three steps apart, **uncited**
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 218 section 218.1 binds R_i to an 11-tuple per-step record, colliding with Step 215 section 215.1's binding of R(S_i) to an unrelated 5-tuple three steps earlier, with no citation or reconciliation -- the same glyph with two different arities and meanings.

b_rows_sample.anchor: **`K` is defined twice, incompatibly, WITHIN Step 218** `[SUPERVISOR-VERIFIED]` ... **This brings the corpus total to at least eight incompatible definitions of `K`**
b_rows_sample.statement: Supervisor-verified finding: Step 218 defines K twice incompatibly within the same file, 37 lines apart -- a 7-tuple (Identity, Version, Content, Context, Provenance, Validity, EpistemicStatus) at section 218.27, and a 5-tuple (x,c,t,p,e = content, context, temporal validity, provenance, epistemic state) at section 218.30, the latter being the one the Semantic Preservation Principle is actually stated over; this brings the corpus total to at least eight incompatible definitions of K across the whole programme.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 218.22 | **`Deprecated ≠ Falsified`** | **SURVIVES — new, correct, and non-obvious**
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 218 section 218.22 introduces Deprecated != Falsified as a new, correct, and non-obvious distinction, judged to survive verification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: `Loss_semantic = CriticalAttributes_in − CriticalAttributes_out`, prefaced ***"instead of literal subtraction"*** | **CORRECT — and an improvement.** Set difference over attribute sets is well-defined. Contrast §208.10/§212.19, which perform the same subtraction on an undefined *measure*
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 218 section 218.33's semantic-loss formula, explicitly reframed as set difference over attribute sets rather than literal numeric subtraction, is judged correct and an improvement, contrasted favorably against Step 208 section 208.10 and Step 212 section 212.19's earlier subtraction on an undefined information measure.

group_evidence.why_grouped: working_label token overlap Jaccard=0.50 (shared tokens: ['evidence', 'ledger'])

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 280 has executed the empirical closure test. The result is clear: EC = NOT ACHIEVED. The reason is Critical Failure #7: missingness is silently converted into a substantive value. The theory cannot distinguish: "nobody ever asked" from "we asked and it isn't there". Both are a ∉ 𝒜.
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 281 is commissioned because Step 280's empirical closure test found EC=NOT ACHIEVED: Critical Failure #7, where both 'nobody ever asked' and 'we asked and it isn't there' render identically as absence from the assertion set (a not-in A), silently converting missingness into a substantive value.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Contradiction → Reproduce → Classify → Locate → Correct → Retest. Step 280 completed up to Locate. Step 281 must complete Correct and Retest.
a_rows_sample.statement: The governing six-stage principle for defect handling (Contradiction -> Reproduce -> Classify -> Locate -> Correct -> Retest), with Step 280 explicitly having completed only the first four stages and Step 281 tasked with completing Correct and Retest.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Minimum extension preserving all mandatory distinctions. The repair must be the minimum change required to distinguish all empirically required forms of absence, unknownness, non-asking, and disconnected knowledge, without violating the already-established invariants.
a_rows_sample.statement: The Step 281 governing principle: any repair must be the minimum extension that distinguishes all mandatory epistemic states while preserving every already-established invariant -- later formalized as the M1/M2/M3 minimality criterion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A — Explicit ⊥-assertion | Introduce a bottom assertion to represent "not asked" | Clean, minimal | May conflate with "unknown". B — Questions-asked register | Separate structure recording propositions that were queried | Preserves provenance | Adds complexity. C — Hybrid | ⊥-assertion + questions-a
a_rows_sample.statement: Three high-level candidate repairs are proposed at commissioning time: A (an explicit bottom-value assertion representing 'not asked'), B (a separate questions-asked register preserving provenance at the cost of added structure), and C (a hybrid of both, judged possibly redundant) -- later formally specified and executed in the correction document and exec/ artifacts.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not redesign the entire theory. Do not introduce unnecessary complexity. Do not ignore the minimality criterion. Do not silently repair without evidence. Do not claim closure without verification. Do not proceed to Step 282 until missingness is resolved.
a_rows_sample.statement: Six negative constraints scope Step 281: no full theory redesign, no unnecessary complexity, minimality must not be ignored, no silent repair without evidence, no closure claim without verification, and no proceeding to Step 282 until missingness is resolved.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 281 is CONDITIONALLY ACCEPTED with required corrections. ... 1. Detail the candidate repairs (A, B, C) with precise representations 2. Define the minimality criterion 3. Analyze the orphan state separately 4. Define the empirical re-test protocol
a_rows_sample.statement: The supervisory review's HPA ruling CONDITIONALLY ACCEPTS the Step-281 mandate, requiring ten mandatory corrections: precise per-option formal representations for candidates A/B/C, an explicit minimality criterion, a separate analysis of the orphan state, and a defined executable empirical re-test protocol.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 5. Define the gap register update criteria 6. Define internal closure 7. Analyze missingness in Σ 8. Analyze orphan formal semantics 9. Define repair governance 10. Define explicit success criteria
a_rows_sample.statement: The remaining six of the ten mandatory corrections in the HPA ruling: define gap-register update criteria, define 'internal closure', analyze whether missingness belongs in Sigma, formally analyze orphan semantics (including the EKP's orphan_document), define an explicit repair-governance process, and define explicit success criteria for Step 281.

a_rows_sample.anchor: M1 Not Asked ... M2 Asked + Absent ... M3 Asked + Unknown ... M4 Supported ... M5 Refuted ... M6 Conflicted ... M7 Orphan | An assertion/document exists but has no required semantic relationship. The first six are epistemic cases. The seventh is not automatically an epistemic status.
a_rows_sample.statement: The seven mandatory states any missingness repair must distinguish: M1 Not Asked, M2 Asked+Absent, M3 Asked+Unknown, M4 Supported, M5 Refuted, M6 Conflicted (six epistemic cases), and M7 Orphan, explicitly flagged as not automatically an epistemic status but possibly a structural condition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ⊥_p = (id,p,BOTTOM,t,π) ... Advantage: very small extension. Defect: ⊥ becomes overloaded unless its semantics explicitly distinguish: absent; unknown; unavailable; not determined.
a_rows_sample.statement: Candidate Repair A is formally defined as a bottom-tuple (id,proposition,BOTTOM,timestamp,provenance) recording explicit absence, with the stated defect that BOTTOM becomes semantically overloaded unless it precisely distinguishes absent/unknown/unavailable/not-determined -- later executed and refuted in repairs.py/test_repair_selection.py.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q_t ⊆ P where Q_t records propositions that have actually been queried/evaluated. ... This directly solves the E4 distinction. However, it introduces a new explicit structure: Q_t. That structure must then participate in: identity; equality; replay; serialization; persistence; transformation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Candidate Repair B is formally defined as an inquiry register Q_t (a subset of the proposition space P recording what was actually queried), noted to directly solve the E4 distinction but to require Q_t's participation in identity, equality, replay, serialization, persistence and transformation -- later executed and SELECTED in repairs.py/test_repair_selection.py, with those participation questions answered PRESERVED by test_invariant_preservation.py.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C1 — Absent and Unknown are equivalent ... The E4 failure provides evidence against making that assumption automatically. C2 — Inquiry and epistemic result remain separate dimensions: Σ* = I × E ... Therefore C cannot be accepted merely because it is elegant.
a_rows_sample.statement: Candidate Repair C is refined into two sub-forms: C1 (collapsing Asked+Absent into Unknown, rejected because E4's own failure is evidence against that assumption) and C2 (a typed epistemic state Sigma*=I x E keeping inquiry and epistemic-result as separate dimensions), with an explicit warning that elegance alone cannot justify accepting C -- later executed and found isomorphic to, but less minimal than, Repair B.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R* is minimal iff: M1 — Necessity: every component of ΔR is required to distinguish at least one mandatory state pair. M2 — Irreducibility: no proper subset ΔR′⊂ΔR can distinguish all mandatory states. M3 — No redundant distinction: the repair must not distinguish states that the mandatory operation
a_rows_sample.statement: The formal minimality criterion answering the supervisory review's demand: a proposed repair R* (with ΔR=R*-R0) is minimal iff every component of ΔR is necessary (M1), no proper subset of ΔR suffices (M2), and no unnecessary distinction is introduced beyond what the mandatory operation set can consume (M3) -- this exact three-part test is later executed verbatim in test_minimality.py and test_repair_selection.py.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Σ-A: Missingness becomes a component of Σ: Σ=(I,A,S,R,V,C). Σ-B: Missingness remains in the inquiry/evidence layer. Σ-C: A two-level model: Σ=Σ_inquiry×Σ_epistemic. ... Placement in Σ remains a design decision until minimality is demonstrated.
a_rows_sample.statement: Three alternative placements of missingness relative to Sigma are distinguished: Sigma-A (fold missingness into Sigma itself), Sigma-B (keep it in a separate inquiry/evidence layer), Sigma-C (a two-level product Sigma_inquiry x Sigma_epistemic) -- with the correction document leaving this an open design decision pending minimality proof rather than assuming Sigma-A as the earlier uncorrected Step 281 draft had done.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C* = typed inquiry + epistemic semantics ... ε_t(p)=(I_t(p),E_t(p)) where I_t(p)∈{NotAsked,Asked} and E_t(p) is defined only once inquiry has occurred. ... this candidate becomes canonical only after the minimality and empirical tests below succeed.
a_rows_sample.statement: The corrected document's working (not-yet-canonical) candidate: epsilon_t(p)=(I_t(p),E_t(p)) with I_t(p) in {NotAsked,Asked} and E_t(p) defined only once inquiry has occurred, explicitly gated on passing later minimality and empirical tests -- later found isomorphic to but less minimal than the executed Repair B (inquiry register).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The theory must prohibit an implicit transition: NotAsked → Refuted merely because p∉A. Thus: Absence cannot generate negative epistemic evidence.
a_rows_sample.statement: A new transformation invariant required of the repair: absence of an assertion must never generate an implicit transition to a substantive negative epistemic value (NotAsked directly to Refuted) merely from non-membership in the assertion set -- absence cannot generate negative epistemic evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I_{K_1}(p)≠I_{K_2}(p) is sufficient to establish: K_1 ≉_O K_2, provided an O_core operation can observe that distinction. This is the exact connection between the missingness defect and the earlier equality theory.
a_rows_sample.statement: A new equality consequence: because inquiry state becomes observable under the repair, a difference in inquiry state between two knowledge states K1 and K2 is sufficient by itself to establish observational non-equivalence K1 not-approx_O K2, provided some O_core operation can observe that distinction -- connecting the missingness repair directly to the pre-existing observational-equality theory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H_t=[Ask(p), NoDetermination(p)] must produce ε_t(p)=(Asked,Unknown/Absent) and not (NotAsked,∅). Therefore the repair creates a new replay invariant: Replay preserves inquiry semantics. This must be tested, not merely asserted.
a_rows_sample.statement: A new replay invariant required by the repair: replaying a history containing an Ask(p) event followed by NoDetermination(p) must reconstruct the (Asked,Unknown/Absent) state and never silently collapse back to (NotAsked,empty) -- explicitly flagged as requiring empirical testing, not mere assertion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: E4-R1 — Not Asked ... E4-R2 — Asked but Absent ... E4-R3 — Asked + Unknown ... E4-R7 — Orphan ... Create an asserted document/object without semantic relationships. Expected: Orphan=True without automatically changing E(p).
a_rows_sample.statement: The corrected, executable E4 re-test protocol defines seven test records (E4-R1 through E4-R7), each specifying a setup, an expected representation and an expected semantic result, including E4-R7 (orphan) requiring that Orphan=True while the epistemic state E(p) remains unchanged -- this exact protocol is executed verbatim (7/7 PASS) in exec/test_e4_rerun.py.

a_rows_sample.anchor: F1 | Policy-free result may otherwise be interpreted as absence | F3 | Policy conflict must not collapse into unknown merely through missing policy | F5 | Missing policy must remain distinct from no inquiry | F6 | Expired policy must not be represented as nonexistent policy | F10 | Historical replay
a_rows_sample.statement: Five falsification tests (F1, F3, F5, F6, F10) are identified as affected by the missingness repair because they interact with absence, policy, or historical semantics, and must be re-run under the chosen repair -- later executed 5/5 PASS in exec/test_affected_falsification.py.

a_rows_sample.anchor: {CLOSED,PARTIAL,OPEN,BLOCKED,NORMATIVE,EMPIRICAL} ... CLOSED: Defect repaired, required test passes, evidence preserved. ... NORMATIVE: Mathematics/evidence cannot determine the answer; governance decision required. EMPIRICAL: Theory is specified but executable evidence is still required.
a_rows_sample.statement: A six-status gap classification scheme replacing the earlier vague OPEN/PARTIAL treatment: CLOSED, PARTIAL, OPEN, BLOCKED, NORMATIVE (mathematics/evidence cannot decide; governance decision required), and EMPIRICAL (theory specified but executable evidence still needed).

b_rows_sample.anchor: C = (C_F,C_C,C_E,C_G,C_D,C_H)
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a six-dimensional closure vector C=(C_F,C_C,C_E,C_G,C_D,C_H) for Formal, Computational, Empirical, Governance, DDD/Architectural, and Historical/Traceability closure respectively, each given a precise informal definition (e.g. Empirical closure means the theory's claims have been tested against the actual KnowledgeOS/EKP environment and agree within declared acceptance criteria), with the mandatory chain: Executable reference implementation != Real KnowledgeOS implementation != Empirical validation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Level 0 — Conceptual ... Level 6 — Operationally validated
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an explicit seven-level evidence hierarchy (L0 Conceptual, L1 Corpus-supported, L2 Formally specified, L3 Reference-implemented, L4 Reproducibly executed, L5 Real-environment empirical, L6 Operationally validated) and states as a hard rule that Level 4 != Level 5 and Level 5 != Level 6, so no Level-4 result may be represented as Level-5 empirical closure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C_E = NOT\ ACHIEVED
b_rows_sample.statement: Empirical closure C_E is explicitly ruled NOT ACHIEVED because 15/24 constructs lack real-environment observation, the missingness repair has only Level-4 validation, some policy/authority behavior remains unobserved, measurement execution is incomplete, and real operational propagation is undemonstrated; this is called 'a hard decision.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: KNOWLEDGEOS THEORY — FORMALLY SUBSTANTIALLY CLOSED ... EMPIRICAL CLOSURE PENDING ... GOVERNANCE RATIFICATION PENDING
b_rows_sample.statement: HPA Decision (this draft): KnowledgeOS shall not be declared fully complete at Step 282; official state is 'FORMALLY SUBSTANTIALLY CLOSED' with 'EMPIRICAL CLOSURE PENDING' and 'GOVERNANCE RATIFICATION PENDING'; recommends the sequence Step 283 Governance Ratification -> Step 284 Final Empirical Conformance -> Step 285 Canonical Theory Freeze -> Step 286 Book/Architecture Publication Gate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A = REJECTED ... C2 = NOT\ REQUIRED ... Q_t\subseteq P ... is selected.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates and ratifies the Step 281 candidate outcome at governance level: Candidate A (bottom assertion) REJECTED; Candidate C2 (typed Sigma*=IxE) NOT REQUIRED (if governance later chooses C2 for implementation reasons this must be an explicit documented design decision, not a mathematical consequence); Candidate B (Q_t subset of P) SELECTED, subject to the obligation that Q_t become replayable and serializable in a real implementation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Uncertainty} \neq \text{Probability} ... \text{Unknown} \neq \text{Random Variable}
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues that the mere existence of uncertainty, incomplete information, unknown values, competing evidence, and non-identifiability does not logically imply a probability structure; probability is required only if KnowledgeOS makes claims of the form P(X in A)=p or uses probabilistic inference, Bayesian updating, or stochastic transition semantics, none of which the canonical state-transition model K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,e_t) or any of Unknown/Missing/Supported/Refuted/Conflicted/Superseded/provenance/lineage/replay requires.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \boxed{\text{T-3 = NOT REQUIRED FOR THE CORE THEORY}}
b_rows_sample.statement: Rules T-3 (probability space requirement) NOT REQUIRED FOR THE CORE THEORY, closed at core-theory level; states it must not be reopened merely because KnowledgeOS represents uncertainty, and that probability remains an optional measurement/statistical extension a future bounded context may explicitly supply.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Unknown} \not\equiv \text{Non-identifiable}
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Unknown (the system currently lacks a justified value) from Non-identifiable (available observation/evidence cannot uniquely determine the value even in principle under the specified model, formally f(theta1)=f(theta2) with theta1!=theta2); rules T-4 NOT A CORE-THEORY BLOCKER because the core does not require latent-parameter inference, but the distinction Unknown != Missing != NonIdentifiable must be preserved once any inference context is introduced.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Policy \rightarrow Assessment \rightarrow \Sigma ... does not imply ... \Sigma \rightarrow Policy
b_rows_sample.statement: Resolves the I-2 circular-dependency warning (Policy -> Assessment -> Sigma and Sigma -> Validation -> Policy) by separating semantic/ontological dependency from operational dependency: the canonical semantic graph is Evidence -> Assessment (parameterized by Policy) -> Sigma -> K, and Validation may READ Sigma/Policy without Sigma constructing the Policy against which it is evaluated; classifies I-2 as an implementation/dependency-graph artifact provided the implementation respects the dependency direction, with three explicit resolution criteria.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q_t = \pi_Q(Replay(K_0,H_t))
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Q_t as an event-derived projection of History rather than an independently authoritative state component: Q_t = pi_Q(Replay(K_0,H_t)), equivalently p in Q_t iff there exists e in H_t with e=Ask(p); requires the replay invariant H_t=H'_t => Q_t=Q'_t, and a canonical serialized InquiryEvent schema (proposition_id, inquiry_timestamp, actor/context, event_id, schema_version) satisfying Deserialize(Serialize(e))=e. Concludes Q_t is not a new component of minimal K or Sigma, is replayable and serializable, and is not independently authoritative -- the remaining obligation is engineering closure, not theory redesign.

b_rows_sample.anchor: G0 — Exact correspondence ... G4 — Theory underspecified
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a five-category Theory-Implementation Gap Protocol Delta(T,I) for classifying any construct's correspondence between theory and implementation: G0 exact correspondence, G1 implemented but untested, G2 implemented differently (behavior diverges from spec), G3 not implemented, G4 theory underspecified (implementation exposes a missing theoretical definition). States G0/G1/G3 do not imply a theory defect, G2 may indicate either a theory or implementation defect, and G4 is the only category that automatically reopens theoretical work.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \textbf{THEORY PROVISIONALLY CLOSED — EMPIRICAL CERTIFICATION PENDING}
b_rows_sample.statement: Revises the overall Step 282 verdict from the first draft's 'FORMALLY SUBSTANTIALLY CLOSED' wording to the more precise 'THEORY PROVISIONALLY CLOSED — EMPIRICAL CERTIFICATION PENDING,' meaning no currently identified core theoretical blocker remains but the theory has not been empirically validated against the complete KnowledgeOS/EKP environment; three possible outcomes (A still incomplete, B provisionally closed, C fully closed) are given with B as the currently supported one, conditional on completing residual formal checks (T-3, T-4, I-2, Q_t).

b_rows_sample.anchor: We should stop asking: "Is KnowledgeOS theory complete?" as one binary question. Instead ask: "Is there any remaining unresolved construct that is necessary for the definition, semantics, transformation, identity, or invariants of the theory?"
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the entire Step 282 question from a binary completeness question into a load-bearing-dependency question: whether any remaining unresolved construct is necessary for the theory's definition, semantics, transformation, identity, or invariants; if no, the theory has reached a 'theoretical stopping point' independent of whether the real EKP implements or observes everything.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would **not yet accept this wording**: > **KNOWLEDGEOS THEORY — FORMALLY SUBSTANTIALLY CLOSED**
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the original Step 282 draft's claim that Formal Closure is 'ACHIEVED/SUBSTANTIAL' while simultaneously leaving T-4 OPEN and T-3 BLOCKED, arguing this is potentially too strong and that Step 282 must first prove T-3 and T-4 are actually theory-critical via a dependency-based closure argument rather than merely presenting a status table.

b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the three legitimate stopping-decision outcomes for Step 282: A (a genuine theory-critical construct remains unresolved -> continue theory work), B (no theory-critical defect remains but empirical/governance evidence is incomplete -> stop theory invention, move to validation/ratification), C (formal, computational, empirical and governance all satisfied -> canonical freeze); states current evidence strongly suggests B but Step 282 must demonstrate it, not assume it.

b_rows_sample.statement: Retrospective narrative of the programme's own history: from '200+ archaeology steps' to '53 gaps' to '13 critical gaps' the original interpretation assumed more theory must be invented, but later independent verification progressively falsified that interpretation as many apparent gaps turned out to be transcription/category errors, with O, authority, and Determination recovered and Sigma reduced to minimal structure and missingness repaired with Q_t.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 282 is COMMISSIONED in its corrected form.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formal HPA ruling: Step 282 is commissioned in its corrected form as a theory-criticality and residual-gap classification gate (not a completion declaration), with the corrected outcome expected to be 'B — THEORY THEORETICALLY CLOSED AT THE DECLARED SCOPE' but requiring Step 282 to demonstrate rather than assume this, and an explicit instruction not to synchronize into the book yet.

b_rows_sample.anchor: TC-1 — Semantic definition ... TC-8 — Internal consistency
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines eight theory-criticality (TC) criteria used to test whether a residual gap is genuinely load-bearing: TC-1 semantic definition, TC-2 type closure, TC-3 identity/equality, TC-4 transformation closure, TC-5 invariant preservation, TC-6 mandatory distinguishability, TC-7 falsifiability, TC-8 internal consistency; a gap is theory-critical only if it fails at least one.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do **not** invent new theory unless an actual theory-critical failure is demonstrated. Do **not** declare closure because most constructs are already defined. Do **not** keep the theory open merely because implementation, empirical validation, or governance is incomplete.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the governing methodological sequence for Step 282 execution (Identify -> Classify -> Test -> Falsify -> Close or Escalate) with three explicit anti-bias prohibitions: do not invent new theory absent a demonstrated theory-critical failure; do not declare closure merely because most constructs are defined; do not keep the theory open merely because implementation/empirical/governance work is incomplete.

a_rows_sample.statement: Step 281 is commissioned because Step 280's empirical closure test found EC=NOT ACHIEVED: Critical Failure #7, where both 'nobody ever asked' and 'we asked and it isn't there' render identically as absence from the assertion set (a not-in A), silently converting missingness into a substantive value.

a_rows_sample.statement: The Step 281 governing principle: any repair must be the minimum extension that distinguishes all mandatory epistemic states while preserving every already-established invariant -- later formalized as the M1/M2/M3 minimality criterion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: M1 Not Asked ... M2 Asked + Absent ... M3 Asked + Unknown ... M4 Supported ... M5 Refuted ... M6 Conflicted ... M7 Orphan | An assertion/document exists but has no required semantic relationship. The first six are epistemic cases. The seventh is not automatically an epistemic status.
a_rows_sample.statement: The seven mandatory states any missingness repair must distinguish: M1 Not Asked, M2 Asked+Absent, M3 Asked+Unknown, M4 Supported, M5 Refuted, M6 Conflicted (six epistemic cases), and M7 Orphan, explicitly flagged as not automatically an epistemic status but possibly a structural condition.

a_rows_sample.statement: Candidate Repair A is formally defined as a bottom-tuple (id,proposition,BOTTOM,timestamp,provenance) recording explicit absence, with the stated defect that BOTTOM becomes semantically overloaded unless it precisely distinguishes absent/unknown/unavailable/not-determined -- later executed and refuted in repairs.py/test_repair_selection.py.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q_t ⊆ P where Q_t records propositions that have actually been queried/evaluated. ... This directly solves the E4 distinction. However, it introduces a new explicit structure: Q_t. That structure must then participate in: identity; equality; replay; serialization; persistence; transformation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Candidate Repair B is formally defined as an inquiry register Q_t (a subset of the proposition space P recording what was actually queried), noted to directly solve the E4 distinction but to require Q_t's participation in identity, equality, replay, serialization, persistence and transformation -- later executed and SELECTED in repairs.py/test_repair_selection.py, with those participation questions answered PRESERVED by test_invariant_preservation.py.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C1 — Absent and Unknown are equivalent ... The E4 failure provides evidence against making that assumption automatically. C2 — Inquiry and epistemic result remain separate dimensions: Σ* = I × E ... Therefore C cannot be accepted merely because it is elegant.
a_rows_sample.statement: Candidate Repair C is refined into two sub-forms: C1 (collapsing Asked+Absent into Unknown, rejected because E4's own failure is evidence against that assumption) and C2 (a typed epistemic state Sigma*=I x E keeping inquiry and epistemic-result as separate dimensions), with an explicit warning that elegance alone cannot justify accepting C -- later executed and found isomorphic to, but less minimal than, Repair B.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R* is minimal iff: M1 — Necessity: every component of ΔR is required to distinguish at least one mandatory state pair. M2 — Irreducibility: no proper subset ΔR′⊂ΔR can distinguish all mandatory states. M3 — No redundant distinction: the repair must not distinguish states that the mandatory operation
a_rows_sample.statement: The formal minimality criterion answering the supervisory review's demand: a proposed repair R* (with ΔR=R*-R0) is minimal iff every component of ΔR is necessary (M1), no proper subset of ΔR suffices (M2), and no unnecessary distinction is introduced beyond what the mandatory operation set can consume (M3) -- this exact three-part test is later executed verbatim in test_minimality.py and test_repair_selection.py.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Σ-A: Missingness becomes a component of Σ: Σ=(I,A,S,R,V,C). Σ-B: Missingness remains in the inquiry/evidence layer. Σ-C: A two-level model: Σ=Σ_inquiry×Σ_epistemic. ... Placement in Σ remains a design decision until minimality is demonstrated.
a_rows_sample.statement: Three alternative placements of missingness relative to Sigma are distinguished: Sigma-A (fold missingness into Sigma itself), Sigma-B (keep it in a separate inquiry/evidence layer), Sigma-C (a two-level product Sigma_inquiry x Sigma_epistemic) -- with the correction document leaving this an open design decision pending minimality proof rather than assuming Sigma-A as the earlier uncorrected Step 281 draft had done.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C* = typed inquiry + epistemic semantics ... ε_t(p)=(I_t(p),E_t(p)) where I_t(p)∈{NotAsked,Asked} and E_t(p) is defined only once inquiry has occurred. ... this candidate becomes canonical only after the minimality and empirical tests below succeed.
a_rows_sample.statement: The corrected document's working (not-yet-canonical) candidate: epsilon_t(p)=(I_t(p),E_t(p)) with I_t(p) in {NotAsked,Asked} and E_t(p) defined only once inquiry has occurred, explicitly gated on passing later minimality and empirical tests -- later found isomorphic to but less minimal than the executed Repair B (inquiry register).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The theory must prohibit an implicit transition: NotAsked → Refuted merely because p∉A. Thus: Absence cannot generate negative epistemic evidence.
a_rows_sample.statement: A new transformation invariant required of the repair: absence of an assertion must never generate an implicit transition to a substantive negative epistemic value (NotAsked directly to Refuted) merely from non-membership in the assertion set -- absence cannot generate negative epistemic evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I_{K_1}(p)≠I_{K_2}(p) is sufficient to establish: K_1 ≉_O K_2, provided an O_core operation can observe that distinction. This is the exact connection between the missingness defect and the earlier equality theory.
a_rows_sample.statement: A new equality consequence: because inquiry state becomes observable under the repair, a difference in inquiry state between two knowledge states K1 and K2 is sufficient by itself to establish observational non-equivalence K1 not-approx_O K2, provided some O_core operation can observe that distinction -- connecting the missingness repair directly to the pre-existing observational-equality theory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H_t=[Ask(p), NoDetermination(p)] must produce ε_t(p)=(Asked,Unknown/Absent) and not (NotAsked,∅). Therefore the repair creates a new replay invariant: Replay preserves inquiry semantics. This must be tested, not merely asserted.
a_rows_sample.statement: A new replay invariant required by the repair: replaying a history containing an Ask(p) event followed by NoDetermination(p) must reconstruct the (Asked,Unknown/Absent) state and never silently collapse back to (NotAsked,empty) -- explicitly flagged as requiring empirical testing, not mere assertion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: E4-R1 — Not Asked ... E4-R2 — Asked but Absent ... E4-R3 — Asked + Unknown ... E4-R7 — Orphan ... Create an asserted document/object without semantic relationships. Expected: Orphan=True without automatically changing E(p).
a_rows_sample.statement: The corrected, executable E4 re-test protocol defines seven test records (E4-R1 through E4-R7), each specifying a setup, an expected representation and an expected semantic result, including E4-R7 (orphan) requiring that Orphan=True while the epistemic state E(p) remains unchanged -- this exact protocol is executed verbatim (7/7 PASS) in exec/test_e4_rerun.py.

a_rows_sample.anchor: F1 | Policy-free result may otherwise be interpreted as absence | F3 | Policy conflict must not collapse into unknown merely through missing policy | F5 | Missing policy must remain distinct from no inquiry | F6 | Expired policy must not be represented as nonexistent policy | F10 | Historical replay
a_rows_sample.statement: Five falsification tests (F1, F3, F5, F6, F10) are identified as affected by the missingness repair because they interact with absence, policy, or historical semantics, and must be re-run under the chosen repair -- later executed 5/5 PASS in exec/test_affected_falsification.py.

a_rows_sample.anchor: {CLOSED,PARTIAL,OPEN,BLOCKED,NORMATIVE,EMPIRICAL} ... CLOSED: Defect repaired, required test passes, evidence preserved. ... NORMATIVE: Mathematics/evidence cannot determine the answer; governance decision required. EMPIRICAL: Theory is specified but executable evidence is still required.
a_rows_sample.statement: A six-status gap classification scheme replacing the earlier vague OPEN/PARTIAL treatment: CLOSED, PARTIAL, OPEN, BLOCKED, NORMATIVE (mathematics/evidence cannot decide; governance decision required), and EMPIRICAL (theory specified but executable evidence still needed).

b_rows_sample.anchor: after Repair B: system state = (K,\ Q_t,\ H) \qquad\text{not}\qquad K ... the sufficiency question re-opens **one level up**
b_rows_sample.statement: Mathematician's-lens argument that Repair B, though invariant-preserving over K, silently changes what 'the state' means to (K,Q_t,H); K alone can no longer distinguish M1 from M2, so the sufficiency question reopens one level up: is (K,Q_t) sufficient and minimal? Names G-56 (Sufficient(K,O,I)) as exactly the needed instrument, noting it remains unadopted as of this document.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
def expressive(F, predicates, space=SPACE):
    """Expressive(F, I): no two F-identified states disagree on any predicate."""
b_rows_sample.statement: Ground-truth executable definition of Expressive(F,I): for a given finite enumerated space of states, bucket states by their F-image, then check that no two states sharing an F-image disagree on any predicate in I; returns (bool, list of witnessing disagreements). This is the operational form of the Expressive conjunct used throughout the Sufficient(F,O,I) adoption argument.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathrm{Sufficient}(F,\mathcal O,\mathcal I)\;&:\Longleftrightarrow\; \mathrm{Congruent}(F,\mathcal O)\ \wedge\ \mathrm{Expressive}(F,\mathcal I)
b_rows_sample.statement: Formal definition proposed for adoption: for a state abstraction F with s1~F s2 iff F(s1)=F(s2), Congruent(F,O) requires every state-transforming operation in O to respect F-indistinguishability, Expressive(F,I) requires every mandated predicate/invariant in I to respect F-indistinguishability (i.e. Expressive is Congruence for the 0-ary/predicate case), and Sufficient(F,O,I) is their conjunction. Closes G-56 (previously open since the second-order pass, at 0 adoption).

type_signature.domain: state abstraction F, operation set O, predicate set I

b_rows_sample.anchor: Congruent ∧ ¬Expressive | `F₄ = K=(𝒜,ℛ)` ... Expressive ∧ ¬Congruent | `F₂ = content+status`
b_rows_sample.statement: Executed independence proof that Congruent and Expressive are neither redundant: witness (a) F4=K=(A,R) is Congruent=True but Expressive(I_merge_prov)=False against the section-265.11 merge-provenance invariant; witness (b) F2=content+status is Congruent=False (fails on Remove/Revise/Transform) but Expressive(I_any_accepted)=True. Both directions realized, so the conjunction Sufficient=Congruent AND Expressive is a proper (non-redundant) conjunction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sufficient(K,\mathcal O,\mathcal I)\ \text{FAILS on the EXPRESSIBILITY conjunct the moment } \textit{“was }p\textit{ asked?”}\ \in \mathcal I
b_rows_sample.statement: The decisive adoption argument: modeling the Step 280 defect (proposition p, inquiry recorded or not) shows K alone is CONGRUENT (the only operations are Assert and Ask; Ask changes only the inquiry register, which K does not project, so K-indistinguishability is preserved by every K-transformation) but NOT EXPRESSIVE the moment 'was p asked?' is admitted as a mandated predicate -- so Sufficient(K,O,I) would have located the exact Step 280 defect, and named the repair site (the smallest carrier making I_was_asked expressible), BEFORE the empirical test ran, i.e. a priori rather than by post-failure comparison.

b_rows_sample.anchor: `ℐ` now carries the weight `𝒪` used to. ... **There is no invariant register.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Adoption obligation stated: while the mandatory-operation set O is usable now (15 named, 5-class partition, 14-element lower bound forced, 4 operations' mandatory status open as D-1), the invariant/predicate set I has NEVER been enumerated -- opened as new gap G-67, a class-(1) actual theoretical hole inheriting the load-bearing role O held before Step 272A; recommends I become a maintained register with the same citation discipline O received, seeded with the seven known members (one of which, section 265.11's merge-provenance invariant, is currently inexpressible in K=(A,R)).

b_rows_sample.anchor: `Sufficient` is *demonstrated* on a bounded model and *derived* from the corpus's own two criteria. It is **`DERIVED`, not proven**, and it should not be described as a theorem until `ℐ` is closed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit epistemic-status caveat on the adoption document's own claim: Sufficient(F,O,I) is demonstrated on a bounded 3-state model and derived from two pre-existing corpus criteria (congruence, and the corpus's own restriction noted at 259.8), not proven as a general theorem, and must not be described as a theorem until the invariant set I is fully enumerated (G-67).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Eliminability, Preservation and Realization are three distinct questions. None implies another.
a_rows_sample.statement: The load-bearing result of the Theory 00-14 programme: Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))) [Zero/eliminability], Hhat(Q|T(D))=0 [Adequacy/preservation] and O(T(D))=Q(D) [Realization] are shown to differ in every system tested, by independent mechanisms; tagged [EXP] deliberately rather than [THM] because necessity of the separation in general is unproven.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Eliminability does not predict Preservation
a_rows_sample.statement: Four experiments of increasing power (H-RR2 boundary-crossing Zero rate 0.0377 vs 0.0426; KR-BRIDGE-01 marginal RD=-0.363 fully explained by redundancy confounding; KR-BRIDGE-02 H1 not refuted; KR-BRIDGE-03 at 13x informative strata, H1 still not refuted, surviving cells 14->1) converge on the same negative finding, stable under a 13-fold power increase.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Preservation does not give Realization
a_rows_sample.statement: Hhat(Q|R5)=0 (adequate) is a separate fact from O(R5)=Q(D) (realized): a fixed decoder can fail on information-theoretically adequate data because it was fixed in advance and not refit; flagged as a design defect that the KR-REP-REDUCTION chain never operationalized this separation (no dropped record/source ever made constraint C fail), so 'the separation is real; that experiment could not exhibit it.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Eliminability does not give Realization
a_rows_sample.statement: Not derivable merely from the other two separations (explicitly not a corollary): Zero is defined via Pi, which is read-disjoint from Q by construction, so it carries no information about Q's recoverability 'by design' — verified rather than assumed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Realization ⟹ Adequacy
a_rows_sample.statement: Standing conjecture that if a fixed decoder recovers Q from R on every observed case, R determines Q on the realized cases; refutable by a decoder that is right by luck (correct on every observed case while the fiber is Q-heterogeneous); explicitly 'not tested.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do the separations survive a non-synthetic carrier?
a_rows_sample.statement: Flagged as the central transfer problem: whether eliminability/preservation/realization separations generalize beyond the tested synthetic carrier is explicitly open.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The estimand for any bridge claim is the within-stratum effect.
a_rows_sample.statement: The programme's central methodological error was estimating the wrong quantity competently — the marginal P(A|Z)-P(A|not Z) was already known to be confounded before KR-BRIDGE-02 ran; re-estimating it produced a false 'H2 SUPPORTED'; the correct estimand is the Mantel-Haenszel within-stratum effect.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A stratum is informative iff (a_k+b_k)>0 ∧ (c_k+d_k)>0 ∧ (a_k+c_k)>0 ∧ (b_k+d_k)>0
a_rows_sample.statement: Both Zero and non-Zero must occur and both Adequate and Inadequate must occur for a stratum to be informative; strata at deterministic extremes contribute nothing, explaining why flattening the redundancy distribution failed (balance is not power) and why choosing a finer stratification variable (multiplicity partition, then partition x |S|) gave 13x the informative strata.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sign agreement alone is not replication.
a_rows_sample.statement: Under a sign-only replication rule, 14 cells 'replicated' with |RD|~0.001 and 12 of 14 had no stratum CI excluding zero; all 14 collapsed at higher power. Replication requires sign agreement AND clearing a substantive floor on both splits AND at least one stratum's 95% CI excluding zero; per-stratum RDs must be reported, not only the pooled MH estimate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If the floor is declared after first inspection, record that fact in the artifact
a_rows_sample.statement: Effect-size floors must be declared and used as a reporting tier rather than a filter (publish every surviving cell at both tiers) since at n~10^5 statistical significance is not evidence of anything; a post-inspection floor must be disclosed as such.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Bootstrap CI on Ĥ ... [DEFECT] invalid here
a_rows_sample.statement: Estimator hygiene register: N_viol is exact and bias-free (authoritative for combinatorial adequacy questions), the Miller-Madow correction is used for Hhat, Haldane+0.5/Woolf CI is used for sparse odds-ratio tables, and bootstrap CI on Hhat is invalid because resampling duplicates cases and depresses conditional entropy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Within the tested deduplication regime, redundancy behaves as a common cause of Zero occurrence and of inadequacy.
a_rows_sample.statement: Standard formalized here: never state a regime-specific empirical finding as a general causal law; a single-mechanism explanation of the KR-BRIDGE-01 confound was itself withdrawn once the Zero-count was found constant at r=1 but varying at r=2, showing the exact RD=0 had two different causes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Power is a property of the informative region, not of n.
a_rows_sample.statement: Measured across four candidate power levers: population size (no effect, 73/74/70 across n=1500/4000/8000) and flattening the confounder distribution (73->75, no effect) both do nothing, while record count (73->233) and finer stratification variable (~30->388) are the effective levers; when power stops responding to sampling, the constraint has moved into the design (the 67 dead cells are invariant across nine generator regimes because the adequacy definition itself saturates).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Everything in this set is built from six objects and one operator.
a_rows_sample.statement: Theory 01 fixes the six-object signature of the KnowledgeOS transformation carrier: D (data, a finite multiset of records), T (transformation D->R), R=T(D) (representation), Q (inquiry D->Y), Pi (observable R->O), O (decoder R->Y), and C (constraint predicate on R), plus the inquiry frame Pi_frame=(Q,C,O) with O fixed in advance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: a record r = (value, source, tag, timestamp)
a_rows_sample.statement: A record in the tested carriers is r=(value,source,tag,timestamp), optionally a derived rank; explicitly flagged as an experimental carrier, not declared to be the mathematical carrier of KnowledgeOS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Set subtraction D \ S is INVALID wherever a field is relative.
a_rows_sample.statement: The elimination operator E_S must be typed to the level it acts at and must recompute relative fields (e.g. within-group rank) after removing S; naive set subtraction D\S leaves stale relative values and produces a representation the level's own rules forbid.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero is indexed by (T,Π) and by the subset S; adequacy by (T,Q) and the population; realization by (T,Q,O) and the case.
a_rows_sample.statement: Zero, Adequacy and Realization are defined with different index sets and are not three readings of one quantity: Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) <=> Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))); Adequate(T,Q) <=> Hhat(Q|T(D))=0; Realized(T,Q,O) <=> O(T(D))=Q(D).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Π and Q must read disjoint fields, and disjointness must be discharged on the triple (Π, Q, T), not the pair (Π, Q).
a_rows_sample.statement: An anti-circularity requirement (candidate FR-003) is proposed: read-disjointness of Pi and Q must be verified on the triple (Pi,Q,T) because T can derive an output field Pi reads from sources Pi never declared; two concrete KR-BRIDGE-02 failures (a rank field secretly shared with Q's tag field, and an arity observable secretly reading value via deduplication survivorship) show declaration is not verification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS has no declared mathematical carrier.
a_rows_sample.statement: Every experiment used a deliberately small numerical carrier (|D|<=6) so fibers would collide and adequacy would be measurable; this is a calibration choice, not an ontological one, and the move to documents/claims/entities/relations/provenance/contradictions/temporal states/evidence is the open research problem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A transformation family is either sequential (Rk+1 = Tk(Rk)) or parallel (Rk = Tk(D)) — never silently mixed
a_rows_sample.statement: Sequential vs parallel transformation families is a permanent type-discipline rule, load-bearing because the data-processing inequality (document 04) applies to sequential families and not to parallel ones.

b_rows_sample.anchor: > **What evaluation structure is minimally required to preserve the distinctions the KnowledgeOS programme has already declared important?**
b_rows_sample.statement: W-KR-CONTR-2026-09 reframes the Contr question from 'three vs four values' to the deeper question of what evaluation structure is minimally required to preserve the programme's already-declared-important distinctions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: * Candidate A — fourth value: **7/12** * Candidate B — delegation: **7/12** * Candidate C — exclusive construction: **7/12** * Candidate D — structured evaluation: **12/12**
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports the core scoring result: A/B/C each pass only 7/12 required distinctions, failing on the identical seven; D (structured evaluation) passes all 12. The seven common failures collapse the unknown family (Unobservable≡InsufficientEvidence≡Underdetermined≡TheoryIncomplete≡...→U), meaning adding a contradiction value does not address distinctions lying outside the contradiction dimension.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
$$
\chi(G)=3.
$$... **Given this particular required-distinction set and this adequacy criterion, at least three distinguishable flat classes are required.**
b_rows_sample.statement: The experiment turns adequacy into a graph-coloring/injectivity problem over the required-distinction graph, finding chromatic number chi(G)=3; carefully qualified: this does not establish the correct evaluation domain has three values, only that at least three distinguishable flat classes are required given this distinction set and adequacy criterion -- and separately, nine 'no determinate value' conditions cannot be adequately represented by any flat value domain regardless of cardinality, making the obstruction structural rather than cardinal.

States a methodological principle from the chromatic-number finding: colourability only proves pairwise coding capacity under the chosen abstraction, it does not establish that resulting values carry the required semantic or operational meaning -- cardinality sufficiency is not semantic adequacy.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
$$
\min |\text{representation}|=2
$$

with the two minimum representations: $$
\{\text{value},\text{reason}\}
$$

and $$
\{\text{polarity},\text{reason}\}.
$$

And: **reason is indispensable.**

b_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate C maps contradiction to `T`. Yet it passes invariants I1–I5. Why? Because those invariants test contradiction against the **unknown family**, rather than against satisfaction itself.

b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes evaluation should be represented as Eval(x)=(Status(x),Reason(x)) rather than Status(x) alone, giving concrete examples (U,Unobservable) vs (U,Underdetermined) sharing top-level status but remaining distinguishable -- distinguishing Flat semantics Eval:X->V from Structured semantics Eval:X->V×R as a new research vocabulary distinction, and noting D is conceptually a product/structured evaluation space E=V×R, not simply a richer many-valued logic.

States a general methodological principle from the Candidate C failure: passing invariants does not imply semantic adequacy -- an invariant suite covering only one axis of separation (contradiction vs unknown) can miss another (contradiction vs satisfied) entirely, motivating I11 (Contr≠Satisfied) as a candidate, not yet canonical, invariant.
